Concurrently, the electron-withdrawing fluorinated motifs weaken the Li+-polymer coordination, steering an anion-derived decomposition pathway to form a homogeneous, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Consequently, the PTFMO-BEP electrolyte enables exceptional cyclability in Li||Li symmetric cells (>800 h) and uniform, dendrite-free lithium deposition. When paired with high-loading LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cathodes (∼4.4 mAh cm–2) and thin lithium anode (50 μm), the Li||NCM811 full cells achieve outstanding capacity retention of 85.6% after 150 cycles at 4.3 V and 91.5% after 100 cycles at 4.5 V. Remarkably, stable operation is maintained even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.7 V with a 20 μm Li anode (88.7% retention over 100 cycles). Furthermore, ampere-hour-scale pouch cells configured with LiNi0.90Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (NCM9055) cathodes deliver a high gravimetric energy density of 510.1 Wh kg–1. This work exemplifies a potent molecular-design strategy to advance polyether electrolytes for practical high-energy-density lithium metal batteries.

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Oxidative Remote (4 + 1)-Cyclization of 1,6-Enynes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed enantioselective oxidative remote (4 + 1) cyclization of 1,6-enynes using PhI(OPiv)2 as the oxidant. Both Z- and E-enynes are competent substrates, affording the same cyclopentane-fused lactones and lactams with high efficiency, and excellent enantioselectivity is achieved using chiral pyridinyl oxazoline ligands. These cyclopentane-fused lactones can be readily transformed to other chiral cyclopentane derivatives. Notably, the use of TFE as the solvent is critical for attaining high chemoselectivity and enantioselectivity. Density functional theory calculations reveal that unlike previous reports of asymmetric enyne cyclization, the enantioselectivity of this reaction is governed by cis-oxypalladation of the alkyne. The resulting vinyl-Pd(II) intermediate undergoes sequential alkene insertion, palladium migration, and oxidation steps. The generated terminal alkyl-Pd(IV) species then undergoes an SN2-type reductive elimination with the enol ester as the nucleophile, which accounts for the formation of the cyclopentane skeleton.

title: Terahertz Stimulation Enhances Nanopore Capture Rate via Mitigating Voltage-Induced Water Compression
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nanopore sensing has emerged as a powerful tool for proteomic analysis, yet controlling molecular translocation, particularly for neutral residues, remains a significant challenge. Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the translocation of electrically neutral peptides and amino acids, and to elucidate how nanoslit geometry and applied voltage jointly regulate the process from both kinetic and thermodynamic perspectives. As the applied voltage increases from 0 to 1 V, the biomolecule capture time doubles, whereas the dwell time is reduced by half. Potential-of-mean-force calculations reveal a higher entry barrier and a lower exit barrier. Further analyses of solvent density and the corresponding bulk-equivalent pressure show that increasing the voltage or narrowing the nanoslit raises the density of the confined solution, generating a bulk-equivalent static-pressure differential that increases resistance to molecular entry while reducing resistance to exit. To relieve this voltage-induced compression, we apply an external terahertz (THz) electromagnetic stimulation, which effectively shortens the capture time by lowering the entry barrier from 48.49 to 38.76 kJ/mol. This study provides molecular-level insights into nanopore translocation and offers practical strategies to enhance molecular capture, potentially advancing nanopore proteomics and informing related applications. Notably, this computational research is the first to introduce THz stimulation for regulating nanopore translocation, offering a noncontact approach to mitigate water compression, as well as for active and reversible nanopore control.

title: A Three-Motif-Based One-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework as an Efficient Cathode Material for Stable Rechargeable Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Crystalline one-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (1D COFs) hold great promise for diverse applications; however, their synthesis remains challenging, as it requires simultaneous control over chain dimensionality and crystallization of polymeric chains that are intrinsically prone to entanglement. Here, we show that benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b′]difuran-2,6(3H,7H)-dione (BDFO), in the presence of isoquinoline, effectively compels the trifunctional monomer 2,4,6-tris(4-formylphenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TPFT) to polymerize as a V-shaped ditopic linker, affording 1D zigzag chains that stack in a staggered arrangement to form the crystalline porous framework (CityU-31). CityU-31 exhibits a rectangular nanowire morphology with well-defined lattice fringes, a narrow pore-size distribution of 1–2 nm, and a surface area of 185 m2 g–1. Importantly, the V-shaped connectivity leaves one formyl group at each TPFT unit unreacted, and these pendant aldehydes serve as built-in handles for postsynthetic functionalization. As a proof of concept, a third motif was covalently linked via Knoevenagel condensation, converting the aldehyde groups into cyano functionalities to yield CityU-31-CN. Endowed with the cyano-decorated 1D backbone, CityU-31-CN delivers an extended voltage window (0.8–3.5 V), a high capacity of 160 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, and outstanding cycling stability (>10,000 cycles). The intrinsic backbone reactivity of CityU-31 thus offers a versatile platform for postsynthetic modification, greatly expanding the application scope of crystalline 1D polymers.

title: 8-Oxoguanine Is the Major Product of the Reaction of Guanine Radical Cations with •NO2: A Spin-Orchestrated, Anisotropic Reaction Landscape and Its Biological Implications
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Formation of guanine radical cations (G•+) represents a hallmark DNA lesion produced by ionizing radiation and one-electron oxidation processes. •NO2, a reactive nitrogen species in living systems, drives nitrative and oxidative damage linked to mutagenesis and inflammation. Herein, we delineate spin-orchestrated interactions between •NO2 and radical cations of 2′-deoxyguanosine (dGuo•+) and its model compound 9-methylguanine (9MG•+) to probe synergistic pathways that exacerbate guanine nucleobase and nucleoside damage. Kinetic energy-resolved reaction coupled with mass spectrometric measurements revealed distinct pathways governing regioselective nitrite- and nitro-additions, adduct decomposition, and charge transfer. Direct dynamics simulations and potential energy surface analyses of the 9MG•+ + •NO2 model system, using spin-projected and time-dependent DFT, CCSD(T), and CASPT2 theories, characterized reaction mechanisms, thermodynamics, and kinetics arising from anisotropic interactions within open-shell 1,OS[G•+(↑)···(↓)•NO2] and 3[G•+(↑)···(↑)•NO2]. Through radical combination, the reaction system advances through multiple excited electronic and vibrational manifolds while preserving spin states (no intersystem crossing); only singlet states are open to chemical transformations. •NO2 markedly amplifies the lesion of guanine radicals by promoting sequential electron and H loss, producing 8-oxoguanine in neutral, radical cation, and doubly oxidized forms, along with release of •NO, NO+, and HNO. These pathways proceed through nitrite addition rather than guanine nitration, and HNO forms through •NO-mediated hydrogen abstraction via both conventional and roaming mechanisms. The studies identified new routes to the 8-oxoguanine lesion that has been traditionally attributed to reactive oxygen species. The biological implications of •NO2-mediated damage to guanine radical cations are discussed.

title: A Unified Asymmetric Approach to Tetracyclic Diterpenoids via Ring Reconstruction Strategy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tetracyclic diterpenoids exhibit intricate densely fused and bridged polycyclic architectures and diverse biological profiles, yet their collective asymmetric synthesis from a unified precursor remains a formidable challenge due to immense topological barriers between distinct scaffolds. Herein, we report a divergent asymmetric synthesis of the tetracyclic diterpenoid family driven by a “ring reconstruction” strategy. Commencing with a platinum-catalyzed diboration/tandem allylation to establish the initial stereocenters, we assemble a highly oxidized ent-kaurane central hub via an orchestrated sequence featuring hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and Johnson–Claisen rearrangement. Leveraging this platform, we deploy tailored radical and photochemical skeletal editing to overcome inherent topological constraints. This enables the divergent remodeling of the ent-kaurane core into an array of complex architectures, including ent-atisane, ent-beyerane, jungermannenone, and ent-aphidicolane frameworks. This unified strategy provides an efficient route to complex polycyclic natural products and highlights the power of skeletal editing for rapidly expanding chemical space.

title: 1,8-Azulenedicarboxylic Imides: Excited-State Properties and Catalytic Activity of a Nonalternant π-System
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Imide-functionalized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) represent an important class of π-conjugated molecules; however, their nonalternant isomers remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis and investigation of the structural, photophysical, and excited-state properties of 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides as nonalternant isomers of 1,8-naphthalimides. These compounds retain the characteristic photophysics of the azulene framework, including near-infrared (NIR) absorption and anti-Kasha emission, while substitution at the imide nitrogen enables modulation of their excited-state electronic structures. QD-NEVPT2 calculations identified an S2–T1 pair with relatively large SOC and LE-to-CT character, suggesting a plausible ISC pathway associated with the observed singlet-oxygen photosensitization. Consequently, 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides function as an effective visible-light photocatalyst for the α-cyanation of secondary and tertiary amines. These findings demonstrate that the present nonalternant molecular design provides a strategy for tuning excited-state properties by modulating locally excited and charge-transfer states in imide chromophores.

title: Molecular Origins of Lithium-Ion Transport in the Anionic Metal–Organic Framework SU-102
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF) quasi-solid electrolytes offer chemically tunable environments for ion transport, but the molecular roles of framework coordination and confined solvent remain unclear. We combined solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) measurements with molecular dynamics simulations to determine the Li+ transport mechanism in propylene carbonate (PC)-filled SU-102. Variable-temperature direct- and cross-polarization 7Li ssNMR reveal two distinct Li+ populations with different local tumbling dynamics. Our simulations identified Zr-associated, linker-associated, and fully PC-solvated Li+ coordination environments. The most strongly stabilizing Li+ site is not necessarily the one that carries transport: Zr-associated sites bind Li+ most strongly but form a discontinuous network along the pore axis, whereas the weaker-binding linker sites form a continuous one. Linker-associated Li+ also shows faster site-persistence decay and the largest trial-weighted displacement, and linker-to-linker hopping is the most frequent classified event, followed by Zr-to-Zr hopping. Chemical color-diffusion nonequilibrium molecular dynamics yielded an ionic conductivity of 1.34 ± 0.48 mS cm–1 along the one-dimensional channels and negligible conductivity perpendicular to them, giving an orientational average of 0.45 ± 0.16 mS cm–1, in close agreement with experiment (0.52 mS cm–1). Together, our results indicate that PC-assisted hopping between linker sites contributes more strongly than vehicular diffusion of fully solvated ions, with confined PC retained in the coordination shell across these transfers. These findings identify the balance between ion–framework stabilization and facile site-to-site exchange as a key design principle for reticular quasi-solid electrolytes.

title: Piezocatalytic Sulfonation Enables Nongenetic Competition Therapy for Colorectal Cancer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Irreversible post-translational modifications provide a potential means to impose persistent changes in protein function, yet their controlled generation inside living cells remains challenging. Here, we develop an ultrasound-responsive potassium sodium niobate–gold (KNN@Au) piezoelectric nanoheterojunction functionalized with hyaluronic acid (KNN@Au-HA) to enable in situ terminal protein sulfonation. Under ultrasound excitation, the dynamic modulation of KNN polarization generates a piezo-potential that facilitates interfacial charge separation and electron transfer, promoting the single-electron reduction of O2 to •O2–. Meanwhile, Au–S coordination positions thiol substrates in close proximity to the catalytic surface, facilitating the subsequent multistep oxidation of cysteine thiols to the terminal −SO3H state. Using this platform, we identify ribosomal protein RPL32 as a functionally relevant sulfonation target and resolve sulfonation at Cys96 by mass spectrometry. This modification disrupts ribosomal proteostasis, induces NRF2 nuclear translocation and stress signaling, and converts colorectal cancer cells into a competitive “loser” state that undergoes neighbor-dependent apoptotic elimination. In HCT116 xenograft-bearing mice, ultrasound-activated KNN@Au-HA suppresses colorectal tumor growth; analysis of patient-derived single-cell transcriptomic data reveals RPL32 upregulation as a hallmark of the malignant “winner” state, establishing a functional match between this competition therapy and colorectal cancer. Together, these findings demonstrate that piezocatalytic protein modification can chemically reprogram cellular competitive fitness without genome editing, providing a proof of concept for nongenetic competition therapy against cancer.

title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Maintenance of plant CG DNA methylation requires VARIANT IN METHYLATION (VIM) proteins, a family of E3 ligases that couple hemimethylated CG (hemiCG) with histone ubiquitylation to regulate MET1-mediated DNA methylation. How the hemiCG readout guides VIM proteins for histone ubiquitylation remains unclear. Here we report structure-function characterization of VIM1-mediated histone ubiquitylation, revealing the N-terminal tails of H3 and H4 as the VIM1 substrates. The structures of VIM1 complexed with hemiCG-containing nucleosome and/or E2 UBC11 reveal that VIM1 is positioned over the nucleosome disk surface, with the RING2 and SRA domains anchored to the H2A-H2B acidic patch and linker hemiCG site, respectively, and the RING1 domain mediating UBC11 loading. The RING2-mediated anchoring helps position RING1 near the H3/H4 tails for substrate access, while the SRA-mediated anchoring antagonizes an autoinhibitory state. Together, such dual nucleosome anchoring by RING2-SRA mechanistically links the position-varying hemiCG mark to persistent, yet context-dependent H3/H4 ubiquitylation.

title: Preorganized electrolyte reduction chemistry enables lithium-ion batteries under extreme conditions
abstract: The reduction propensity of the electrolyte governs the interfacial stability of batteries. By examining solvation participation and electron-acquisition propensity, this work establishes a preorganized interphasial reduction principle that quantifies molecular reduction propensity. Leveraging this principle, we screened 72 molecules and identified CMDO as the effective additive capable of suppressing the side reactions of ethyl acetate at the interface.

title: Precise regulation of iridium electronic state reversely stabilizes cobalt oxide for practical proton-exchange membrane electrolysis
abstract: Reducing iridium use without sacrificing activity and durability is a key challenge for proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis. This work shows that confining low-valent Ir within the Co3O4 lattice can electronically stabilize neighboring Co sites, suppressing support degradation and Ir loss. By linking Ir electronic state to catalyst stability, this study offers a general strategy for designing low-Ir, durable anodes for practical green hydrogen production.

title: Mineralogical evidence for hydrous carbonaceous chondrite relics in Chang’e-6 regolith
abstract: Hydrous carbonaceous chondrites are potential carriers of exogenous water to the Earth–Moon system, yet well-preserved hydrous carbonaceous impactor fragments are rarely found in lunar samples, with previous discoveries limited to the lunar nearside. The Chang’e-6 mission returned the first sample from the farside, providing a unique opportunity to identify the exogenous materials that have added volatiles to this region. We document well‑preserved relics showing C1-like mineralogical features in a Chang’e-6 regolith breccia. They are dominated by fine-grained Mg-rich saponite with partially collapsed basal spacing, along with magnetite, dolomite, sulfides, and organic nanoglobules, matching mineral assemblages of heavily altered carbonaceous chondrites and hydrous materials returned from asteroids Ryugu and Bennu. This diagnostic mineral assemblage and in‑situ space‑weathering overprint confirm that these clasts are surviving fragments of the incoming impactor, and in situ dehydration records water loss during lunar surface exposure. Our study provides the first mineralogical and petrographic evidence for preserved hydrous carbonaceous impact debris in lunar farside regolith, revealing the microscale preservation of hydrated minerals and carbonaceous components and providing new constraints on impact-induced volatile injection and release from carbonaceous materials.

title: Awakening Latent Diradicals to Enhance Antiferromagnetic Coupling between Localized Organic Spin Centers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Connecting persistent radicals through π-conjugated linkers provides a promising route for developing organic magnetic systems. However, the simultaneous realization of localized addressable spins and thermally robust antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling remains challenging. Conventional approaches based on quinoidal versus aromatic resonance forms impose electronic constraints that limit access to this regime. Here, we introduce a molecular design principle in which the latent open-shell character of selected heterocyclic linkers is activated to significantly strengthen AFM interactions between localized radical centers. First-principles calculations reveal that this enhancement: i) originates from increased linker spin polarization acting synergistically with partial quinoidalization, and ii) is robust across a series of diradicals combining an expandable family of linkers with representative persistent radicals. We identify diradicals displaying pronounced open-shell character with unusually large singlet–triplet energy gaps typically associated with closed-shell systems. Extending this concept to two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks, we further show that our approach translates from discrete molecules to strongly AFM materials.

title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme
abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

title: Asymmetric Amyloid Cross-Seeding Beyond “Like-Seeds-Like”
abstract: Abstract Amyloid cross-seeding has often been viewed as a “like-seeds-like” extension of homologous nucleation, in which structurally similar amyloid proteins reciprocally accelerate assembly through a shared cross-β architecture. Increasing evidence instead reveals frequent asymmetry: A→B and B→A can differ in rate, mechanism, structural outcome, and biological consequence, and may change with seed state, fibril polymorph, or microenvironment. Here, we propose that productive cross-seeding is governed by directionally selective compatibility rather than generic β-sheet similarity. We examine six mechanistic origins of asymmetry: conformational selection and population shift, fibril-end templating, dock-and-lock kinetic gating, lateral-face recognition, surface-catalyzed secondary nucleation, and coaggregation coupled to strain selection. We integrate kinetic, structural, cellular, animal, and human evidence, emphasizing that bulk aggregation measurements alone cannot distinguish templated elongation from secondary nucleation, adsorption, sequestration, coaggregation, or strain conversion. We further discuss how heterotypic interfaces reshape fibril polymorphism and disease relevance, and assess emerging molecular-simulation and machine-learning approaches for predicting directional cross-seeding. This mechanism-centered framework provides a basis for understanding mixed amyloid pathologies and for developing strategies to block, redirect, or exploit heterotypic propagation in disease.

title: Comparative analysis of PV allocation rules in heterogeneous energy communities for collective self-consumption
abstract: This paper investigates how photovoltaic (PV) electricity allocation rules shape the technical, economic, and distributional performance of collective self-consumption schemes at both community and individual levels. A unified analytical framework is developed to compare four allocation mechanisms—static, hourly-variable, dynamic, and priority-based—across three community configurations: a prosumer-only community, an expanded community with fixed PV capacity, and an expanded community with PV capacity scaled to demand. The study is based on a real-case study of the CERCA energy community in Spain, using one year of measured hourly consumption, meteorological, and tariff data. Results show that allocation rules significantly influence both technical and economic outcomes. In the reference scenario, self-consumption ( SC ) rises from 0.39 to 0.41 (static, hourly-variable) to 0.45 (dynamic, priority), while IRR increases from 10.0% to 11.7% and payback decreases from 8.1 to 7.2 years. Community expansion with unchanged PV capacity improves local PV utilization, reaching SC values of 0.58–0.59, maximum IRR of 12.7% and payback of 6.7 years. At the individual level, priority allocation achieves the highest returns but the greatest dispersion of benefits (the coefficient of variation ( CV ) of individual SC is in the 20.7%–41.8% range), whereas dynamic allocation delivers comparable performance with a more balanced distribution ( CV of individual SC up to 9.2%). Sensitivity analysis shows that, for fixed PV capacity, profitability is maximized with 13–15 additional consumers, yielding an IRR of up to 13.3%. Overall, allocation rules are crucial in shaping both efficiency and equity in energy communities, with direct implications for policy and market design.

title: A defence-in-depth strategy for securing AI-driven biological sequence design
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can design biological sequences, from proteins to whole genomes, opening opportunities for medicine and biotechnology, but the same capability can be misused. The Wübben Sandpit conference brought together experts in biology, AI, biosecurity, ethics, medicine and policy to ask how the field can capture the benefits while managing the risks. Here we set out a defence-in-depth strategy that builds safeguards into every stage, from the data used to train models, to the models themselves, to the synthesis of physical DNA. We argue that responsible governance is not a brake on progress but a precondition for it.

title: Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers’ mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers’ mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

title: Macrophage-exacerbated viral lung injury and mechanical overdistension-driven bacterial superinfection replicated in a human lung chip
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Patients with influenza-induced lung injury exhibit disrupted lung tissue barrier and persistent viral load, accompanied by hyperinflammation, immune cell recruitment, and risk of bacterial superinfection. These complications are often exacerbated in patients undergoing mechanical ventilation. Leveraging an immune-competent human lung-on-a-chip (Lung Chip) lined by human lung epithelium co-cultured with monocyte-derived macrophages and interfaced with lung microvascular endothelium, we show that monocyte-derived macrophages play a central role in driving key features of severe influenza, including activated cell death programs. Physiological strain mimicking breathing motions supports lung homeostasis, whereas pathological strain analogous to mechanical ventilator-induced lung overdistension promotes secondary Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection. Computational gene network analysis combined with experimental validation identified SIRT1 as a candidate modulator of inflammation and susceptibility to bacterial superinfection, which can be mitigated using pharmacological SIRT1 activators. Together, these findings underscore the importance of incorporating macrophages into preclinical models of viral lung injury and establish an integrated workflow combining human Organ Chips and computational approaches for gaining insights into biophysical and molecular disease drivers while facilitating the identification of therapeutic targets and candidate countermeasures.

title: Structure-guided design of a dual-antigen mRNA vaccine conferring broad protection against Henipaviruses
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Henipaviruses (HNVs), including Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV), are zoonotic paramyxoviruses with high case fatality rates and pandemic potential. Despite their threat, no licensed vaccines are currently available for human use. Here, we present a structure-guided mRNA vaccine strategy that overcomes key challenges in antigen stability, fusogenicity, and cross-protective efficacy. Using rationally engineered NiV F glycoproteins stabilized in the prefusion conformation, we identify a lead candidate (F-205) that abolishes syncytium formation and elicits high prefusion-specific antibody titers. Through systematic combinatorial screening, we determine that co-delivery of F-205 (NiV-M) and G (NiV-B) antigens via mRNA–lipid nanoparticles induces potent neutralizing and cellular immune responses. In stringent golden hamster challenge models, this vaccine confers complete survival against lethal NiV-M, NiV-B and HeV challenge, with viral RNA undetectable in lung, spleen and brain after NiV challenge and significantly reduced viral burden after HeV challenge. We also introduce surrogate assays to assess F conformation and fusion activity under standard biosafety conditions, enabling iterative antigen optimization without live-virus handling. This study defines a broadly protective, mechanistically informed vaccine platform for HNVs and provides a generalizable framework for rational design of mRNA vaccines targeting class I fusion viruses.

title: In vivo programming of dual-targeted CAR-T cells facilitates vascular disruption and T-cell infiltration in solid tumors
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: T-cell therapies for solid tumors are restricted by abnormal tumor vasculature, which creates structural and immunological barriers to infiltration. Here we report a programmable mRNA lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platform that orchestrates a division-of-labor immune response in vivo. By modulating the LNP nano-bio interface through 10% 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-L-serine (DOPS) doping and indirect IgG-based anti-CD5 tethering, we achieve selective and efficient transfection of endogenous splenic T cells. This platform simultaneously generates two complementary chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T populations: a vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2)-directed subset that transiently remodels the tumor endothelium, and a tumor-antigen-directed subset that executes cytotoxic clearance. Mechanistic analyses reveal that focal endothelial disruption creates a permissive window for the infiltration, expansion, and activation of tumor-directed CAR-T cells. In refractory melanoma and colorectal carcinoma models in female mice, this dual-programming strategy achieves superior tumor control and drives tumor regression while reducing systemic toxicity. By bypassing ex vivo manufacturing, this approach provides a scalable and host-directed strategy to breach infiltrative barriers in solid-tumor immunotherapy.

title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

title: Numerosity is directly sensed and dynamically transformed in the human brain
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Humans can estimate the number of objects in a scene within a fraction of a second, suggesting that numerosity is encoded rapidly and directly by the visual system. Yet how this encoding unfolds over time and interacts with other visual features remains unclear. Here, we combined magnetoencephalography (MEG) with time-resolved representational similarity analysis (RSA) and MEG–fMRI fusion to track how numerosity is represented in the brain over time. We also used multidimensional scaling (MDS) to visualize the evolving patterns of neural activity. Two main findings emerged. First, numerosity exhibited the hallmarks of a primary perceptual attribute: its neural signature appeared very rapidly after stimulus onset, preceding the encoding of non-numeric features that could otherwise define number. Second, multidimensional scaling of the neural manifolds revealed a temporal shift in representational geometry: an early linear structure, consistent with a summation-based code and predominant in occipital regions, transitioned into a curvilinear structure characteristic of numerosity-tuned coding, emerging more prominently in associative areas along the dorsal stream. Together, these findings demonstrate that numerosity processing is encoded directly from the visual image and unfolds through a rapid hierarchical transformation, from a broad quantity signal to a finely tuned, number-specific code, linking perceptual encoding to higher-level numerical abstraction.

title: The evolutionary plateau of efflux-mediated drug resistance in mycobacteria
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Bacterial genomes encode a large repertoire of multidrug efflux pumps, which could theoretically combine to achieve exceptionally high levels of resistance. To delineate the extent of resistance achievable through efflux driven adaptation, we performed adaptive laboratory evolution of Mycobacterium smegmatis mc²155 wild-type and efflux-deleted (ΔlfrA, ΔefpA) strains against ethidium bromide, a broad-spectrum efflux substrate. Despite prolonged selection, resistance reproducibly plateaued at 8-16 fold increase in MIC under the tested conditions. This plateau emerged through distinct evolutionary trajectories characterized by non-overlapping efflux pump sets: from overexpression of the well-characterized lfrA to upregulation of multiple uncharacterized pumps, all conferring cross-resistance. Genetic reconstruction of mutations in a transcriptional regulator and a membrane protein, together with overexpression of efflux pumps, recapitulated the resistance phenotypes of the evolved strains. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance.

title: Impacts of medications for obesity on global health and the environment
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. We apply a global food system model to project the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1) uptake to 2050 among people with obesity under two scenarios: reduced calorie intake while maintaining dietary composition, and reduced calorie intake combined with shifts towards the EAT–Lancet diet. Compared with the Reference scenario, GLP-1-mediated calorie reduction alone results in up to 6.6 million avoided deaths globally in 2050 and 32 Mha more natural land area, reflecting reductions in cropland, pasture and managed forest. Combining GLP-1 use with EAT–Lancet dietary shifts increases these estimates to 7.7 million avoided deaths and 46 Mha more natural land. Lower food prices increase food consumption among untreated populations, including unhealthy foods, partially offsetting these gains.

title: Governing cryospheric risk beyond political timeframes
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryospheric risks unfold over decades to millennia, while climate governance remains tied to short political cycles. We argue that cryosphere science must be embedded in governance mechanisms that connect near-term decisions with long-term accountability for irreversible change.

title: Greenland ice sheet retreat intensifies the African monsoon through a polar-tropical atmospheric teleconnection
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Global climate forcing drives major changes in the North African summer monsoon (NASM), yet how high-latitude cryospheric changes influence tropical hydroclimate through atmospheric dynamics remains unclear. Integrating paleoclimate proxy evidence with coupled climate-model simulations, sensitivity experiments, and idealized atmospheric modeling, we show that Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) retreat acts as a dynamically important amplifier of NASM rainfall. Using the mid-Pliocene as a natural experiment for sustained global warming, we find that NASM rainfall was markedly stronger than that simulated under transient future warming for comparable global-mean temperature increases. GrIS retreat enhances Arctic warming, thereby perturbing the upper-tropospheric westerly jet and triggering a stationary Rossby wave train linking Greenland to North Africa. This polar–tropical atmospheric teleconnection strengthens monsoon circulation and moisture convergence, producing wetter conditions across the Sahara–Sahel. These results reveal a high-latitude pathway through which slow cryospheric changes modulate low-latitude monsoon variability under sustained warming.

title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Artificial intelligence for combinatorial optimization depends on high-quality, structured training data, yet transforming ambiguous natural-language descriptions into precise, executable formal models remains a major bottleneck, traditionally requiring extensive manual effort and domain expertise. We develop CPAM-LLM, an automated constraint-programming modeling framework based on large language models that converts unstructured problem specifications into validated and executable formal models. The framework integrates retrieval-augmented generation grounded in formal concept analysis for structural validation, chaos-mapping-based data augmentation to enhance cross-domain generalization, and dynamic constraint adaptation to accommodate evolving problem settings. We demonstrate its effectiveness across five scenarios, including DNA sequence design, reconfigurable energy storage systems, and unmanned vehicle logistics. The results show that the framework can automate the data-to-model pipeline while adapting reliably to changing requirements, providing a practical approach to automated data formalization and indicating the importance of accessible, high-quality structured data for reliable downstream artificial intelligence applications.

title: Chiral SERS and photochemistry via collective hotspot asymmetry in metasurface-templated gold networks with disordered nanoscale porosity
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chiral molecules interact with light so weakly that discriminating enantiomers or driving enantioselective chemistry by using optical approaches requires intense circularly polarised lasers or complex resonant structures. Here we combine a geometrically disordered electrodeposited network with a lithographic chiral template resembling the shape of a shuriken. The resulting substrate generates superchiral fields that neither individual component produces. The mechanism underlying this anomalous response arises from two distinct effects: first, the shuriken structures generate substantial intrinsic optical chirality; second, the nanoporous network adds densely distributed plasmonic hotspots and an interference cross-term, which augments the local chirality even more prominently. This chiral plasmonic nanoporous network achieves not only ultrasensitive chiral detection by reaching the attomole range, but also introduces enantiospecific photochemical reactivity on a single substrate under continuous-wave linearly polarised light. Raman asymmetries approach the theoretical maximum ( ≈ 2), while enantiomeric excesses exceed 25%. Finally, a six-order-of-magnitude enhancement over conventional Raman optical activity was calculated.

title: Rapid and selective metal-free O2 reduction to H2O2 using a molecular CpN3 electrocatalyst
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a commodity chemical used broadly in the industrial sector that heavily relies on the 80+-year-old anthraquinone process, requiring significant energy input in combination with precious metal-catalyzed hydrogenation. We describe a metal-free molecular cyclopentadiene-iminium electrocatalyst for producing H2O2 under ambient conditions with high Faradaic efficiency (> 99%) and turnover frequency up to 104 s−1, surpassing some of the most active transition-metal-based molecular catalyst systems. One-electron reduction of the dication [CpN3H]2+ generates a radical cation [CpN3H]+• that becomes a potent hydrogen atom (H•) donor to O2, operating through an unusual radical-rebound mechanism to form a key hydroperoxyl intermediate ([CpN3OOH]+•). This proposed pathway is rigorously supported by cutting-edge computational and experimental mechanistic analyses. Overall, this work demonstrates an innovative and sustainable molecular approach to furnish a valuable commodity chemical through an electrically driven process without the need for transition metals.

title: Interstitial proton buffering enables decoupled transfer dynamics for acidic wastewater decontamination
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The remediation of aggressive acidic wastewater is fundamentally hindered by the coupled proton-release/electron-transfer barrier that suppresses high-valent metal-oxo chemistry in conventional advanced oxidation processes. Here we report an interstitial proton-buffering strategy in which boron is incorporated into a cobalt-manganese phosphide lattice, guiding self-limited reconstruction into a stable oxyhydroxide interface. The interstitial B-regulated interface acts as a local Brønsted-base proton buffer, establishing a proton-acceptor–electron-donor mechanism that enables decoupled proton-electron transfer, as supported by a super-Nernstian E1/2-pH response. This pathway stabilizes CoIV-oxo formation and drives complete imidacloprid degradation within 3 min in simulated water. In 80 h continuous-flow treatment of electroplating acid-pickling wastewater at pH 0.85, the system retains 49.48% total organic carbon reduction. These results identify interstitial proton buffering as a route to sustain high-valent oxidation chemistry in strongly acidic water matrices.

title: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta-benzene
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In 2019, we hypothesised that bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes could mimic meta-benzenes in bioactive compounds. In this work, we have supported this hypothesis experimentally. Incorporation of the bicyclo[2.1.1]hexane fragment instead of meta-benzene into the drug Sonidegib preserves physico-chemical properties and membrane permeability. Incorporation of bicyclo[2.1.1]hexane instead of meta-benzene into the drug Meclizine improves its metabolic stability and preserves the anticancer activity.

title: Lanthanide-dependent methanotroph thrives on radioactive promethium
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lanthanides serve as essential cofactors in the methanol dehydrogenases of methylotrophic bacteria. While biological function has been characterized for the naturally occurring members of the series, promethium, the only lanthanide existing as exclusively radioactive isotopes and virtually absent from nature, has remained unexplored. Here, the acidophilic methanotroph Methylacidiphilum fumariolicum SolV grows on β⁻-emitting Pm-147 as its sole lanthanide source, removing 98% of the isotope from the medium over 60 h despite a calculated radiation dose of 3.6 Gy. Reconstituted methanol dehydrogenase of the type XoxF-MDH displays Pm-dependent activity precisely between the neodymium and samarium variants. Bacterial lanthanide metabolism thus incorporates a naturally absent and radioactive member of the lanthanide series.

title: Atomically ordered few-layer molybdenum boride MBenes for enhanced electromagnetic response
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal borides (MBenes), boride analogues of MXenes, combine layered frameworks with tunable surface chemistry, yet high-quality MBenes remain difficult to access. Existing methods for preparing MBenes often suffer from incomplete dealumination, Mo2AlB2 intermediate-phase formation, multilayer restacking, or Mo vacancies. Here, we report a Lewis-acid molten-salt route that converts MoAlB into few-layer MoB MBene nanosheets with an atomically ordered Mo−B framework and a low density of Mo vacancies. Comparative thermodynamic calculations and control experiments with ZnCl2, ZnBr2, ZnF2, and ZnS identify molten ZnBr2 as the preferred etchant for redox-driven Al extraction and delamination. Temperature-dependent free-energy analysis and Mo−Al−B ternary isothermal sections further define 700 °C as a processing window that suppresses Mo2AlB2 formation and promotes direct conversion from MoAlB to MoB MBene. Selective Al extraction from MoAlB produces few-layer MoB MBene, retaining an ordered Mo−B framework while inducing b-axis contraction, strengthened Mo−B covalency, and enhanced electron localization. Together with O/OH and Br surface terminations, these structural and electronic features promote multiple polarizations and enable an effective absorption bandwidth of 8.7 GHz at 2.1 mm. This theory-informed molten-salt etching strategy expands redox-mediated MBene synthesis and connects atomically ordered few-layer MoB MBene with electromagnetic functionality.

title: Decarbonising industrial hydrogen supply systems under EU taxonomy regulation: A multi-objective decision-support framework for existing facilities
abstract: Hydrogen is a crucial vector for decarbonising hard-to-abate industrial sectors, but its deployment increasingly depends on regulatory sustainability criteria alongside economic performance. In Europe, frameworks such as the EU Taxonomy and Renewable Energy Directive impose life cycle emission thresholds that directly influence hydrogen system design. This work proposes a flexible multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming framework for planning low-carbon hydrogen supply systems at existing, non-relocatable industrial facilities, such as oil refineries. Regulatory compliance with EU Taxonomy thresholds is assessed a posteriori across the unconstrained and discretised Pareto-optimal solution space, rather than embedded as a hard constraint, revealing the cost premium of regulatory alignment. This approach preserves the unconstrained economic baseline and enables alternative or evolving emission thresholds to be screened directly on the stored Pareto set, with a single warm-started solve needed to pinpoint the exact compliance cost. Unlike existing approaches that treat electricity generation and hydrogen production as loosely coupled subsystems, the model integrates renewable and biogenic resource allocation, electricity generation, hydrogen production technologies, and inter-monthly hydrogen storage within a unified optimization structure, anchored to a fixed industrial site, at monthly resolution. Water consumption is explicitly included as a constrained resource, extending the environmental scope beyond carbon metrics. A modular, data-driven architecture fully decouples the mathematical model from the input data layer, enabling adaptation to new regions or technology scenarios by modifying only the input data, without altering the model core. The framework is applied to western Andalusia (Spain) and the Republic of Ireland, which differ in resource availability, technology portfolio, and hydrogen demand. Regional resource-to-demand ratios strongly shape Pareto front structures and technology portfolios. Biomass gasification emerges as the most cost-effective pathway in biomass-abundant settings, while electrolytic routes appear to prevail in resource-constrained regions. While all Pareto-optimal solutions calculated naturally comply with the EU Taxonomy emission threshold (3 kg CO 2 eq/kg H 2 ) in Ireland, compliance in Andalusia requires minor technological reconfiguration from the economic baseline, incurring a 2.1% cost premium. The framework provides a transparent and replicable decision-support tool for policy-consistent hydrogen planning across contrasting regional contexts.

title: Characterizing autothermal reformer operating conditions for inline integration with a solid oxide fuel cell stack
abstract: High-power density solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems running on hydrocarbon fuels warrant compact upstream fuel reforming and reactant preheating to minimize system size and startup time. To that end, this work investigates a CH 4 -fueled autothermal reformer/heat exchanger (ATR/HX) designed for inline integration directly upstream of an SOFC stack, where mildly exothermic catalytic oxidative reforming simultaneously drives H 2 production for the SOFC anode and air preheating for the SOFC cathode. A quasi-1D ATR/HX model with detailed reforming chemistry guides reactor sizing and selection of operating conditions for controlled partial reforming and effective thermal integration. Modeling results indicate that an in-line reactor length of 3.6 cm sufficiently preheats the anode and cathode streams from 400 ∘ C to 550 -- 650 ∘ C with a cathode air outlet approach temperature of < 30 ∘ C to support high-power-density performance for SOFC cells with thin-film yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) or gadolinium-doped ceria (GDC) electrolytes. Experiments at atmospheric pressure demonstrate stable ATR light-off ≤ 450 ∘ C in a single-cell configuration and near 400 ∘ C in a 3-cell short-stack configuration. These experiments characterize the ATR/HX subsystem in SOFC-relevant hardware but do not constitute validation with an electrochemically active SOFC stack. The model and experimental tests show that the compact ATR/HX operates under residence-time-limited conditions, enabling efficient thermal conditioning while preserving residual CH 4 for downstream internal reforming within the SOFC anode. These results demonstrate the feasibility of compact inline ATR/HX integration and establish operating guidelines for subsequent thermally integrated SOFC systems with reduced startup time and improved system compactness.

title: Bordetella pertussis adapts to human nasal mucosa through biofilm-associated virulence reprogramming and host-defense attenuation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Current acellular pertussis vaccines fail to control the burden of Bordetella pertussis (Bp) in the human nasopharynx, a reservoir for transmission. To better understand the unique host and bacterial signatures in the nasal microenvironment, we inoculated primary human nasal epithelial cultures (HNEC) with Bp. Bp adhered and replicated robustly on cilia forming structured and matrix-encased biofilms. HNEC-associated biofilms were more resistant to killing by the antimicrobial peptide, LL-37, compared to abiotic biofilms and planktonic cells. Profiling of the host and bacterial mRNA signatures during infection revealed the differential regulation of host genes encoding mucins and downregulation of those involved in mucociliary clearance, epithelial barrier integrity, and host immunity. Measurement of mucins revealed an initial reduction followed by a sharp increase in MUC5AC and MUC5B, and the presence of mucin-embedded Bp biofilms. A striking downregulation of Bp genes encoding virulence factors, including all the components of current acellular pertussis vaccines, metabolic pathways; and upregulation of genes encoding iron acquisition pathways and the Bps polysaccharide was uncovered. Bps was critical for Bp-HNEC interaction and biofilm formation. Our results reveal biofilms as a potential source of Bp carriage and transmission, the cascade of host-pathogen transcriptional events during nasal infection and targets for vaccine development.

title: Coherence toroidal vortices and statistic-veiled correlation topologies
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Toroidal vortices in fluid and gas dynamics underpin a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields, from elementary particle physics to condensed matter systems, and have recently garnered significant attention in optics because of their inherent topological stability. Here we report the experimental observation of toroidal vortices in stochastic optical wavefields with partial coherence, termed coherence toroidal vortices, which eliminates deterministic topological signatures in conventional optical degrees of freedom while unveiling statistically hidden correlation topologies. These underlying topologies—including both fundamental and higher-order hopfionic textures—emerge in second-order field correlations and are accessible only through statistical measurements. We further examine the impact of chaotic channels on the stability of these statistically veiled correlation topologies, demonstrating that their topological invariants remain robust under realistic environmental perturbations. These findings are experimentally validated and offer novel insights into the potential of toroidal light vortices serving as controllable channels for directional energy and information transfer within complex media.

title: Toward real-world-representative durability testing of fuel cells for heavy-duty transport
abstract: Low-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells are considered one of the most promising technologies for decarbonizing the transport sector due to their high efficiency, fast response, and zero emissions. However, the dynamic and highly transient operating conditions encountered in heavy-duty fuel cell vehicles pose an additional challenge to the development of suitable and durable materials. Developing standardized load profile test methodologies that faithfully reproduce real operating scenarios is a key step toward timely material screening and the harmonization of durability benchmarks across different research facilities. Here we present a Markov Chains-based LPT representative of heavy-duty FCVs application, providing a reproducible model that can be used in other case studies as a reference for investigating different operating conditions to mimic different behaviors in a fuel cell stack, generate experimental data for simulation-based lifetime predictions and allow the development of ASTs. Drive cycle data extracted from TEN-T corridors, processed through a validated LT-PEMFC system model representative of the Toyota Mirai architecture, form the basis of the proposed load profile generation methodology. In this work, the performance in terms of H 2 consumption and FC lifetime for a HDFCV operating in real-world conditions is evaluated and directly compared with the performance of the FC system following the developed LPT, showing a high level of fidelity to the representative operating conditions of the LT-PEMFC in heavy-duty vehicle operation.

title: Hybrid-parity sliding multiferroics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In this work, we introduce a class of hybrid-parity sliding multiferroics in which the spontaneous ferroelectric polarization is coupled to certain nonrelativistic spin splitting components through interlayer sliding, allowing these components to be reversibly switched in an electrical way. Symmetry analysis identifies coplanar magnets as natural platforms for realizing this form of sliding multiferroicity. First-principles calculations establish bilayer VBr2 as a representative example, demonstrating the coupled reversal of the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization and the signs of both even- and odd-parity nonrelativistic spin splitting components via an interlayer-sliding pathway. The signs of these nonrelativistic spin splitting components are locked to the sliding-switchable ferroelectric polarization and encoded in the spin-current responses, providing a signature of the coupled ferroic switching. Our findings expand the scope of sliding multiferroics and the functionality of sliding ferroelectrics for low-energy, nonvolatile logic devices.

title: Symmetry-breaking antibody binding reveals extensive capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Virus capsids are metastable assemblies with an exquisite balance between stability and flexibility, obligatory for entry, infectivity, and immune escape. Yet the extent to which human viruses exploit capsid plasticity and how that consequently shapes antigenic landscapes remains poorly understood. Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. GII.4 HuNoVs have been evolving epochally, driving most global pandemics, and since 2012, GII.4 Sydney has been the dominant variant. The major capsid protein, VP1, is central to infectivity and immune recognition, and VP1-based virus-like particles (VLPs) are considered promising vaccine candidates. Yet, how the icosahedral HuNoV capsid responds to antibody pressure at the atomic level remains unclear. Here, we present the first atomic structure of GII.4 Sydney capsid determined by cryo-EM, revealing the structural features that likely contribute to its sustained dominance. Using focused refinement, we uncover the remarkable capsid plasticity in response to symmetry-breaking binding of neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies. VP1 adopts 11 distinct conformational modalities to accommodate asymmetric antibody binding, and antibody-disrupted VLPs reassemble into smaller particles with five additional VP1 states. This previously unrecognized extent of conformational adaptability provides key insights for designing next-generation VLP- or mRNA-based vaccines targeting HuNoV infections.

title: Quantum sensing-enabled deuterium NMR spectroscopy with nanoscale sensitivity at low magnetic fields
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unparalleled access to molecular structure and dynamics but is traditionally limited by weak signal strength, requiring large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. Here, we demonstrate nanoscale deuterium (2H) NMR spectroscopy using nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, yielding characteristic quadrupolar powder line shapes that are present in conventional bulk NMR spectra. By detecting statistical spin fluctuations from nanometer-scale detection volumes, our approach delivers a sensitivity enhancement of seven to eight orders of magnitude in terms of spin sensitivity over inductive detection, while operating at magnetic fields two orders of magnitude lower than those used in conventional NMR. Temperature-dependent measurements of a deuterated polymer and a molecular solid reveal distinct motional averaging and phase transitions with nanoscale sensitivity. Powder-like NV-detected 2H NMR establishes a powerful tool for probing molecular dynamics on the nanoscale - capabilities beyond those of most existing spectroscopic techniques.

title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

title: Large electrocaloric effects in unannealed multilayer capacitors of partially ordered lead scandium tantalate
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multilayer capacitors of PbSc0.5Ta0.5O3 with good B-site cation order (S111 ~ 0.9-0.96) are driven by supercritical fields of 15.8 V μm−1 in prototype coolers, such that large electrocaloric effects arise over a wide range of temperatures and peak to give thermocouple-measured temperature jumps of |∆Tj | ~ 4.0 K near room temperature. However, the high degree of B-site order requires an energetically expensive 42-day high-temperature anneal that would be economically expensive and environmentally damaging in mass production. Here we report that the performance reduction (4.0 K → 3.1 K) for unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc0.5Ta0.5O3 with partial B-site order (S111 ~ 0.6) is surprisingly small because reduced latent heat is mitigated by high-field electrocaloric effects in the induced ferroelectric phase. Eliminating the anneal without unduly compromising performance should render unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc0.5Ta0.5O3 attractive for applications.

title: Early face-experience deprivation leads to long-lasting deficits in macaque cortical face processing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Experience-dependent plasticity in early sensory cortex is restricted to critical periods early in development. Whether plasticity in higher-order cortex is similarly restricted remains unclear. In the primate ventral visual stream, face-selective cortex emerges with experience during development, providing a powerful system to test how the timing of experience shapes higher-order representations. Using three male rhesus macaques selectively deprived of early face experience followed by prolonged normal face exposure, we found that face-experience-deprived monkeys acquire face-directed viewing behavior and neural face selectivity. However, they showed atypical within-face viewing patterns, while their neural representations retained lasting signatures of early deprivation, including selectivity for both faces and hands and reduced discrimination for face identity, expression, and viewpoint. Thus, higher-order visual cortex remains plastic beyond early development, yet the timing of experience fundamentally constrains the refinement of later-acquired neural representations.

title: Vertically aligned dual-channel metal-organic framework nanosheet membranes for gas separation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The nanostructure of two-dimensional (2D) membranes is crucial for their separation performance. However, in conventional 2D membranes, guest species unavoidably permeate through tortuous pathways, resulting in effective transport lengths that are orders of magnitude greater than the membrane thickness. Here, we propose vertically aligned metal-organic framework (MOF) nanosheet membranes featuring bimodal porosity: intrinsic lateral pores within the MOF nanosheets and interlamellar pores between them, forming an ultralow-tortuosity, dual-sieving channel system for efficient gas separation. Despite their relatively large thickness, the resulting MOF nanosheet membranes exhibit a high H2 permeance of 16673 GPU (up to an order of magnitude higher than the reported average) along with an H2/CO2 separation selectivity of 325 under standardized atmospheric Wicke-Kallenbach conditions (zero transmembrane partial pressure difference). This work not only provides a promising membrane platform for H2/CO2 separation but also offers an alternative strategy for constructing next-generation molecular sieve membranes.

title: Evolutionary plasticity of bacterial surface layer protein exoskeletons
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Prokaryotic surface layer (S-layer) exoskeletons, with their homopolymer paracrystalline architecture, offer a more tractable model of an environmental interface. However, extreme sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation of S-layer proteins confound conventional evolutionary analyses. Here, by combining phylogenomics with structural modelling, we show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across both monoderm (Bacillaceae, Peptostreptococcaceae) and diderm (Caulobacteraceae, Deinococcaceae) bacteria. Focusing on the Gram-positive order Peptostreptococcales, including environmental isolates and clinical pathogens, we uncover multiple S-layer architectures conferring divergent physiological properties. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile. Our findings establish the S-layer as a paradigm of molecular modularity and evolutionary plasticity. Specifically, evolution of a single structural protein enables rapid cell-surface reconfiguration and contributes to immune evasion in bacterial pathogens.

title: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Stalled progress and funding constraints raise important questions about the dependence of current malaria burden on sustained intervention coverage. Here, we estimate malaria transmission potential under a low-intervention scenario where major malaria interventions are withdrawn while broader ecological and demographic conditions remain constant. We develop a contrastive representation-learning framework applied to 30-m Landsat 8 satellite imagery, integrating the resulting environmental representations within a Bayesian hierarchical model. This approach improves predictive accuracy over existing covariate-based malaria mapping methods. Using contemporary Global Burden of Disease 2024 population estimates, we estimate an annual malaria burden of 422 (275-582) million cases across sub-Saharan Africa, representing a 131% increase relative to current estimates. These findings quantify the structural vulnerability of malaria control gains across sub-Saharan Africa and reveal where intervention disruption could have the greatest impact.

title: A metal ion-assisted workflow for practical and scalable enrichment of small extracellular vesicles from biofluids
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Small extracellular vesicles hold immense diagnostic and therapeutic potential, yet clinical translation is hindered by inefficient separation and concentration. Current methods like ultracentrifugation and polymer-based precipitation suffer from low throughput or persistent contaminants. Here, we develop an optimized workflow that adapts the well-established binding between transition metal ions (copper(II), manganese(II), zinc(II)) and membrane phosphate groups to induce vesicle aggregation that facilitates small extracellular vesicle recovery from urine, blood and cell culture-conditioned medium using conventional centrifugation. We elucidate how buffer composition (albumin, phosphate, and hydron) and small extracellular vesicle surface properties (surface charge, phospholipid content) modulate these ion-vesicle interactions. By optimizing protocols using copper(II) for blood, zinc(II) for urine and cell culture-conditioned medium, we achieve higher yields than ultracentrifugation and polymer-based precipitation while preserving vesicle ultrastructure, molecular markers, biological function and safety. Thus, we establish a practical and scalable workflow that accelerates extracellular vesicle-based translational research.

title: Droplet-Assisted Growth of Re-Entrant Micro-Mushroom Surfaces with Switchable Superhydrophobicity and Adhesive Resistance
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nature-inspired designs for surface micro- and nanostructures have long attracted attention for their potential multifunctionality. This study introduces a mushroom-shaped silicone re-entrant structure achieved through a one-step, in-situ dynamic Droplet-Assisted Growth and Shaping strategy. The unique shape and multicomponent hybrid properties of the inert rod base and chemically modifiable spherical head of these silicone micro-mushrooms (SMMs) provide exceptional surface wetting and adhesion characteristics. The engineered single-scale rough surface exhibits the remarkable rose petal effect, featuring a water contact angle exceeding 150° and demonstrating extraordinary water adhesion. The wetting states of these surfaces can be easily altered through O2-plasma treatment with the reconstruction of secondary and tertiary hierarchical nanostructures. This approach also effectively converts petal-effect surfaces into lotus-effect surfaces, significantly enhancing their self-cleaning performance. Furthermore, the SMM coatings display extremely low adhesion to various adhesives, including tapes, hot glue, and all-purpose adhesives, with pull-off forces nearing 0. This characteristic ensures a smooth detachment from sticky surfaces. The durability of the SMM structures is noteworthy, as they maintain their morphology even after 1,000 loop tack tests and can endure 8.7 MPa compression and 500 cycles of linear abrasion on sticky surfaces.

title: Data centre materials need an end-of-life strategy as deployment accelerates
abstract: Data centres are fast-growing stocks of copper, steel and critical materials, yet what happens to these materials at end of life is understudied. The scale, timing and geography of retiring hardware make it an unusually recoverable resource, if corporate and governmental policy incentivizes action now.

title: Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ3-iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: While 2- and 4-aryloxypyridines are ubiquitous in pharmaceutical molecules, efficient synthetic strategies—especially for synthesizing scaffolds with diverse multiple substituents on the pyridine core—remain limited. Here we show a hook-and-slide strategy for constructing these scaffolds, involving the in-situ generation of pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salts from pyridones and Koser’s reagent (hook, C3 selectivity), followed by an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration (slide, O selectivity). Such newly designed iodonium salts feature dual vicinal nucleophilic sites, and we demonstrate that using C2 − H imidazolium ionic liquids can exclusively transfer the aryl group to the strategic O site. This approach is transition-metal-free, scalable, and applicable to substrates with diverse electronic and steric properties or complex structures. Importantly, the resulting products retain −I and −NH2 handles that are amenable to downstream derivatizations, enabling extensive exploration of previously inaccessible chemical space. The utility of this approach is further demonstrated through the concise synthesis of multiple pharmaceutical intermediates and a CRF1 antagonist, CP-376395.

title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The construction of atomically precise heterogeneous catalysts that integrate multiple distinct active sites into a synergistic architecture is highly attractive but challenging. Here, we report an Au39(PPhpy2)2(R1C ≡ C)19 (PPhpy2 = 2,2’-(phenylphosphanediyl) dipyridine, R1C ≡ CH = 4-ethynyl-α, α, α-trifluorotoluene) nanocluster. The heteroatoms (such as nitrogen) were introduced to modulate the local coordination environment and construct asymmetric coordination units on the surface of Au39 nanoclusters. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that, in addition to the symmetric R1C ≡ C-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif, Au39 features two asymmetric pyN-Au-C ≡ CR1 coordination motifs on the surface. Au39/XC-72 delivers 96.6% conversion of benzyl alcohol with 94.4% selectivity for benzaldehyde under mild conditions (40 °C, air). Mechanistic studies show that the pyN-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif facilitates O2 adsorption and activation, whereas the R1C ≡ C-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif adsorbs benzyl alcohol. The exceptional catalytic performance stems from the synergy between adjacent, functionally distinct Au sites, enabled by the asymmetric coordination strategy. This study highlights the critical role of asymmetric coordination protocols in synergistic dual-site catalysis for aerobic oxidation, providing new ideas for the rational design of synergistic catalysts.

title: Multifunctional Electrospun Fibers Embedding CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals: A Route toward Superhydrophobic Flexible Polarized Optical Sources
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
