abstract: Abstract Cesium lead bromide (CsPbBr3) perovskite nanocrystals attract significant interest due to their exceptional optical properties, such as high photoluminescence quantum yield, tunable emission wavelength, and narrow emission bandwidth. These features make them ideal candidates for light-emitting diodes (LEDs), lasers, and optoelectronic devices. However, their practical application is limited by poor environmental stability and difficulties in preserving their optical performance. Embedding CsPbBr3 nanocrystals into optically inert polymers improves their resistance to moisture and oxidation while enabling flexible and scalable device fabrication. When polymers are processed into fibers, particularly via electrospinning, additional opportunities emerge. Electrospun fibers can align nanocrystals, producing anisotropic structures with directionally controlled emission and advanced wettability properties. This study investigates pre-synthesized CsPbBr3 nanocrystals embedded in electrospun PMMA fibers, focusing on their structural, physicochemical, and optical behavior. We analyze microcrystal formation and alignment along the fiber axis, which affects both crystallographic orientation and optical properties (absorption and emission wavelength, PL lifetime, and PL polarization). The aligned fibers also exhibit anisotropic wettability, showing a quasi-superhydrophobic behavior perpendicular to the fiber axis (contact angle ∼142°) and a hydrophilic character along it (∼80°), alongside strong PL stability under continuous laser excitation in standard ambient conditions (retaining about 85% of the initial PL intensity after 48 h of continuous laser pumping). By correlating crystal morphology, fiber alignment, and emission properties, this work advances the design of stable, directionally emissive perovskite-polymer composites for optoelectronic applications.

title: Janus Mesoporous Composite Nanospheres Assisted by Mild Thermal-Enhanced Bacterial Cuproptosis-like Death for Accelerated Wound Healing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Biofilm-induced bacterial infections are refractory to conventional antibiotics and easily cause persistent tissue damage, severely threatening human health. Copper-initiated cuproptosis-like death serves as an antibacterial pathway, yet simple copper supplementation fails to achieve satisfactory bactericidal effects due to bacterial copper homeostasis and physiological copper chelation. Copper ionophore elesclomol (ES) can selectively deliver intracellular copper to trigger cuproptosis, while photothermal therapy (PTT) is a promising antibacterial strategy with a low drug resistance risk. Herein, a Janus mesoporous ES-loaded nanoparticle (CSP@ES NPs) was fabricated to integrate cuproptosis-like death and PTT for therapy. In the acidic biofilm microenvironment, CSP@ES degrades sustainably to release Cu and ES, which disrupts bacterial copper homeostasis, downregulates dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase (DLAT)/FDX1 expression, and may trigger responses compatible with cuproptosis-like bacterial death. Combined with PTT, CSP@ES achieves prominent in vitro antibiofilm and in vivo antibacterial effects with favorable biosafety. This work provides a feasible multimodal therapeutic strategy for refractory bacterial infections with great clinical translation potential.

title: Performance-Based Evolution of Near-Infrared Serotonin Nanosensors from DNA-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Libraries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5HT) is an important neurotransmitter involved in the regulation of mood, appetite, and sleep, and its dysregulation has been associated with disorders such as depression and Parkinson’s disease. Selective molecular tools that can distinguish 5HT from other neurochemicals are essential for advancing both neurochemistry and disease-related research. However, conventional analytical methods are labor-intensive and sometimes suffer from poor discrimination among closely related neurotransmitters. In this study, we developed a near-infrared fluorescent 5HT nanosensor based on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) using a performance-based systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (pSELEC) strategy. Unlike conventional affinity-focused selection, this approach prioritized fluorescence modulation as the screening output and combined high-throughput microarray printing with automated fluorescence imaging to evaluate more than 108 ssDNA-SWCNT configurations. After characterizing the enriched DNA candidates, Seq6 was selected as a lead scaffold and underwent post-selection engineering, including covalent modification with a quencher dye and co-wrapping with spacer ssDNA. A methylene blue-conjugated Seq6 produced a “turn-off” fluorescence response to 5HT together with an opposite-direction response to dopamine (DA), providing improved discrimination between the two analytes. These findings demonstrate that pSELEC is a useful strategy for developing sensitive and selective near-infrared nanosensors for real-time neurotransmitter sensing.

title: Atomic-Scale Interface Engineering of CsPbBr3/TPBi Heterostructures for Tailored Optoelectronic Properties
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermal evaporation of halide perovskites and their organic barrier materials enables precise engineering of multiple quantum wells (MQWs) and superlattices for next-generation perovskite-based optoelectronics. However, the complex interplay of the interfacial interactions between the organic and inorganic moieties, which governs their structure–function properties, remains poorly understood. Here, we present a comprehensive theoretical–experimental investigation of CsPbBr3/TPBi heterostructures, focusing on the interplay between the perovskite growth front and TPBi molecular orientation. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that the CsBr-rich interface preferentially binds TPBi in an R45° configuration with a pronounced interfacial dipole (φID ≈ 0.018 eV) and significant upward band bending that enhances charge confinement. In contrast, the PbBr2-rich interface favors an R0° orientation, with minimal band bending (φID ≈ 0.002 eV). The molecular orientation modulates vacuum level shifts (ΔVLS), modifying the interfacial energy alignment. These predictions are corroborated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiling, UV–Vis absorption, and photoluminescence (PL) measurements, which confirm termination-dependent band bending and show enhanced PL from CsBr-rich interfaces. Our findings demonstrate that interfacial electronic properties can be precisely engineered through interface chemistry and molecular orientation. This paves the way for custom-designed perovskite MQWs with optimized charge confinement, emission, and carrier dynamics for high-performance optoelectronic applications.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: Optimal integration of Power-to-Vehicle and Power-to-Heat systems to support renewable deployment in smart urban energy districts
abstract: Decarbonising smart urban energy districts through distributed renewable generation requires planning frameworks able to capture sector-coupling flexibility, while accounting for the multidimensional trade-offs among technical, economic and environmental objectives. This study aims to address the complexity of energy district planning by applying a multi-objective optimisation framework to assess how Power-to-Heat and Power-to-Vehicle strategies can jointly enhance renewable integration. A residential district is modelled in EnergyPLAN comparing a reference configuration based on electricity grid and gas boilers with electrified scenarios including heating, cooling and transport demand under five electric vehicle penetration levels. For each scenario, photovoltaic, small-scale wind, electric batteries, and thermal storage capacities are optimised by minimising annual costs, critical excess electricity production, and CO 2 emissions. Results show that increasing electric vehicle penetration reduces emissions and annual costs, while lowering stationary battery requirements through smart charging flexibility. Beyond a certain level of on-site renewable deployment, further decarbonisation depends primarily on the combined electrification of mobility and domestic end-uses, rather than on additional renewable capacity alone. At intermediate electrification levels, thermal storage supports a solar-dominated mix, whereas higher electric vehicle penetration favours a more balanced renewable mix with reduced storage needs. The fully electrified configuration decreases primary fossil energy consumption, achieving 90% CO 2 abatement and reduces annual costs by about 7% compared with the reference case, while reaching 67% self-sufficiency and 79% self-consumption. The findings demonstrate that exploiting heat pumps and electric vehicles for system flexibility can enhance renewable integration and limit local excess electricity production.

title: Conformal La2O3 Interphase Regulates CEI Formation and Buffers Lattice Strain in 4.6 V LiCoO2 Cathodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Unlocking the high-voltage capability of LiCoO2 (LCO) is critical for next-generation high-energy lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), yet batteries cycled above 4.5 V suffer from an unstable cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), electrolyte corrosion, and lattice degradation. Herein, a conformal nano-La2O3 interphase is fabricated on LCO to regulate CEI formation and buffer lattice strain at 4.6 V. Different from inert coatings, the chemically active La2O3 interphase neutralizes HF from electrolyte decomposition and suppresses cobalt dissolution. In situ XRD verifies relieved anisotropic lattice fluctuation during Li+ (de)intercalation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that surface electronic reconstruction reduces the Li+ diffusion barrier from 1.50 to 1.05 eV and inhibits parasitic side reactions, while finite element simulations (FES) confirm homogenized local current and mitigated chemo-mechanical stress. Post-mortem characterizations demonstrate the formation of a thin, uniform CEI and restrained oxygen release. Owing to synergistic protection, La2O3@LCO delivers an initial charge capacity of 233.45 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and 77% retention after 300 cycles at 0.5 C (4.6 V cut-off). This work provides insights into functional interphase design for durable high-voltage layered oxide cathodes.

title: Atomic-Scale View of Water Adsorption on the TiO2 Anatase Surface: From Isolated Molecules to Multilayers
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Water adsorption governs the surface chemistry of TiO2 nanomaterials, yet its molecular organization under realistic hydration conditions remains difficult to resolve. Combining theory and experiment on both shape-controlled and commercial TiO2 nanoparticles, we provide an atomic-scale picture of water adsorption from isolated molecules to multilayers, bridging surface science and realistic nanomaterials. By integrating microgravimetry with in situ IR spectroscopy, we correlate the intensity of the water bending mode and the adsorbed water amount, determining a molar absorption coefficient of ε(δH2O) = 1.54 ± 0.08 cm µmol–1. This enables the water bending vibration to be used as a quantitative spectroscopic descriptor of surface hydration. Comparison with static and dynamic DFT vibrational spectra shows that finite-temperature molecular dynamics is essential to reproduce the experimental spectral evolution, as static calculations overconstrain the hydrogen-bond network. The combined IR–microgravimetric–computational approach allows representative hydration regimes to be assigned to molecular surface organizations: from strongly bound water molecules at Ti sites, through a hydrogen-bonded monolayer, to weakly bound outer multilayers. By translating surface-science precision to realistic nanomaterials, this work provides a transferable framework for quantifying and interpreting water adsorption at oxide surfaces at atomistic level, opening the way to operando tracking of hydration-dependent surface chemistry in (photo)catalysis and biointerfaces.

title: Interfacial Control of a GaN-Based High Electron Mobility Transistor via a SiN x Nanomask: From Wetting Dynamics to Breakdown Enhancement
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The controlled overgrowth of GaN on Si using a SiNx nanomask has attracted considerable attention, yet the relationship between the SiH4 precursor flux, interfacial growth kinetics, and device performance has not been fully established. Here, we employed pixel-wise spatial and spectral information from hyperspectral cathodoluminescence (HYP-CL) mapping to expose the SiH4 flow rate-mediated interfacial wetting/dewetting behavior of the SiNx nanomask that drastically affected the GaN nucleation kinetics at the SiNx/GaN interface. A low SiH4 flux induced wetting behavior, leading to a laterally extended SiNx nanomask, resulting in premature GaN island coalescence. Meanwhile, at a higher SiH4 flux, the observations are consistent with a wetting-to-dewetting behavioral transition, leading to aggregated SiNx clusters, resulting in vertically extended coalescence-free GaN pillars. Through this study, we unraveled the trade-off between cross-sectional film continuity and threading dislocation density suppression, which directly translates to the electrical performance. Also, we establish a design principle for nanomask engineering at semiconductor interfaces based on CL imaging for optimizing buffer layer design in high-voltage GaN-based devices.

title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. However, early-stage formation of passivating oxide shells severely restricts oxygen diffusion, resulting in incomplete oxidation and limited energy utilization. Here, we report a Ce-assisted microstructure design strategy to overcome this long-standing diffusion barrier by constructing three-dimensional oxygen-diffusion scaffolds within aluminum-based fuels through trace cerium addition. Rapidly solidified Al–xCe powders develop an interconnected Al11Ce3 network, which subdivides the Al matrix into fine domains. During heating and combustion, this Al11Ce3 network is preferentially oxidized into a CeO2-x/CeO2-containing scaffold before extensive Al oxidation, thereby providing continuous oxygen-transport pathways into the particle interior. As a result, Al–xCe alloy powders exhibit shorter ignition delay, faster flame propagation, shorter combustion duration, and more complete oxidation than pure Al. This work establishes a general and scalable design principle for enhancing metal-fuel combustion through rare-earth-enabled oxygen-diffusion networks.

title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BOx catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BOx inverse catalyst featuring engineered defects localized at face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter. Using an oxidative atmosphere-induced exsolution strategy, we continuously tune the face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase ratio, maximizing the density of stacking faults at a 1:1 phase ratio. Catalytic activity exhibits a strong positive correlation with stacking fault density, with the optimal CoF/H-1.0@BOx catalyst achieving 32% propane conversion and 83% olefin selectivity at 450 °C—5.1 times that of pristine cobalt boride. Density functional theory reveals that stacking faults modulate Co atomic spacing, weakening the excessively strong BOx-Co interfacial interaction. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Friction at solid-liquid interfaces is typically interpreted through classical contact mechanics, but molecular origins of gas-bubble friction in aqueous environments remain elusive. Here we report the direct quantification of gas-bubble friction at solid surfaces using atomic force microscopy with nanonewton resolution. We show that bubbles enter a contact-line friction regime only after film-mediated attachment, with static and kinetic responses that reflect contact-line pinning and sliding. On octadecyltrichlorosilane-grafted substrates, friction varies non-monotonically with surface hydrophobicity, peaking at intermediate hydrophobicity due to enhanced chemical heterogeneity. Surface chemistry and nanostructure further regulate energy dissipation, with relatively low friction on uniformly rough polydimethylsiloxane-grafted surfaces. Oxygen bubbles generate higher friction than air, nitrogen and carbon dioxide bubbles, as supported by molecular dynamics simulations that implicate gas-specific intermolecular interactions in contact-line dissipation. These findings provide molecular-level insight into gas-bubble friction, with implications for friction-tunable interfaces in catalysis, microfluidics, and medical applications.

title: Performance and damage mechanisms of dispersion-strengthened tungsten under H-mode plasma in DIII-D
abstract: Dispersion strengthened tungsten (DSW) alloys are promising materials for plasma facing components, displaying improved mechanical properties and microstructure stability compared to pure tungsten. In this work, the performance of DSW reinforced with 1 wt% transition-metal carbide (TaC, TiC, or ZrC) has been examined under H-mode plasma in the DIII-D tokamak. DSW samples were mounted both flush with the divertor floor and at a 10 angle towards the incoming plasma fluxes to further increase the heat and particle loading. To simulate the impact of prolonged tokamak operation, similar plasma exposures were repeated on two additional sets of DSW samples: one set pre-implanted with 10 m helium, and another set heated in-situ to an additional 500 C. Flush mounted samples exhibited good surface stability, with no evidence of melting or cracking regardless of composition or treatment. Carbon redeposition was observed on most samples, likely due to the graphite environment of DIII-D. Under coupled thermal loading and helium implantation, surface nanostructuring developed in some DSW samples; however, DSW containing tantalum dispersion phases showed strong resistance to such surface modification. In contrast, obvious surface melting was observed on 10 angled samples containing TaC and ZrC dispersoids, likely associated with dispersoid oxidation during fabrication, which reduced thermal conductivity and promoted elevated surface temperatures during plasma exposure. The grain morphology of DSW containing TiC remained largely unchanged, although near-surface dispersoids on the angled TiC sample were missing after plasma exposure. The loss is associated with oxidation of the dispersoids during fabrication, followed by sublimation during plasma exposure. Through systematic comparison of DSW performance under H mode plasma conditions, this study identifies key degradation mechanisms and highlights strategies to improve the performance of DSW as plasma facing materials.

title: First experimental observation of ‘Staircase’ high confinement mode in tokamak plasma
abstract: In magnetically confined nuclear fusion, the achievement of ignition necessitates the tokamak plasma in a high confinement state known as H-mode. A major challenge encountered in the standard H-mode is the abrupt collapse of its ultrathin edge layer. Here, we report a first experimental demonstration that a stable H-mode can be sustained by a staircase plasma profile. The basic physical picture is: by staircasing the plasma profile, the potential free energy stored in one single large edge layer is distributed into multiple mesoscale layers throughout the entire plasma volume. Consequently, the large scale edge collapse is converted into small scale desynchronized fluctuations, effectively reducing the risk of violent relaxation event. This finding uncovers a new benign high confinement regime of the tokamak plasma.

title: Dry Surface Decontamination of Nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and Blister (HD) Chemical Warfare Agents Using TiO2/CeO2 Nanosorbents
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dry surface decontamination is a highly practical approach for mitigating chemical warfare agent (CWA) threats without generating liquid waste. Herein, we systematically investigate the dry decontamination performance of nanoscale TiO2, CeO2, and mixed TiO2/CeO2 (TiCe) sorbents against nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and blister (HD) agents. Materials characterization confirms that mixing Ti and Ce shifts the microstructure into a highly open, mesoporous network, significantly expanding the total pore volume to 1.01 cm3/g. In dry batch experiments, all nanosorbents achieved rapid, complete depletion of parent extractable G-agents within 10 min, while the Novichok agent A-234 was reduced to <4% within 10 min, exhibiting comparable performance under both ambient daylight and complete darkness. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first demonstration of fully dry Novichok detoxification using metal oxide-based sorbents. Blister agent HD underwent slower degradation, achieving near-complete depletion (with <3% residual) after 480 min. GC–MS analysis confirmed that depletion is driven by safe hydrolytic pathways yielding low-toxicity derivatives, without hazardous oxidation byproducts. When applied to contaminated ceramic tiles, the dry powders successfully transferred and removed all parent CWAs to levels undetectable by GC–FID and GC–MS in both immediate and aged scenarios, except for A-234 on CeO2 (3.7% residue). These findings demonstrate that practical dry surface decontamination is governed by rapid mechanical transfer followed by intra-sorbent degradation. Furthermore, the successful up-scaling of the nanoporous TiO2 synthesis to a kilo-lab scale highlights the straightforward scalability of these materials for real-world applications on delicate equipment.

title: Interface Engineering of the Insulator to Metal Transition in V2O3 Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Vanadium sesquioxide (V2O3) is a strongly correlated oxide that presents an insulator-to-metal transition (IMT) at a critical temperature (Tc) of about 160 K. In this work, we present a systematic control of Tc and resistance ratio across the IMT of sputtered V2O3 thin films by interface engineering. Implementing a pregrown nanometer-thick V2O3 buffer layer allows tuning of Tc over a 20 K range toward higher temperatures. Extensive state-of-the-art structural analysis, including X-ray diffraction and high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, shows that the Tc shift is primarily associated with modulated strain at the film/substrate interface. Furthermore, incorporating nitrogen during buffer layer growth continuously reduces the resistance of the insulating phase, providing a straightforward method to tune the IMT on–off ratio. Engineered films show enhanced functionalities, including a reduction in resistive-switching threshold power and stable self-spiking oscillations. Our results show that a two-step deposition of V2O3 films offers a robust and practical pathway to energy efficiency and scalability in neuromorphic and resistive-switching applications.

title: Scalable Deposition Strategies for All-Inorganic Perovskite Thin Films via Ambient Slot-Die Coating
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract All-inorganic cesium lead halide perovskites, such as CsPbI3, exhibit excellent thermal stability and outstanding optoelectronic properties, making them highly attractive for next-generation photovoltaic and light-emitting applications. Despite these advantages, their practical implementation is hindered by intrinsic polymorphism triggering spontaneous phase transitions toward the non-photoactive yellow δ-phase, severely compromising device performance and long-term stability. To overcome these challenges, we deploy phase-stabilization strategies based on dimethylammonium iodide (DMAI) additive and mixed-halide I/Br compositional engineering to suppress undesired phase formation and enable reproducible, high-quality thin films. Beyond materials design, scalable fabrication remains a critical requirement for industrial adoption. Here, we demonstrate the deposition of CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite films over large areas under ambient atmosphere using slot-die coating. Process optimization combined with effective surface passivation yields devices achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.8% for slot-die-coated solar cells fabricated on 5 × 10 cm2 substrates (active area of 0.09 cm2). Furthermore, a five-cell minimodule with an active area of 3.65 cm2 delivers a PCE reaching 13.0%, underscoring the scalability and industrial relevance of the proposed approach. In addition, the device stability, assessed through light cycling tests, reveals promising durability, with devices maintaining 80% of their initial performance (T80) for more than 80 h.

title: Interfacially Compliant Li+-Ion Conductive Polymer Layer for Stabilizing Composite Cathode in Sulfide-Based All-Solid-State Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) are promising next-generation energy storage systems owing to their high energy density and enhanced safety. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish Li+ transport and oxidative degradation of sulfide solid electrolytes within the composite cathode, which progressively increase interfacial resistance during cycling. Here, we introduce an interfacially compliant and Li+-ion conductive polymer layer (ICPL), composed of poly(1,4-butylene adipate) (PBA) and lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB), to simultaneously facilitate Li+ transport and stabilize the LiNi0.90Co0.05Mn0.05O2(NCM90)/Li6PS5Cl interface. The PBA matrix promotes the dissociation of LiDFOB while maintaining a viscous, amorphous state, thereby establishing intimate and conformal contact with Li6PS5Cl. Within the ICPL, the mobile Li+ provides additional ion-conduction pathways within the composite cathode, whereas DFOB– preferentially contributes to the formation of a robust B-rich interphase that mitigates the oxidative decomposition of Li6PS5Cl. This synergistic regulation of interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport suppresses impedance growth and enables stable cycling of ASSLBs employing NCM90 composite cathodes at 0.33 C. These findings demonstrate that coupling interfacial compliance with salt-mediated ion conduction and interphase chemistry provides an effective materials-design strategy for stabilizing high-energy sulfide-based ASSLBs.

title: Colloidal Quantum Dot Photodetectors: From Nanocrystal Materials to Monolithically Integrated Imaging
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Colloidal quantum dot (CQD) photodetectors offer a promising, low-cost, solution-processed approach to infrared imaging. This review details their development, from controlling nanocrystal synthesis to integrating CQD photodiodes with silicon readout circuits. It focuses on five material platforms: lead and mercury chalcogenides, perovskite CQDs, heavy-metal-free silver chalcogenides and AgBiS2, and III–V CQDs such as InAs and InSb. The discussion covers device architectures that balance gain, noise, and speed, as well as the evolution from single pixels to complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor focal plane arrays and flexible wearable devices. The review concludes by examining key challenges, operational stability, the gain–noise–speed tradeoff, pixel yield, heavy-metal substitution, spectral extension, and defect passivation that will determine whether CQD imagers progress from experimental demos to commercial products.

title: Resolving Coupled Cathode–Anode Failures in Li–S Batteries via Spin-State-Modulated Spinel Dual Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage due to their high theoretical specific energy. However, their practical applications are limited by kinetic mismatch between cathodic sulfur conversion and anodic lithium deposition, causing sluggish sulfur redox kinetics and heterogeneous Li growth. Here, we employ a homologous dual-interface CoMnFe@CNF architecture to reveal a site-differentiated interfacial regulation mechanism for synchronizing sulfur and lithium kinetics. Fe3+ incorporation triggers spin-state-dependent electronic reconstruction in the spinel lattice, generating distinct tetrahedral (Td) Co3+ and octahedral (Oh) Mn3+ centers. The reconstructed Td-Co3+ sites enhance polysulfide adsorption and facilitate sulfur redox kinetics. Meanwhile, Oh-Mn3+ centers regulate Li+ solvation and transport, enabling uniform Li deposition. This site-differentiated coordination establishes a cathode–anode kinetic synchronization mechanism, enabling Li–S full cells to retain 76.9% capacity after 400 cycles at 1 C. This work provides a spinel site-engineering strategy for rational regulation of coupled interfacial kinetics.

title: Interfacial Reorganization by Nonionic Surfactants Governs the Stability and Bioactivity of Exosomes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Exosomes are promising nanoscale agents that can serve both as efficient drug delivery carriers and as bioactive therapeutics with intrinsic biological functions. Yet their clinical translation is hindered by formulation-dependent instability and an incomplete understanding of excipient–membrane interactions. Here, we systematically and, to our knowledge, for the first time dissect how nonionic surfactants govern exosome stability, membrane organization, and bioactivity across sub- to supra-critical micelle concentration regimes. Using bovine exosomes as a model, we verify that exosomes in phosphate-buffered saline are intrinsically metastable, undergoing progressive interfacial reorganization and particle loss even at 4 °C. Surfactants exhibit distinct, structure-dependent effects: polysorbates (PS20, PS80) reduce hydrodynamic size but accelerate particle loss, whereas poloxamer 188 (P188) preserves both size and concentration. Membrane analysis shows that polysorbates increase lipid fluidity, potentially through interactions with the lipid bilayer. P188 may act through preferential surface association with limited effects on the measured lipid packing environment. Functionally, PS20 enhances cellular uptake at the expense of structural integrity, whereas P188 maintains vesicle integrity with moderate functional gain. Across multiple exosome sources, these trends are conserved, demonstrating the generality of the underlying mechanisms. Together, our results establish a mechanistic framework linking surfactant structure, concentration, and membrane interaction to both physicochemical stability and biological performance, providing actionable design principles for exosome formulations.

title: Metal–Organic Framework-Derived Magnetic Nanoparticles Inducing Interfacial Polarization Enabling MXene-Based Composite Films with High-Efficiency Electromagnetic Interference Shielding
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With outstanding conductivity, tunable structure, and rich surface functional groups, two-dimensional (2D) MXene is extensively used for the electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding field. However, MXene suffers from self-stacking and secondary reflection pollution, which weakens the electromagnetic wave (EMW) attenuation performance. Herein, we introduced one-dimensional (1D) PPy nanotubes (NTs) and (FeO)0.198(MnO)0.802 (FMO) magnetic nanoparticles derived from FeMn-metal–organic frameworks into the MXene system. Furthermore, combined with K+-induced filtration and freeze-drying technology, MXene/PPy NTs/FMO (MPFMO) composite films with three-dimensional (3D) porous structures were successfully constructed, thereby achieving significantly enhanced EMI shielding performances. The introduction of conductive PPy NTs not only refines the 3D conductive architecture embedded within the composite film but also induces forming hydrogen bonding and supports adjacent MXene nanosheets to increase the mechanical properties. The abundant heterogeneous interfaces can generate interfacial polarization and promote EMW absorption, and the intrinsic magnetic loss of FMO can further attenuate EMWs. Profiting from multiple synergy mechanisms, the MPFMO porous composite film delivers a high EMI SE of 62.43 dB, an absorption loss ratio of 72.50%, and specific shielding effectiveness SSEt of 1.21 × 104 dB cm2 g–1 at a thickness of only 55 μm. Notably, the as-prepared composite membrane also demonstrates a superior thermal conductivity of 18.82 W m–1 K–1.

title: Graphene/MXene/Polydimethylsiloxane Composite Skin with Multiband Electromagnetic Absorption and Active/Passive Dual-Mode Infrared Camouflage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of low-cost, highly reliable, and multispectral-compatible stealth materials remains challenging, necessitating ingenious microstructure design and a suitable multicomponent strategy. In this study, we fabricate graphene/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and MXene-graphene/PDMS composite elastic films. The construction of porous architectures and multidimensional heterogeneous interfaces has enabled the realization of an integrated design that combines radar wave absorption with active and passive infrared thermal management. The superior microwave absorption performance exhibited by the elastic films is attributable to the electromagnetic wave loss mechanisms facilitated by extensive continuous heterogeneous interfaces, including appropriate impedance matching, abundant interface/dipole polarization, and multiple reflections and scattering. At a thickness of 2.5 mm, the G5T3P minimum reflection loss (RLmin) reaches as low as –48.84 dB, and at a thickness of 2 mm, the G8P effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) reaches 5.32 GHz. Concurrently, the intrinsic low infrared emissivity of MXene, combined with the porous framework, generates a powerful thermal camouflage effect. Within a broad temperature range of 100–300 °C, the material provides both stable passive infrared stealth and the capacity for active modulation of thermal infrared signals under an applied voltage of 10–50 V. This work offers a potential technical approach toward improving radar/IR compatibility for stealth materials.

title: Direct Inkjet Printing of Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
last_author: Louis C. P. M. de Smet
abstract: Abstract There is a growing need for gas and volatile organic compound (VOC) sensors in many areas, including air quality, safety monitoring, and (early) disease detection. VOC sensors can make use of affinity coatings to increase their sensitivity and selectivity. With their intrinsic high surface areas and chemically tunable pores, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are excellent candidates for the design and fabrication of such affinity coatings. However, precise, scalable, and easy deposition of such COF materials is proven to still be a challenge. In this study, we show the controlled deposition of COFs through direct inkjet printing for the first time, for which COFs are prepared as colloidal suspensions, serving as ready-to-use inks. We present a facile colloidal synthesis, leading to colloidal suspensions that are stable for months and which allow inkjet printing without any further processing. The COFs can be printed on gold as both isolated spots and as thin layers. The synthesis and printing conditions were carefully optimized to strike the balance between colloidal stability, printing robustness, and controlled drying. After exposure to saturated VOC environments, the printed layers show VOC desorption as monitored by infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy, not only confirming partial retention of the porous nature of the printed COF particles but also demonstrating the applicability of printed COF layers as affinity coatings on VOC sensors.

title: Atom-level pinning effect reinforced electrooxidative coupling of anilines into azos
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrosynthesis of azo compounds via aniline oxidation represents a sustainable alternative to conventional methods, yet its efficiency is largely limited by sequential N–H dehydrogenation and N–N self-coupling steps. Herein, a single-atom Ba-doped nickel hydroxide (C-Ba1Ni1-x(OH)2) with an atom-level pinning effect is engineered to tailor a robust carbonate-functionalized interface and a spatially favorable Ni–O–Ni motif for N–H dehydrogenation and N–N coupling of aniline, respectively. The C-Ba1Ni1-x(OH)2 achieves electrooxidative coupling of various anilines, with up to 95.8% yield and 98.2% Faradaic efficiency for azos, along with good tolerance. Mechanistic investigations elucidate that carbonate bound on Ba single-atom weakens O/N–H interaction to increase their H removability that promotes adjacent Ni2+–OH reconstruction to generate active Ni3+–O species and bolsters N–H dehydrogenation of aniline (Ph-NH2), favoring *Ph-N intermediate generation. Further, single-atom Ba compresses the neighboring Ni–O–Ni distance to spatially favor *Ph-N self-coupling, overall facilitating azo electrosynthesis. This atomic-level strain engineering delivers a generalizable paradigm to construct self-adaptive electrodes for multi-step electrochemical transformations.

title: Mitigating brittleness in ceramics via transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ceramics usually exhibit inherent brittleness at room temperature due to their strong covalent/ionic bonding and few active slip systems. Consequently, ceramics exhibit a low damage-bearing capacity and typically sudden failure prior to yielding. Thus, achieving room-temperature plasticity while maintaining or enhancing the strength of ceramics remains critical and challenging. Here, we report a promising strategy to address this problem by concurrently activating twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in a monolithic TaN ceramic film. Through precisely controlled physical vapor deposition, we stabilize the metastable δ-TaN phase with hierarchical nanotwinned architectures. Then, by combining micromechanical tests, atomic-resolution characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the synergy of phase transformation and twinning brings exceptional damage tolerance and plasticity, achieving up to 60% compressive strain without catastrophic fracture alongside a hardness of ~43 GPa. Our work not only proves the feasibility of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity synergy in designing ultrahard and ductile materials, but also highlights the architecture optimization in nanotwinned ceramics.

title: Thermodynamic Activity Regulation Enables Low-Voltage Alloy-Mediated CO2-to-Carbon Conversion
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molten-carbonate electrolysis integrates CO2 capture with conversion to storable solid carbon, yet direct carbonate electroreduction suffers from cathodic polarization, raising cell voltage and energy consumption. Here, the cathodic pathway is redesigned by coupling electrochemical alkali-metal alloying with thermochemical carbonate reduction. Alloying with liquid metals lowers the thermodynamic activity of the alkali-metal mediator and shifts its equilibrium alloying potential to more positive values, while sufficient activity must be retained to drive subsequent thermochemical carbonate reduction. These competing constraints define a thermodynamic reactive window that guides liquid-metal screening, identifying Sb as a host. Stepwise experiments separating alloying from open-circuit thermochemical carbon formation directly support the proposed pathway. Liquid Sb sustains CO2-to-carbon electrolysis for 72 h at 700 °C and 2.0 V with 80.9% Faradaic efficiency and 22.08 kWh kg C–1 electrical energy consumption, 36.9% below a reported solid-electrode benchmark. These results establish thermodynamic activity regulation as a strategy for lower-voltage electrochemical–chemical conversion.

title: When Is Molecular-Dynamics-Predicted Ionic Diffusivity Reliable in Solid Electrolytes?
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics is widely used to predict ionic diffusivity in solid electrolytes, but the reliability of these predictions is often difficult to assess. Our analysis identifies finite trajectory length, limited cell size, and insufficient sampling as key limitations. Using cubic Li7La3Zr2O12, we show that these limitations can remain hidden behind apparently linear mean-squared displacements and well-behaved Arrhenius relations, leading to inaccurate diffusivities, activation energies, and extrapolated Nernst–Einstein conductivity estimates. Such errors can misrank candidate materials and misdirect computational screening. We examine the local mean-squared-displacement exponent, α(t), as a diagnostic of dynamical convergence and relate it quantitatively to finite-time bias in an MSD-ratio estimator within a caging-diffusion model. This relation estimates a characteristic analysis time for a prescribed accuracy. Independent replicas reduce statistical uncertainty, while selective single-axis expansion mitigates finite-size effects. These findings improve materials ranking and the efficiency of computational screening.

title: Ionic and bicontinuous mesoporous carbon nitride with multilevel structures for continuous tandem photosynthesis of value-added chemicals

By repurposing a sacrificial agent into a high-value pharmaceutical intermediate (BzlM), this dual-functional catalyst sustains co-production in a continuous-flow reactor for over 200 hours, offering a generalizable strategy for sustainable biphasic chemical synthesis.

title: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination
abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

title: Beyond Current Matching: A Voltage-Matched Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Mini-module as an Alternative to Monolithic Tandems
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Current matching limits the performance of two-terminal (2T) monolithic perovskite-silicon tandems. Voltage-matched (VM) tandems remove this constraint by connecting the perovskite and silicon sub-modules in parallel. Here, we report an area-matched 2T VM perovskite-silicon mini-module with a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.77% at minimal voltage mismatch. Tuning the voltage-matching ratio (VMratio, the ratio of the perovskite to silicon maximum-power-point voltages) through the silicon cell count reveals an asymmetry between the silicon- and perovskite-limited regimes: at equal voltage mismatch, the PCE loss relative to the four-terminal (4T) tandem is 1.1% (absolute) lower in the silicon-limited regime. Under controlled temperature (0–60 °C) and spectral variation, the VM tandem remains within 0.1–1.7% and 0.8–1.2% absolute of the 4T tandem, respectively, demonstrating near-4T performance with a two-terminal connection.

title: Competitive Coordination of Solvent in Electrolyte to Stabilize Li-Rich Mn-Based Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The practical application of lithium metal batteries equipped with lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxide (LRMO) cathodes is severely impeded by aggressive electrolyte decomposition under operational voltage above 4.5 V. Herein, we discover a unique competitive solvent coordination behavior in the electrolyte solvation structure that enables significant stabilization of LRMO-based batteries. This rarely reported mechanism inspires the design of a low-concentration electrolyte (0.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate, LiPF6), which employs a binary fluorinated solvent system consisting of weakly solvating tris(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) phosphate (TFP) and ethyl difluoroacetate (EDFA). Benefiting from the optimized solvation structure, the assembled Li||LRMO cells achieve cycling stability, retaining 80.5% of the initial capacity after 450 cycles at 4.8 V and 0.5 C. We further establish a molecular-level interfacial model to elucidate the performance enhancement mechanism. This work provides insights into the unique competitive coordination effect of solvents within solvation structures and offers an innovative strategy for electrolyte design toward LRMO-based battery systems and beyond.

title: Incorporating Noncanonical Amino Acids for Protein Structure Analysis: Site-Directed Spin Labeling CW and Pulsed EPR Approaches
abstract: Abstract Site-directed spin labeling in combination with electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy (SDSL–EPR) has emerged as a powerful and highly adaptable platform probing protein structure and dynamics with residue-level precision. In its classical strategy, a stable paramagnetic label, most commonly a nitroxide radical, but not only, is covalently introduced at a predefined position, typically through an engineered cysteine residue. Continuous-wave (cw) EPR spectroscopy provides sensitivity to protein dynamics across a broad range of time scales (and techniques), from backbone motions (ps-ns) to protein complex assembly and conformational transitions (ms-s) or characterization of protein conformational exchange (μs-ms). Pulsed EPR methodologies, particularly double electron–electron resonance (DEER), provide access to long-range distance distributions in the nanometer regime (ca. 2–8 nm) through the measurement of dipolar interactions between pairs of spin labels. Recent developments in the genetic encoding of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) have substantially expanded the scope of SDSL–EPR by overcoming the intrinsic limitations associated with cysteine-based labeling. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of ncAA-based spin-labeling strategies for SDSL–EPR, discuss the repertoire of reported spin labels and their synthetic routes, and highlight representative applications in structural investigations of proteins in vitro as well as in cellular environments.

title: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
abstract: The economics of residential electrification in high-cost electricity regions remain uncertain. Using metered data from over 20,000 California homes, we assess the economic, environmental, and equity impacts of end-use electrification under rollout strategies based on household income and gas infrastructure age. Even under favorable electricity rates, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values (NPVs). Cost-effectiveness improves with deeper electrification scenarios, particularly when more costs are shifted to fixed charges and for homes with existing air conditioning—54–67% of these households break even when electrifying space heating, compared to fewer than 5% of those without. Income-based rebates more than double the share of low- and moderate-income households with positive NPVs. Prioritizing areas with aging gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions on par with high-income-led adoption and avoids costly pipeline replacement, but requires the highest subsidy to achieve cost-effectiveness across all households. These findings highlight trade-offs in designing equitable electrification strategies.

title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
abstract: The active transport and retention principle states that nanoparticles enter tumours via endothelial cells and exit via lymphatic drainage. How nanoparticles are retained in the tumour microenvironment remains unclear. Here we report a computational strategy to determine the mechanism of nanoparticle retention in solid tumours. We find that tumour cellular and acellular components delay and obstruct the movement of nanoparticles by influencing nanoparticle drag, Brownian and electric forces. We mathematically define nanoparticle retention based on these interactions, linking retention quantitatively to tumour pathophysiology, nanoparticle design and delivery efficiency. We create a software interface to simulate and predict nanoparticle retention across different tumour systems and nanoparticle designs, enabling us to select optimal tumour and nanoparticle delivery conditions for better therapeutic outcomes.

title: Development and Application of Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing
abstract: Abstract Individual RNA strands can be sequenced directly using nanoscale protein pores. This process, Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing (Nanopore DRS), uses a helicase motor protein to regulate RNA displacement through the nanopore orifice in single nucleotide steps. Partial blockade of the monovalent ionic current is recorded at 4 kHz and converted to a string of RNA nucleotide basecalls using machine learning models. In this review, we discuss the development of Nanopore DRS from 1996 to the present. This includes performance metrics, evolution of machine learning models, and applications of Nanopore DRS to major RNA classes across kingdoms. Advantages of the technology are highlighted with special emphasis on nucleotide modifications along intact single strands. Shortcomings of the technology are also considered along with possible solutions. We close with forward looking Nanopore DRS applications: Single cell RNA sequencing; remote monitoring of infectious agents; principled understanding of nanopore ionic current patterns using all-atoms simulations; global food security; and clinical applications.

title: Revealing the Atomic-Scale Degradation of Platinum-Based Intermetallic Nanocatalysts Upon Relevant Fuel Cell Conditions
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Platinum-based intermetallic nanomaterials are promising catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, insights regarding their degradation under realistic PEMFC conditions still represent a knowledge gap. Herein, a systematic series of L12-Pt3M (M = V, Cr, or Zn) intermetallics with a similar structure, chemical composition, and morphology were synthesized, and their activity-stability trends were evaluated under conditions relevant to PEMFCs. Time- and potential-resolved catalyst dissolution were acquired and quantified through online ICP-MS using 1 M HClO4 at 65 °C, revealing that the first catalyst/electrolyte contact induces significant catalyst degradation before operation. During electrochemical operation, the anodic dissolution at 65 °C is substantially higher than at 25 °C, and a strong competition between cathodic dissolution and ion redeposition takes place. Identical-location electron microscopy analyses captured atomic degradation processes directly linked to catalyst electrochemical dissolution enhanced by temperature, providing new understanding for developing robust catalysts for PEMFCs.

title: Substitution Reactions of Halogen-Substituted Acetals: Glycosylations and Related Reactions
abstract: Abstract The nucleophilic substitution reactions of halogen-substituted acetals are useful for the synthesis of a variety of compounds, most particularly of sugar derivatives. This review will summarize the current understanding of the mechanisms involved in these reactions and will present substitution reactions of carbohydrate derivatives with fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine substituents. The halogen atom at C-2 can have a powerful influence on the stereoselectivities of the glycosylation reactions, most often leading to 1,2-trans stereoselectivity. Examples of the uses of these halogen-substituted products will also be provided.

title: Stepwise Proximity Labeling With a Switchable Organophotocatalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoinducible proximity labeling (PL) using photocatalysts offers high spatiotemporal resolution for profiling protein–protein interactions (PPIs). Conventional approaches require genetic installation of a tag to tether the photocatalyst to a protein of interest (POI), which may perturb native protein function and cause artificial labeling. Ligand‐directed delivery of photocatalysts to native POIs has emerged as a tag‐free alternative; however, this strategy suffers from nonspecific labeling by unbound catalysts and an inherent washing dilemma, where insufficient washing leads to background labeling while excessive washing disrupts ligand binding. These limitations have severely restricted tag‐free and ligand‐directed PPI profiling. Herein, we report a switchable photoinducible PL strategy based on a nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) unit that becomes catalytically active only after covalent conjugation to a POI. This approach consists of a two‐step process: introduction of an N ‐NBD moiety into the POI using a catalytically inactive O ‐NBD unit, followed by light‐induced PL catalyzed by N ‐NBD. N ‐methyl luminol and 1‐methyl‐4‐arylurazole were identified as labeling reagents selectively activated by N ‐NBD. Targeting mitochondrial voltage‐dependent anion channel (VDAC) enabled selective labeling and proteomic identification of mitochondrial proteins. This switchable PL method circumvents the washing dilemma, suppresses nonspecific labeling, and enables tag‐free proteomic analysis with improved spatial selectivity.

title: Anodic Selective Etching: A Mechanism‐Centric Perspective for Electrochemical Subtractive Manufacturing
abstract: ABSTRACT Anodic selective etching (ASE) is a precision electrochemical subtractive manufacturing strategy that enables controllable material removal, interfacial reconstruction, and morphology evolution under electrochemically controlled conditions. Unlike material‐centric reviews that mainly catalogue substrates or products, this mechanism‐centric framework reveals common electrochemical principles, enabling cross‐material comparison, transferable design rules, and predictive control over selectivity, reaction location, and structural evolution. This review unifies ASE across material platforms and structural scales through five dominant modes: composition‐ and phase‐selective anodic dissolution, structural site‐selective anodic etching, semiconductor carrier‐ and space‐charge‐controlled etching, film‐ and passivation‐controlled subtraction, and geometry‐ or three‐phase boundary‐localized etching, together with representative coupled mechanisms. The roles of anodic material characteristics, electrolyte composition, and electrochemical parameters in defining selectivity windows, localization behavior, and structural outcomes are critically discussed. These mechanisms enable low‐dimensional materials, porous and core–shell architectures, surface finishing and shaping, and meniscus‐localized tip fabrication. Key challenges in multicomponent selectivity, electrolyte sustainability, and scalable manufacturing are outlined, alongside opportunities in in situ and operando characterization, multi‐physics modeling, and data‐driven optimization toward reproducible and programmable electrochemical manufacturing.

title: Metallurgical Interface Engineering Constructing In Situ Li 3 N‐Enriched Interphase: A Bulk‐Interface Synergy Strategy Toward Practical Silicon Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries but suffer from volume expansion, unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and sluggish Li + diffusion. Herein, we report a vacuum‐suspension‐melted (VSM) bulk multiphase integration and interphase modification strategy to address these challenges. Unlike conventional mechanical mixing, VSM constructs a SiSnM (M = Bi, Ni) composite with metallurgically bonded Si/metal interfaces, forming a conductive network that buffers internal stress via atomic‐scale interfacial stress transfer. Simultaneously, a polydopamine‐derived nitrogen‐doped carbon coating transforms in situ into a Li 3 N‐enriched interphase during cycling, which exhibits high ionic/electronic conductivity, accelerates interfacial charge transfer, and suppresses continuous SEI breakdown. The resulting SiSnM@Li 3 N anode delivers 87.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1.5 A g −1 and >1000 mAh g −1 at 15 A g −1 , with reliable operation from −30°C to 60°C. Stable cycling at 2.5 mg cm −2 confirms practical relevance. Full cells with Li‐rich Mn‐based cathodes show stable performance, and 5 Ah‐level pouch cells deliver 84.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 6 A discharge. This work concurrently tackles ionic, electronic, and mechanical constraints, offering a practical path to high‐energy durable Si‐based batteries.

title: Acoustic‐Electromagnetic Information Sensing and Security Protection via Intelligent Transparency Metasurfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Acoustic‐electromagnetic (EM) cross‐domain sensing converts information carried by sound‐induced mechanical vibrations into remotely measurable EM signals, supporting applications in human–computer interaction, environmental sensing, and the Internet of Things. However, the ability to reconstruct acoustic information from weak phase signatures in EM echoes also creates a risk of acoustic information leakage. Existing shielding and encryption schemes are difficult to combine with covert integration and real‐time reconfigurability, and struggle to intervene directly in the mapping process, thereby are poorly suited to end‐to‐end threats in complex scenarios. Here, we propose an interface for cross‐domain sensing and security protection based on an optically transparent intelligent metasurface with reconfigurable control over echo amplitude and phase. The intelligent metasurface reshapes the acoustic‐to‐EM mapping and controls the demodulated output without altering the acoustic source signal. We fabricate a prototype with programmable amplitude and phase control and partial optical transparency. Experiments demonstrate three controllable effects along the acoustic–EM transduction chain: acoustic information suppression, ambiguity generation, and hallucinatory speech output in the absence of acoustic excitation. This work provides an integrable and configurable physical‐layer paradigm for cross‐domain protection and information manipulation in cross‐domain sensing systems.

title: Reaction‐Induced Dynamic Covalent Networking Enables Adaptive Vesicles and Hierarchical Biointerfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional vesicular assemblies often face challenges in balancing mechanical robustness with structural adaptability. Here, we develop a reaction‐induced dynamic covalent networking (RIDCN) strategy that integrates vesicle construction with adaptive biointerface engineering. Through the formation of interconnected imine and boronate ester linkages, RIDCN directs the assembly of non‐amphiphilic building blocks into vesicular structures, with dynamic covalent networks serving as integral membrane frameworks. This structural integration reinforces vesicle mechanics while preserving adaptive reorganization through reversible bond exchange. Beyond individual vesicles, RIDCN enables interfacial assembly on diverse implant substrates, forming adaptive coatings with antibacterial, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic activities. These findings demonstrate the potential of RIDCN to connect vesicle construction, mechanical adaptation, and multifunctional biointerface engineering within a unified material design strategy.

title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase–free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue–like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress
abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

title: The scientific record is never finished
abstract: The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need, Science is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

title: Rising risk of deforestation in Indonesia’s pulp sector

title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

title: Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor
abstract: Light carries angular momentum in two forms: spin, associated with polarization, and orbital, associated with helical wavefronts. Whereas spin angular momentum underlies well-known atomic selection rules, the role of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in light-matter interaction continues to be discussed in the literature. In this work, we investigate OAM transfer from a vortex laser beam to a trapped-ion quantum rotor using rotational sidebands of the electric quadrupole transition of 40 Ca + . We directly observe coherent transfer of optical OAM into quantized rotation and identify distinct selection rules for different rotational sidebands. This observation provides experimental evidence for a scale-dependent separation of angular momentum transfer pathways in light-matter interactions. Further, our work elucidates the previously reported modified selection rules in trapped-ion experiments, establishing a unified framework for twisted light–matter interactions.

title: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.

title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.
