abstract: Highlights from the Science family of journals

title: Morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Modern western legal and criminal justice theories assume that punishment should deter criminalized behavior by introducing costs that reduce its expected utility, but, empirically, punishment often has weak effects on rates of crime and recidivism. Here, we hypothesize that when people are motivated to engage in criminalized behavior for moral reasons, they show diminished sensitivity to punishment. We demonstrate our hypothesis across 10 correlational, experimental, and economic game studies with participants drawn from the general population as well as participants with criminal backgrounds. Studies 1 to 3 draw on federal data of over 30,000 offenders and find that participants’ estimates of moral motives for crime predict higher recidivism while estimates of material motives predict the opposite. Studies 4 to 8 use judgment studies and find that morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment across a diversity of crime types, when motives are manipulated but actions are kept constant, persist for different types of consequences, and are unique to moral motivation. Studies 9 and 10 employ economic games and find that when players take money from others for moral reasons, they are less deterred by the imposition of fines. Implications for systems of punishment, offender psychology, and restorative justice approaches are discussed.

title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
abstract: Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

title: Coevolving gene networks underlying a phenotypic syndrome revealed via integrating comparative genomic and microevolutionary analyses
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Complex adaptive traits often comprise interacting, coevolving phenotypes that together for a syndrome that is shaped by multiple genetic loci. While using intraspecific variation is an established approach for investigating syndromes, such polymorphism typically captures only a subset of syndrome traits. Diapause, an alternative developmental pathway that evolved independently in many species to synchronize life cycles with resource availability, exemplifies this challenge. While subsets of this essential phenotype have long been studied at a single species level, the genomic basis of the full diapause syndrome remains poorly understood. This paucity of insights has fueled a long-standing debate about how life cycle synchronization evolves and whether convergent phenotypes employ shared mechanisms. Using a comparative genomic analysis spanning diverse diapause transitions in butterflies, we identified a large network of coevolving genes unique to diapausing species. The network is composed of functional modules spanning circadian regulation, metabolism, and cell cycle control. We tested whether this macroevolutionary scale network predicts microevolutionary dynamics, hypothesizing that this network is the polygenic architecture underlying the diapause syndrome. Analyses revealed that allelic variation in the diapause network is significantly enriched in signatures of local adaptation across latitudes, but only in diapausing species. Thus, we empirically show that diapause evolves through modular, coevolving gene networks, components of which impact intraspecific variation in diapause. Using this integrative perspective on a complex phenotype opens a horizon of inquiry for understanding seasonal adaptation across evolutionary scales, while demonstrating the power of integrating comparative genomics with microevolutionary dynamics to dissect complex phenotypic syndromes.

title: Cryo-EM provides insight into how the Staphylococcus aureus IsdH receptor removes hemin from the hemoglobin:haptoglobin complex
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Staphylococcus aureus
                    extracts hemin from human hemoglobin (Hb) to overcome host-imposed iron limitation. How it recovers Hb-bound hemin from the hemoglobin:haptoglobin (Hb:Hp) complex, the major circulating form of Hb outside red blood cells, remains unclear. Here, we use cryo-electron microscopy, biophysical measurements, and solution kinetics to define how the
                    S. aureus
                    IsdH surface receptor extracts hemin from Hb:Hp. A 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of Hb:Hp bound by full-length IsdH reveals that its N-terminal NEAT domain (N1) anchors it to αHb, whereas its downstream N2N3 extraction unit engages βHb to remove its hemin. The receptor engages Hb:Hp differently than isolated Hb, because N-linked glycans on haptoglobin bias the extraction unit toward βHb, sterically occluding its access to αHb while still permitting engagement by N1. Kinetic assays show that IsdH actively accelerates hemin release from Hb:Hp. Three-dimensional variability analysis indicates that this likely occurs via a dynamic interface in which receptor motions reposition the extraction unit relative to βHb, collectively supporting a model in which IsdH transiently perturbs the F-helix to promote hemin extraction. Alignment of that model with a previously determined CD163:Hb:Hp structure shows how IsdH may disrupt Hb:Hp recognition by macrophage and monocyte CD163 receptors, helping to explain how it may hinder clearance of Hb:Hp from circulation. In aggregate, these results help define the structural basis for hemin extraction from Hb:Hp and how IsdH may subvert receptor-mediated clearance of the Hb:Hp complex.

title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation
abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron–containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
abstract: Mammalian biology unfolds over time, within tissues and organs opaque to our eyes and instruments. We applied DNA Typewriter, a sequential molecular recorder, to record the cell lineage of a mouse over nearly 2 weeks of development. From one embryo, we reconstructed a time-calibrated, parsimony-supported, zygote-rooted phylogeny of 1.28 million transcriptionally profiled cells. A burst of editing unequivocally marks the daughters of the first cleavage, which serve as inline replicates. We quantified clonal dominance arising during gastrulation. Tree siblings share cell type far above chance; heterotypic siblings mark terminal differentiations. Temporal sweeps of clade co-occurrence recover a dated hierarchy of cell type couplings; imputed labels for internal nodes recapitulate known state paths. A lineage-anchored ontogeny of mammalian development, long out of reach, is coming into view.

title: Authentic structure of the CCHFV RNA–nucleoprotein complex at near-atomic resolution
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) poses a major public health threat without approved vaccines or antivirals. Its ribonucleoprotein (RNP) is essential for replication, but its native architecture and RNA packaging remain elusive. Here, we combine AI-based structural prediction with cryo–electron microscopy to resolve the native structure of the CCHFV RNP purified from CCHFV-infected cells. We report a 3.87 Å structure of a single-turn RNP, and local refinement yielded a 3.55 Å structure of two adjacent NP protomers with continuous RNA. This represents the highest-resolution authentic RNP structure reported among segmented negative-strand RNA viruses (sNSVs), and provides the structural basis for CCHFV RNP assembly. Together with mutational analyses, these findings define the molecular basis of RNA encapsidation and NP oligomerization in the native CCHFV RNP. Our findings provide a hybrid structural framework integrating AI and experimental approaches for understanding genome organization in sNSVs and offer a foundation for future antiviral development.

title: Counterions, polarization, and pore hydration relay drive ion permeation through hydrophobic pore formed by the MERS coronavirus E protein
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Hydrophobic pores are generally expected to exclude ions because the large desolvation penalty associated with ion transfer cannot be compensated within a nonpolar environment. The envelope (E) protein of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) presents a striking exception, conducting cations with high efficiency despite forming a predominantly hydrophobic pore. To resolve this apparent paradox, we combine finite-temperature string simulations with additive and polarizable force fields to determine the minimum free-energy pathways for ion permeation through the MERS E channel. The simulations reveal a cooperative permeation mechanism in which transient counterion association, localized pore hydration, and electronic polarization jointly reduce the desolvation penalty. Rather than acting as passive spectators, counterions transiently chaperone the permeating cation before dissociating within the channel, thereby lowering the energetic cost of charge desolvation while preserving net ionic conductance. Explicit electronic polarization further reshapes the pore hydration landscape and cation–
                    
                      
                        π
                      
                    
                    interactions, leading to substantially reduced free-energy barriers and a permeation mechanism that is in substantially better agreement with experiment. These results suggest that efficient ion transport through hydrophobic pores arises from the cooperative interplay between electrostatics, polarization, and hydration rather than complete pore wetting, providing both a mechanistic framework for MERS E protein function and a general physical principle for ion transport through biological and synthetic hydrophobic nanopores.

title: Lipid-induced Caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking is associated with lipid droplet growth
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Caveolae are 50 to 100 nm sized plasma membrane invaginations involved in cellular lipid uptake and lipid accumulation. Several caveolin1 and cavin1 mutations are associated with human lipodystrophy. Previous research identified caveolae proteins at lipid droplets, although their specific cellular function at lipid droplets is not understood. Here, we show that extracellular dietary lipids like oleic acid and cholesterol shift caveolae at the plasma membrane to highly spherical invaginations and induce the internalization of caveolin1. Within 3 h of lipid treatment, caveolin1 accumulates specifically to lipid droplets. Correlative fluorescence Focused Ion Beam – Scanning Electron Microscopy and split-APEX proteomics revealed that this localization occurs in the absence of intact caveolar vesicles but caveolin1 alone. Mechanistically, caveolin1 trafficking to lipid droplets is regulated by EHD2 at the plasma membrane, is dynamin independent, and proceeds via EEA1- and Rab5-positive endosomes within 1 h of oleic acid treatment. Lipid droplet accumulation of caveolin1 is independent of lysosomal activity. Functionally, caveolin1-enriched lipid droplets exhibit a significant increase in size, demonstrating that caveolin1 is critical for lipid droplet growth. Notably, the deletion of the central caveolin1 β-barrel (Cav1-F160X), a mutation identified in lipodystrophy patients, abolished caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking and lipid droplet growth. Taken together, our results show that dietary lipids trigger caveolin1 internalization and accumulation at lipid droplets and a caveolin1-dependent lipid droplet growth, thereby providing an initial mechanistic basis for the lipodystrophic phenotype associated with caveolin1 mutations.

title: Preemptive solving of future problems: Multitask Preplay in humans and machines
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Humans can pursue a near-infinite variety of tasks, but typically can only pursue a small number at the same time. We hypothesize that humans leverage experience on one task to preemptively learn solutions to other tasks that were accessible but not pursued. We formalize this idea as “Multitask Preplay”, an algorithm that replays experience on one task as the starting point for “preplay”—counterfactual simulation of an accessible but unpursued task. Preplay is used to learn a predictive representation that can support fast, adaptive task performance later on. When implemented within deep reinforcement learning, it predicts human generalization to novel tasks more accurately than traditional planning and predictive representation methods across grid-worlds and a 2D Minecraft domain. Additionally, Multitask Preplay improves an artificial agent’s ability to generalize to new environments sharing task co-occurrence structure. These findings demonstrate that Multitask Preplay is a scalable theory of human counterfactual learning and generalization; endowing artificial agents with this capacity can significantly improve their performance in challenging multitask environments.

title: Causal dynamic resonance reduces false positives in detecting causality
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Many dynamical systems in nature, such as brains and weather systems, are highly nonlinear and complex. Determining information flow among the components that make up these dynamical systems is challenging. If the components are the result of a common process or become synchronized, causality measures typically fail. We previously introduced Cross-Dynamical Delay Differential Analysis, a nonlinear method for assessing causal influence, along with a complementary approach for dynamical similarity between time series data, Dynamical Ergodicity Delay Differential Analysis. Here, we show that “Causal Dynamic Resonance (CDR)” further improves the false positive rejection rate by adding white noise to the data, without perturbing the underlying dynamical system. This is followed by a study of CDR in coupled Rössler systems, where ground truth interactions are known and in invasive intracranial electroencephalographic data from drug-resistant epilepsy patients undergoing presurgical monitoring.

title: Serine–glycine lipid homeostasis in Bacteroidota modulates membrane stability and host interactions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Lipid 1256 (L1256) is a large complex aminolipid produced by members of the phylum
                    Bacteroidota
                    that is formed by addition of a phosphatidic acid (PA) moiety to the precursor aminolipid, L654. Studies have shown that L1256 is enriched in diseased gingival tissues, linking synthesis of this aminolipid to sites of chronic inflammation. Given that PA is involved in membrane rearrangements and L654 is a known Toll-like receptor 2 ligand associated with health, we hypothesized that synthesis of L1256 could influence outer membrane vesicle (OMV) biogenesis and innate immune responses. Here, PG1647 was identified as a lipid synthase required for biosynthesis of L1256 in
                    Porphyromonas gingivalis
                    . Loss of PG1647 abolished L1256 and related minor species, while impairing membrane stress resistance and intracellular survival. PG1647 loss also increased OMV production and enhanced the proinflammatory activity of bacterial cells and OMVs. These phenotypes occurred without broad transcriptional changes, supporting lipid remodeling as a central driver. Structural and biochemical analyses supported a phospholipase D-like role for PG1647. Complementation with the
                    Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
                    homologue BT3978 restored L1256 production in
                    P. gingivalis
                    and partially rescued associated phenotypes, suggesting functional conservation among the host-associated
                    Bacteroidota
                    . Additional studies determined that many species in the phylum
                    Bacteroidota
                    carry a similar functional enzyme, further indicating the importance of this class of enzyme for
                    Bacteroidota’s
                    physiological functions. Altogether, these findings show that loss of PG1647 alters OMV biogenesis, inflammatory activity, and host-associated fitness in the endogenous oral pathogen,
                    P. gingivalis
                    , linking these phenotypic changes to PG1647-dependent aminolipid remodeling.

title: Co-translational surveillance of nascent polypeptides times circadian rhythms in Drosophila
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) ensures proteostasis by actively degrading aberrant translation intermediates on stalled ribosomes, yet its physiological role in gene regulation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that
                    Drosophila
                    circadian clocks employ RQC to sustain 24-h behavioral rhythms. RNA interference-mediated depletion of RQC components in circadian pacemaker neurons impaired free-running locomotor rhythms. In particular, the loss of
                    Caliban
                    (
                    Clbn
                    ) function in clearing 60S-associated faulty polypeptides led to weak but long-period rhythms in adult locomotor activity. These behavioral phenotypes were accompanied by delayed accumulation of the core clock protein PERIOD (PER), most evidently in pigment-dispersing factor-expressing clock neurons, and dampened structural plasticity of their axons.
                    per
                    heterozygosity exaggerated CLBN depletion-induced period lengthening, whereas overexpression of the PER-associating factor TIMELESS blunted this effect.
                    Clbn
                    deficiency in
                    Drosophila
                    S2R+ cell cultures increased the generation of prematurely terminated PER species, particularly when PER translation is high, and sensitized full-length PER to phosphorylation-dependent decay. These findings support PER as a clock-relevant RQC substrate, providing a mechanistic link between translation flux, co-translational surveillance, and circadian timekeeping.

title: Linear plasmids mediate antimicrobial resistance gene transfer between environmental bacteria and hospital-adapted enterococci
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
As animal hosts adapted to land,
                    Enterococcus
                    species diverged from a common ancestor shared with
                    Vagococcus
                    species by acquiring genes essential for survival and transmission in the exposed arid environment. In addition to their intrinsic ruggedness, human-associated enterococci now frequently exhibit multidrug resistance, largely driven by the accumulation of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) on mobile genetic elements (MGEs). However, the source of these resistance elements, their diversity in natural reservoirs, and their risks remain unclear. To investigate clinically relevant ARGs and their associated MGEs in a wastewater-impacted environment, we examined environmental vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) recovered from a polluted urban river in Hanoi, Vietnam. Whole-genome sequencing of VRE isolates revealed multidrug-resistance pELF-type linear plasmids harboring a fluoroquinolone resistance gene (
                    qrtA
                    ) encoding a major facilitator superfamily transporter. The
                    qrtA
                    gene appears to have originated on
                    Vagococcus
                    -related chromosomes and may have been mobilized by IS
                    1216E
                    -associated MGEs.
                    Vagococcus
                    genomes show strong associations between ARGs, IS
                    1216E,
                    and plasmids related to those in enterococci, and conjugation experiments demonstrated that pELF-type linear plasmids can transfer between
                    Enterococcus
                    and
                    Vagococcus
                    without major fitness costs. Comparative analysis of pELF-type linear plasmids, together with database mining, identified
                    qrtA
                    -positive clinical isolates from geographically separated regions in Asia and Europe, indicating that
                    qrtA
                    is not confined to a single local setting. These findings highlight the need for coordinated international One Health surveillance of ARG and MGE dynamics, including emerging determinants such as
                    qrtA
                    , together with interventions to limit their spread.

title: Physicochemical microenvironments within biomolecular condensates govern reaction kinetics beyond mass-action effects
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cells utilize phase separation to compartmentalize biochemical reactions within biomolecular condensates. Although these compartments can enhance reaction rates by concentrating reactants, how they modulate kinetics beyond mass-action effects remains poorly understood. Here, using spontaneous protein ligation as a model reaction, we examined how the physicochemical microenvironment within condensates modulates reaction kinetics. We systematically analyzed condensates formed by folded PRM–SH3 scaffolds and intrinsically disordered proteins (LAF, TAF, and FUS). We designed a proximity-sensitive client probe to assess excluded-volume-driven increases in effective reactant concentration. In parallel, we characterized condensate hydrophilicity and associated changes in water activity, identifying these properties as additional key kinetic determinants. Together, our findings elucidate how effective concentration and hydrophilicity jointly regulate biochemical reactions within condensates.

title: Lactate-rich tumor employs the KAT5–HIF1α axis to modulate the activity of the hypoxia pathway and facilitates tumor progression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Substantial evidence shows that hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF1α) up-regulates glycolytic enzymes and promotes lactate production, which contributes to “Warburg Effect.” Nevertheless, the impact of lactate or lactylation modification on hypoxia signaling pathways within the tumor microenvironment remains largely unclear. Here, we report that lactate can induce the upregulation of hypoxia pathway activity in a HIF1α-dependent manner. We identified that KAT5 as a lysine lactyltransferase of HIF1α and the “writer” responsible for lactylation at HIF1α K389, K460, K674, and K682, and HDAC2 as a HIF1α de-lactylase. The lactylation-deficient mutant of HIF1α (HIF1α
                    4KR
                    ) reduced HIF1α stability, along with down-regulating hypoxia-mediated angiogenesis, metastasis, apoptosis, and glycolysis. Mechanistically, the HIF1α
                    4KR
                    mutant enhances the binding of HIF1α to von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor protein (VHL), facilitating its degradation. MG149, a KAT5 inhibitor, can enhance the efficacy of anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)-based combination immunotherapy in a murine model by suppressing hypoxia pathway activity in tumor cells and potentiating the cytotoxic function of CD8
                    +
                    T cells. Clinically, lactylated HIF1α and KAT5 are up-regulated in breast cancer tissues compared with adjacent tissues. Notably, elevated levels of HIF1α lactylation and KAT5 expression were observed in resistant cancer specimens from triple-negative breast cancer patients who had undergone neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Our results indicate that the tumor lactate microenvironment promotes the formation of the tumor hypoxic microenvironment by hijacking and lactylating HIF1α, and the KAT5–HIF1α Kla axis presents a promising therapeutic target for hypoxic tumors.

title: Semiclassical study of muon-enhanced proton-$^{11}\mathrm{B}$ fusion
source: Recent Articles in Phys. Rev. C
abstract: Author(s): Hong-Yi Wang (王弘毅), Ming-Yu Chen (陈铭宇), Hao-Le Ma (马好乐), and Zhu-Fang Cui (崔著钫)Proton–boron-11 (p–11B) fusion only converts its reactants into three charged α particles, so that is an attractive aneutronic path to fusion energy, but the high Coulomb barrier of the 11B nucleus (Z = 5) keeps its reactivity low. We study a new pathway that form a muonic hydrogen atom (pμ) first, whose Bohr radius is about 200 times smaller than ordinary hydrogen, then bombard it with a 11B nucleus. We simulate the full three-body classical motion with the classical trajectory Monte Carlo method, sampling the pμ initial state from the microcanonical ground-state ensemble. From the statistical distribution of classical turning points, we compute the Coulomb-barrier tunneling probability and obtain the cross section. The results show that the μ enhances the low-energy cross section by several orders of magnitude compared with bare nuclei. Thus, if combined with intense laser fields or high-density compression, this mechanism may enable low-energy auxiliary ignition of aneutronic p–11B fusion.[Phys. Rev. C 114, 054609] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026

title: Water-energy-carbon nexus footprint of seawater desalination and transfer for industrial development: a hybrid life cycle -node-flow framework
abstract: Seawater desalination is becoming increasingly important in arid, industrializing regions, but planning assessments often consider the embodied energy of supply chains and the operational energy of water transfer separately. This study presents a hybrid life cycle and node-flow framework that combines embodied energy and carbon emissions with a spatially explicit model of pumping energy based on elevation gain and hydraulic head losses. The framework is applied to Iran's Persian Gulf Seawater Desalination and Transfer (SDT) project, which supplies 138.76 million m 3 of water annually. Two strategies are compared: Water Transfer (WT), which pumps water inland while transporting products to the coast, and Industrial Transfer (IT), which relocates industries to the coast and transports raw materials from inland areas. Rail and truck freight represent the best- and worst-case transport scenarios, respectively. Pumping-energy intensity ranges from 333.2 to 21,462.4 MWh per million m 3 , depending mainly on transfer distance and elevation. Although industrial relocation reduces long-distance pumping-energy by 99.4%, transporting raw materials offsets much of this saving. Under the grid-average electricity scenario, rail transport results in nearly unchanged total energy use (+0.9%) but reduces carbon emissions by 22.7%. With truck transport, energy use and carbon emissions increase by 121.9% and 53.8%, respectively. Under low-carbon electricity, relocation increases carbon emissions with both transport modes. Benefits also vary by industry: relocation reduces energy use at the steel site under both modes and at the pelletizing site by rail, but not at the copper sites, where raw-material requirements are substantially greater than product output. The water footprint changes only slightly (−4.4%). This framework supports integrated assessments of energy and carbon trade-offs in desalination-dependent industrial systems.

title: Spatial patterns of hybrid PV–CSP–TES configurations for green hydrogen production across Algeria
abstract: Existing studies have optimized hybrid PV–CSP plants or mapped suitable locations for solar hydrogen production, but the spatial dependence of the optimal hybrid architecture remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops a national-scale framework that couples GIS–FAHP screening with hourly PV–CSP–TES–electrolyzer simulation and site-specific NSGA-II optimization to determine how the cost-optimal system design changes across Algeria. At each meteorological location, PV capacity, CSP power-block capacity, TES duration, and solar multiple are jointly optimized for a fixed 50 MW electrolyzer, with the final configuration selected as the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) solution satisfying annual demand satisfaction (ADS) ≥ 90%. The resulting architecture varies substantially across the country: optimal PV capacity ranges from 70.03 to 168.86 MW, CSP power-block capacity from 50.00 to 92.98 MW, and solar multiple from 2.35 to 3.40, while annual hydrogen production remains comparatively stable at 7.58–7.65 kt H₂ yr −1 . Unconstrained LCOH ranges from 6.00 to 10.78 € kg −1 H₂ and narrows considerably after GIS-based deployment constraints are imposed. At Hassi R'Mel, the selected architecture combines approximately 100 MW PV, 50 MW CSP, SM = 2.80, and 16 h TES, achieving an LCOH of 6.53 € kg −1 H₂, 90.3% ADS and approximately 7.6 kt H₂ yr −1 . Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate and CSP capital cost as the strongest economic influences within the examined parameter ranges. A matched-output comparison shows that PV-only production can achieve lower LCOH when intermittency is acceptable, whereas PV–CSP–TES substantially increases electrolyzer utilization and production continuity. The results demonstrate that site-specific optimization is necessary to capture how economically preferred generation capacities and solar-field sizing adapt to local solar-resource conditions.

title: Self-Powered Actuation of Commercial UV Sensors via Single-Electrode Triboelectric Nanogenerators Using Self-Exposed MXene Nanosheets in Porous Dielectrics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have emerged as pivotal sustainable energy harvesters. However, single-electrode configurations, despite their structural simplicity and seamless circuit integration, suffer from inherently low output performance compared to double-electrode systems, primarily due to the absence of a top electrode and reduced potential difference across the dielectric layer. To overcome this limitation, we report a high-output, single-electrode TENG platform featuring a porous dielectric layer with self-exposed MXene nanosheets. By monolithically integrating this layer onto a flexible electrode via a water steaming process, we simultaneously achieve structural and interfacial modifications that promote charge accumulation and electrostatic induction. Specifically, the porous structure increases the effective contact area, while the migration and self-exposure of hydrophilic MXene nanosheets at the water–polydimethylsiloxane interfaces during droplet-templating modify the surface electrostatic properties, enhancing the triboelectric performance of the device. The resulting device delivers a remarkable peak power density of 5870 mW/m2 under hand tapping. Crucially, this superior output achieves a 24–28% faster charging rate than MXene-embedded counterparts. The practical utility of our platform is validated through the successful actuation of a commercial UV index sensor system. Operated entirely without external power, the seamless integration of this TENG with standard electronic components demonstrates a fully independent, self-sustainable power solution for practical environmental monitoring. This study provides a robust strategy to enhance energy-harvesting performance of single-electrode TENGs, thereby enabling diverse self-powered applications in next generation electronics.

title: Electron-Donation and Hydrophilicity Synergy in Side-Chain Engineered COFs: Enhanced Photocatalytic U(VI) Reduction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic U(VI) reduction is vital for radioactive wastewater treatment, yet covalent organic frameworks (COFs) face limitations in charge carrier separation and transport, with insufficient studies on functional group effects. Herein, three donor–acceptor COFs (TfBD, TfBD-CH3, and TfBD-OH) were synthesized to investigate electron-donating group modifications. Enhanced light absorption, narrowed bandgaps, increased photocurrent density, and reduced impedance were confirmed. Consequently, the reduction efficiency of U(VI) increased from 73% for TfBD to 77% for TfBD-CH3 and 91% for TfBD-OH, with stronger electron-donating ability leading to superior performance. TfBD-OH exhibited comparable removal efficiency in uranium-spiked seawater due to its synergistic effect of hydrophilicity and electron-donating groups. DFT calculations showed that TfBD-OH had the lowest adsorption energy for U(VI), while photogenerated H2O2 promoted U(VI) removal via formation of (UO2)O2·2H2O precipitates. This study demonstrates a viable strategy for side-chain-modified COFs in photocatalytic uranium enrichment.

title: Local Delivery of Astragalus Polysaccharide via Alginate Hydrogels to Inhibit Postoperative Osteosarcoma Recurrence and Metastasis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The recurrence and metastasis of osteosarcoma after surgery and chemotherapy treatments are still a clinical challenge. Astragalus polysaccharide (APS) possesses notable antitumor activity but rather low bioavailability after intravenous or oral administration. Herein, a porous composite hydrogel combined with alginate (ALG) was prepared for the efficient local delivery of APS, which demonstrated a biphasic release profile with an initial burst release in the first several hours and a sustained release in the long term. The APS/ALG-Ca2+ gel exhibited antitumor activity, specifically enhancing the inhibition of cell proliferation with an inhibition rate of 97.85 ± 0.29% within 48 h, demonstrating cytotoxicity approximately equivalent to a 5-fold dose of APS solution. The promotion of apoptosis was also shown by the increased expression of cleaved caspase-3 by ∼11-fold in vivo. Concurrently, its inhibitory effect on cell migration was validated through a Transwell assay in vitro and metastatic foci in livers and lungs in vivo (with significantly decreased expression of platelet-derived growth factor D (PDGFD) and receptor beta (PDGFRB)). Furthermore, in mouse models, it demonstrated sustained suppression of osteosarcoma recurrence following B-cell maturation in the spleen. Our findings suggested that the APS/ALG-Ca2+ gel could be a feasible local adjuvant strategy of postsurgical osteosarcoma for further preclinical evaluation.

title: Blue-Hazard Free WOLEDs with High Efficiency and Color-Rendering Index by Exciton Confinement and Energy Transfer Sensitization from Bluish-Green Emitter to Ultrathin Light-Emitting Layer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract White organic light-emitting diodes (WOLEDs) demonstrate tremendous potential as next-generation light sources. However, the simultaneous achievement of ideal white emission and high efficiency remains a significant challenge. This work proposes a solution by inserting low-mobility light-emitting layers (EMLs) on both sides of the high-mobility EML and introducing ultrathin red phosphorescent EMLs to regulate exciton distribution and energy transfer processes. The obtained WOLEDs achieve the maximum power efficiency and external quantum efficiency up to 77.1 lm W–1 and 32.2%, respectively, which maintain 52.8 lm W–1 and 29.5% at 1000 cd m–2. Concurrently, the devices exhibit color rendering index exceeding 80 within a luminance range from 1000 to 80000 cd m–2, accompanied by complete elimination of harmful blue emission. Time-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy reveals that the red emission of WOLEDs based on ultrathin red EMLs mainly originates from energy transfer through the quasi-equatorial conformer of bluish-green emitter DMAC-TRZ. This work elucidates the concealed photophysical mechanisms in WOLEDs based on ultrathin EMLs while presenting a promising strategy for energy-efficient and blue-hazard free lighting technologies.

title: Growth-Spiral Control of Defect Topology and Local Vertical Piezoresponse in Bi4Ti3O12 Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aurivillius phase materials are layered ferroelectrics with high thermal stability (>600 °C) and fatigue resistance, yet their polarization is predominantly in-plane, limiting integration into vertical device architectures relevant to future memory, data storage, and neuromorphic computing concepts. Achieving robust vertical polarization in these systems remains fundamentally challenging because of crystallographic symmetry constraints. Although defects can locally reorient polarization, deterministic control of defect topology through growth-mode engineering remains largely unexplored in layered ferroelectrics. Here, we demonstrate that precise control of nominal precursor loading and oxygen partial pressure during direct liquid injection chemical vapor deposition enables a transition in epitaxial Bi4Ti3O12 thin films from two-dimensional growth to dislocation-mediated, chiral spiral growth. This work introduces growth spirals as a controllable route to engineer defect topology and grain morphology, rather than relying on post-growth or stochastic defect formation. Atomic-resolution microscopy and piezoresponse force microscopy reveal that chiral spiral-mediated morphologies exhibit a 135% higher local vertical piezoresponse amplitude and a reduced local vertical switching bias from ±20 to ±5 V compared with two-dimensional films. High-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) displacement mapping and density functional theory indicate that out-of-phase boundary defect-associated local structural distortions modify local symmetry, bonding, and strain in a manner consistent with an enhanced out-of-plane polarization component and local vertical electromechanical response. These results establish spiral-driven defect topology as a growth-controlled pathway for tuning the local vertical piezoresponse in layered ferroelectrics and suggest a broadly applicable design principle for future low-power vertical ferroelectric oxide devices.

title: Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

Strategic autonomy and the energy transition: Rethinking Europe's geopolitical alignment
abstract: Europe's geopolitical alignment, its enduring deference to a US-led unipolar order, has come at the expense of its energy security and its ability to carry out the energy transition. This paper argues that greater strategic autonomy, the capacity and willingness to make economic and foreign policy decisions according to its own interests, would allow Europe to pursue both goals more effectively. It develops this argument in four parts. First, it characterises Europe's geopolitical alignment as a pattern of deference to US strategic priorities, sustained despite mounting costs to Europe's material interests, its standing and the multilateral order it claims to uphold. Second, it traces how this alignment shaped Europe's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contributing to a partly self-inflicted energy crisis followed by an abrupt and costly pivot to American liquefied natural gas that failed to resolve Europe's energy dependency. Third, it argues that on the energy transition Europe's interests are more closely aligned with Beijing's than with Washington's, although closer engagement deepens its dependence on Chinese clean technologies and critical raw materials. Europe should manage this trade-off by maintaining its de-risking approach and extending it to all its strategic dependencies, including those on the US. Finally, it argues that Europe will be unable to recalibrate its alignment and exercise strategic autonomy without building up its industrial and technological capacities and increasing its investment. Europe's choices will help determine the pace of the global energy transition, and with it, the world's chances of meeting its climate goals.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

title: Quantitative Steric Hindrance to Determine Pressure-Induced Emission Harvesting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pressure engineering enables distinctive pressure-induced emission (PIE) and piezochromism in halide perovskites, yet structural reversibility generally prevents ambient condition retention of high-pressure metastable states (HPMS), limiting their practical optoelectronic applications. This perspective compares PIE retention behavior across all-inorganic, aliphatic-cation, and aromatic-cation hybrid halide perovskites. Insufficient steric hindrance yields fully reversible responses in inorganic and aliphatic systems, whereas rigid aromatic cations elevate phase-transition barriers and kinetically trap HPMS after decompression. The steric-effect index (SEI, critical threshold 2.3) quantitatively distinguishes reversible systems from those capable of HPMS retention, establishing a link between cation molecular geometry and PIE persistence. We highlight outstanding quantitative structure–property challenges and outline future research directions, including machine-learning-guided screening, advanced high-pressure characterization, and new strategies for metastable-state stabilization. Extending PIE to phosphorescent and chiral luminescence further expands opportunities for applications in optical anticounterfeiting, information storage, sensing, and display technologies.

abstract: Abstract Heterojunction catalysts have been demonstrated to promote the oxidative degradation of plastics in conjunction with the production of clean hydrogen. However, their practical application is still hampered by inherent drawbacks, including inadequate charge separation and sluggish surface reaction kinetics. Herein, we report an S-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst CdS/CuS-graphdiyne (NCSCG), consisting of N-doped CdS (NCS), CuS, and graphdiyne (GDY) that can produce 1081 μmol of hydrogen within 5 h, which is nearly 5 times that of single NCS. Under the same conditions, NCSCG selectively photoreformed microplastic polylactic acid (PLA) into pyruvic acid (PA) and hydrogen, achieving a hydrogen production of 1029 μmol. In a square-meter-level photocatalytic device, it can generate 379,000 μmol of hydrogen. Mechanistic investigations reveal that N doping modulates the d-band center of CdS and facilitates photogenerated electrons from GDY to NCS, whereas CuS supplies extra electrons to NCS, thus effectively suppressing photogenerated charge recombination. By virtue of this synergistic effect, both the surface reaction kinetics and the hydrogen production performance of the photocatalytic system are effectively improved. This study shows that coupling d-band center modulation with an S-scheme heterojunction significantly enhances photocatalytic performance, offering a practical pathway to scalable photocatalytic hydrogen production and PLA waste valorization.

title: Enantioselective Radical Hydrosilylation of Electron‐Deficient Alkenes Enabled by Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalytic enantioselective hydrosilylation of electron‐deficient alkenes remains an outstanding challenge due to difficulties in simultaneously controlling chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Herein, we report a general and practical strategy enabling the first enantioselective radical hydrosilylation of α,β‐unsaturated esters via metallaphotoredox catalysis. This approach integrates photocatalytically generated bromine radical‐facilitated hydrogen atom transfer to convert hydrosilanes into silyl radicals with a chiral nickel catalyst that stabilizes carbon‐centered radical intermediates and directs asymmetric protonation. The method circumvents alkene coordination and migratory insertion steps, and effectively overrides racemic background radical addition. By decoupling Si─C bond formation from the enantioselectivity‐determining step, it accommodates a broad substrate scope. The redox‐neutral, fully atom‐economical protocol proceeds under mild conditions without stoichiometric organometallic reagents or external oxidants/reductants, delivering β‐silylated carbonyl compounds with high chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Furthermore, the strategy extends to enantioselective hydrogermylation and is amenable to gram‐scale synthesis. This work provides a conceptually distinct blueprint for enantioselective hydrosilylation and establishes a mechanistic rationale for controlling enantioselectivity in radical conjugate addition.

title: MOF-on-MOF Heterojunction for Aerobic Photocatalytic Uranium Extraction from Seawater
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic uranium reduction provides an alternative strategy for seawater uranium extraction, yet it remains challenging due to the high carbonate content and aerobic conditions. In this work, a MOF-on-MOF (MOM) heterostructure was constructed by growing NH2-MIL-125(Ti) (M125) onto MIL-101(Cr) (M101) via a hydrothermal method. The composite integrates the excellent U(VI) adsorption capacity of M101 with the superior photoelectric properties and oxygen activation ability of M125. In air atmosphere, MOM achieved over 95% U(VI) removal from carbonate-containing solution within 2 h under light irradiation, which is significantly higher than that of M101 and M125. 90.1% of uranium was recovered from uranium-spiked seawater, and 87.8% of uranium was extracted from real seawater using MOM. In situ irradiated XPS and KPFM confirmed electron transfer from M101 to M125 in the MOM heterojunction. MOM facilitates the generation of superoxide radicals (·O2–), which play a key role in reducing U(VI) to insoluble U(IV). This work presents a synergistic MOF-on-MOF design strategy for efficient photocatalytic uranium extraction under aerobic conditions.

title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Upon infection, arteriviruses, coronaviruses, and other nidoviruses transform endoplasmic reticulum membranes into viral replication organelles. These include large numbers of double-membrane vesicles (DMVs) whose interior is considered the primary site of viral RNA synthesis. Early studies characterized nidovirus DMVs as sealed compartments, leaving it unclear how newly synthesized viral RNA could be exported to the cytosol. The discovery of DMV-spanning pore complexes in coronavirus-infected cells provided a plausible solution for this topological challenge. However, their structural organization, functional features, and evolutionary conservation across the nidovirus order, have remained unclear. Here, we investigate the macromolecular architecture of DMVs induced by two prototypic arteriviruses using cellular cryo-electron tomography. Despite the substantial evolutionary distance separating arteriviruses and coronaviruses, we observe DMV-spanning pore complexes with striking structural similarities to those previously described in coronaviruses. These pores may facilitate both export and encapsidation of viral RNA. In the absence of viral RNA synthesis, ectopic expression of the arterivirus transmembrane nonstructural proteins nsp2 and nsp3 suffices to induce the formation of pore-containing DMVs. Together, our findings reveal the conservation of key structural features of DMV pores across two distantly related nidovirus families and support a central role for these pores in nidovirus replication.

title: σ-complex stabilization shapes enzymatic C-glycosylation and restricts the scope of natural C-glycosides
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: C-glycosides are valuable compounds containing hydrolytically stable C-C bonds, yet their scarcity in nature and synthetic complexity limit their availability. Enzymes offer a sustainable route to C-glycosides, but few are known to display C-glycosylation activity and their mechanism remains unclear. Here, we study the intricacies of the maize C-glycosyltransferase ZmUGT708A6 using X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and atomistic simulations. Structural and dynamical analyses reveal two flexible gates that control substrate access and reactive conformations. Combined Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics simulations and mutational data support a stepwise SEAr mechanism for C-glycosylation of neutral phloretin, mediated by the catalytic His-Asp dyad and involving a high-energy σ-complex that stabilizes through a water-mediated proton transfer. Complementary pH- and substrate-activity experiments, together with Quantum Mechanics calculations, indicate that substrate hydroxylation patterns, protonation states, and σ-complex energetics restrict the scope of C-glycosides. Our results provide a coherent mechanistic framework that reconciles experimental observations across diverse conditions and advances our understanding of enzymatic C-glycosylation.

title: A renewable autologous biomaterial for reprogramming cellular metabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Autologous blood-derived products are attractive for tissue repair because they are biocompatible, renewable and readily accessible, but their liquid form limits local retention and provides little structural support. Here we show that autologous serum can be transformed into an injectable hydrogel microsphere biomaterial using gas-shearing microfluidics combined with ionic and fibrin-based enzymatic crosslinking. Reconstruction of the fibrin network improves structural support, interfacial lubrication and local retention of serum-derived factors. Compared with citrate-anticoagulated PRP, anticoagulant-free autologous serum better preserves chondrocyte metabolic adaptation under hypoxic inflammatory conditions. Multi-omics analyses further indicate enhanced chondrocyte proliferation, migration and matrix maintenance, together with modulation of hypoxia-responsive metabolic pathways. In osteoarthritis models, the microspheres promote cartilage repair and reduce disease progression. These findings establish a renewable autologous serum biomaterial platform that integrates biochemical and mechanical functions and may support personalized regenerative therapies.

title: Environmental toxicant-induced epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming of transposable elements
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) are mobile DNA sequences that constitute a significant portion of mammalian genomes and are generally epigenetically silenced, yet can regulate gene expression and chromatin architecture. Their roles under environmental exposure remain unclear. Here, we integrated 351 multi-omic datasets from adult mouse liver following early-life exposure to arsenic, lead, bisphenol A, tributyltin, di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate, tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin, and particulate matter less than 2.5 micrometers. Early-life toxicant exposure altered chromatin accessibility and expression of TEs in later life, revealing exposure-specific and sex-dependent responses. Most differentially accessible TEs located in non-coding regions. Genes associated with Long Interspersed Nuclear Elements (LINEs) were enriched in metabolic pathways, while long terminal repeat elements, particularly the ORR1E subfamily, were associated with immune-related genes. We also identified 164 TE-gene chimeric transcripts with TE-derived transcription start sites, highlighting TE-contributed transcriptional plasticity. Our findings depict a landscape of TE response to early-life toxicant exposures in mouse liver.

title: VHSeek: biology foundation model-based virus representations revealing virus host associations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Virus-host association prediction is fundamental to virus-related disease control and phage therapy, yet many existing tools require candidate-host genome sequences, which may be unavailable for some eukaryotic hosts or impractical to search at the scale of large virome studies. We present VHSeek, a supervised virus-host association predictor that integrates DNA- and protein-derived viral representations. VHSeek combines nucleotide representations from AIDO.DNA and protein representations from ESM2 to learn virus-host association patterns, and then transfers predictions through known host taxonomies from lower to higher ranks. During inference, VHSeek uses viral sequence data and known host taxonomies, without host sequence data. Compared with iPHoP, the state-of-the-art baseline evaluated in this study, VHSeek improves genus-level maximum F1 score (Fmax), Top-1 accuracy, and area under the precision–recall curve (AUPR) by 12%, 19%, and 27%, respectively. Confidence thresholding enables abstention and reduces false discoveries. On the processed IMG/VR v4.1 metagenomic collection, VHSeek expands effective host coverage from 36.5% to 64.5% using a validation-calibrated confidence threshold. VHSeek prioritizes candidate viruses and reservoir hosts with potential human health impacts, including multi-host hypotheses in which one virus may be associated with humans and additional hosts (e.g., Saboya virus with Homo sapiens and Culicidae) not currently captured in the dataset.

title: Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dysfunctional CD4 + T helper (Th) cell differentiation and migration, along with bone marrow (BM) myeloid hematopoietic responses, contribute to the progression of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, yet the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we perform single-cell transcriptomics of BM, cervical draining lymph nodes, and retinas in a mouse model of experimental autoimmune uveitis to comprehensively profile T-cell immune dynamics. We find that Wnk1 upregulation promotes expansion, differentiation, and migration of pro-inflammatory Th1 and Th17 cells by activating the c-Myc/glycolysis pathway. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of Wnk1 reduces ocular inflammation, T-cell chemotaxis, and trafficking to BM and retina, accompanied by reduced BM-derived neutrophils and monocytes and fewer myeloid cells in draining lymph nodes and retina. In Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada patients, Wnk1 is elevated in CD4 + T cells, and its inhibition impairs their proliferation and effector functions. Collectively, our data implicate Wnk1 as a key regulator of CD4 + T-cell behavior and inter-organ immune communication.

title: SMC5/6 safeguards chromatin compartments and TAD boundaries for genome stability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: SMC5/6, a member of the Structural Maintenance of Chromosomes family, coordinates 3D genome organization, chromatin states, and transcriptional regulation, yet its role in higher-order chromatin architecture remains poorly defined. Here, we investigate the impact of conditional SMC5 depletion in human B lymphoblastoid cells. Hi-C analyses reveal global rewiring of chromatin interactions, with increased long-range and reduced short-range contacts, leading to altered large-scale chromosome organization. SMC5 loss induces changes in 3D genome compartmentalization affecting ~2% of the genome and is accompanied by transcriptional upregulation of inflammatory and cancer-associated gene programs. SMC5 depletion also promotes double-strand break accumulation, preferentially in active compartments and following gene expression levels. However, regions undergoing architectural reorganization display comparatively fewer breaks, indicating that chromatin changes are not driven by DNA damage. Together, our findings establish SMC5/6 as a key regulator of chromatin compartmentalization and TAD boundary integrity, linking 3D genome organization to transcriptional control and genome stability.

title: Combinatorial mutagenesis of N-terminal sequences reveals expanded stability determinants of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although penultimate residues near the N-terminus are known to influence protein stability, their exact contributions in prokaryotes are not well understood. Here, we utilize combinatorial mutagenesis, cell sorting, and next generation sequencing to perform the deepest sequence coverage screen of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway of proteolysis. Our results reinforce the known influence of canonically destabilizing P1 F/L/Y/W/R/K while revealing unexpected effects from P2 residue identities that influence protein stability comparably to P1 identity, such as for P2 Pro (stabilizing), Gly (stabilizing), or Gln (destabilizing). For low stability sequences without P1 F/L/Y/W/R/K, we identify motifs rich in P1 Cys paired with bulky and negatively charged P2-P5 residues. Furthermore, additive stability effects were observed for motifs rich in bulky (destabilizing), acidic (stabilizing), and flexible Gly/Ser (stabilizing) residues. We train a machine learning model to predict the stability of N-terminal sequences, including motifs that break expected stability rules. We find that these data-driven predictions of P2 identity contributions quantitatively correlate with binding energies predicted from computational docking of peptides to N-recognin ClpS. Our work expands the stability determinants of the N-degron pathway with unprecedented granularity, serving as a resource for N-degron identification, understanding, and design.

title: Soybean Pb encodes a WD40 protein regulating pubescence tip morphology and seed size during domestication
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The classical soybean Pb locus controls pubescence tip morphology, with sharp (Pb/-) and blunt (pb/pb) types. It associates with insect resistance and experiences strong negative selection during domestication, yet the causal gene remains unknown, leaving unclear whether Pb directly confers insect resistance and the selective mechanism. Here, we report the cloning of Pb, which encodes a seven-WD40-repeat protein. A 4.88-kb deletion in the pb allele causes premature translation termination. Transgenic Pb soybeans with sharp pubescence tips show unchanged antibiosis and antixenosis against leaf-chewing insects compared with blunt-tip wild-type plants, demonstrating pubescence tip morphology alone does not confer insect resistance. The Pb gene reduces seed size, likely explaining its near disappearance in modern cultivars. Pb promotes assembly and activity of the GmLEC1a/GmNF-YC2/GmbZIP67 complex to regulate seed development. These findings resolve long-standing questions about the Pb locus and advance our understanding of soybean domestication.

title: A Room‐Temperature Fluorescent‐Free Imidazol‐2‐Ylidene: A Versatile Platform for Fluorophore Diversification
abstract: ABSTRACT N ‐Heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) have become key ligands in luminescent transition‐metal complexes, yet the intrinsic photophysical properties of free NHCs remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of the first isolable free imidazol‐2‐ylidene exhibiting room‐temperature fluorescence in both solution and solid states, through the incorporation of a tetrahedral boron moiety into the backbone of the emblematic 1,3‐dimesityl‐2 H ‐imidazol‐2‐ylidene (IMes) scaffold. Theoretical calculations reveal direct involvement of the carbene center in the lowest singlet excited state and therefore in the emission process. Exploiting the specific reactivity of the carbene center, conversion into the corresponding borane, urea, thiourea, and selenourea adducts enables systematic modulation of the emission wavelength, quantum yield, and photostability. These combined experimental and theoretical results establish free conventional NHCs as a previously unrecognized class of intrinsically emissive organic molecules and identify carbene molecular engineering as a viable strategy for functional luminophores.

title: Constructing Dynamic Interfacial Hydration Network Channel for Efficient Co‑Transport of OH − and H 2 in Water‑Electrolysis Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient mass transport at the electrode–electrolyte interface of anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) is fundamentally constrained by antagonistic hydration requirements. Drawing inspiration from biological channels that mediate hydrophilic yet non‐retentive transport, we designed a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable sulfone densities as synthetic nanochannels. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the sulfone moiety (O═S═O) established weak, labile hydrogen bonds with water, engendering a highly dynamic hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique hydration environment established a surface‐wetting yet bulk‐open state within the COF nanochannels, wherein a dynamic interfacial hydration network channel was maintained within the pores for efficient OH − conduction, while the bulk pore volume remained non‐flooded for unobstructed H 2 evacuation. When incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer, the sulfone‐rich 2S‐COF delivers a current density of 10.30 A cm −2 at 2.0 V under industrially relevant conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C), representing a 48% enhancement over the COF‐free electrode. This work establishes a bio‐inspired strategy for molecular‐level control of interfacial hydration, providing a generalizable platform for designing high‐performance electrochemical interfaces that require concurrent ion and gas management.

title: Regiospecific Sila‐Matteson Homologative Arylation of Biased ( N ‐Oxide) Azines
abstract: ABSTRACT The judicious selection of silicon—as a Lewis acid—able to generate penta‐ and hexavalent hypercoordinated ate complexes is herein presented as a strategy to realize conceptually novel homologative arylations. Chemically stable aryl‐ equipped C1‐silanes, conveniently activated with the same biased ( N‐ oxide) substrate in the presence of fluoride, furnish—upon fine‐tuning of consecutive [1,2]‐transposition events—benzyl‐like nucleophilic elements which are precisely transferred at the C2‐position of azines. These benzyl synthons originate from combining an aryl residue and the homologating methylene fragment. The regioselective logic is levered on the unique capability of silicon to undergo two controllable expansive‐contractive modifications of its coordinative sphere. Compared to single rearrangements accomplished with labile C1‐donors on boron manifolds—retained in the final products (Matteson‐like)—the silicon approach directly gathers heteroatom‐free azines, thus documenting high versatility for rapid and predictable functionalization.

title: Concentration‐Driven Solvation Reorganization Featuring Viologen Clustering Enables Air‐Tolerant Aqueous Organic Redox Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Viologen derivatives are promising anolytes in aqueous organic redox‐flow batteries (AORFBs), but long‐term stability under ambient air remains challenging. Using 1,1′‐bis[3‐(trimethylammonio)propyl]‐4,4′‐bipyridinium tetrachloride (BVCl 4 ), we show through physicochemical characterization and molecular dynamics simulations that increasing BV concentration beyond a critical threshold induces a solvation transition characterized by viologen clustering. Controlled O 2 exposure of bulk‐electrolyzed BV 4+ /BV 3+• solutions using a carbon felt electrode, together with air‐exposed AORFB full‐cell cycling, shows that BV is converted to redox‐inactive byproducts via OH–/reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by BV 3+• ‐O 2 galvanic reactions and electrode‐driven hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The degradation is suppressed in a nonmonotonic manner governed by the solvation‐transition threshold. We suggest that the enhanced air tolerance of concentrated BV electrolytes arises from this solvation reorganization, associated with viologen‐clustering‐induced steric shielding against O 2 /OH − /ROS attack and restricted BV hydration that limits Grotthuss‐type OH − transport to reactive BV sites. Additionally, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance measurements at an Au electrode directly visualize BV 2+ as the most degradation‐prone state, forming redox‐inactive deposits through reactions with OH − /ROS generated locally by HER and oxygen reduction reaction; this pathway is strongly attenuated once electrolyte solvation reorganizes. Voltammetry at an Au ultramicroelectrode further reveals that solvation‐transition‐driven clustering suppresses BV 3+• disproportionation.

title: Disaccharide production in marine cold seeps links dissolved organic carbon to anaerobic oxidation of methane
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) has been proposed as a source of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) at marine cold seeps, but the underlying molecular mechanism for its production remains unknown. Here we demonstrate a previously unrecognized link between AOM and porewater DOC by analyzing disaccharides in sediment and porewaters from a methane-charged cold seep in Astoria Canyon (Oregon, USA). In the AOM zone, sediments contain up to 17.7 mg L−1 trehalose with δ13C values as low as −78‰, and porewaters contain up to 1 mg L−1 sucrose with δ13C values as low as −66‰, representing 4.6% of DOC. Stable isotope probing experiments reveal AOM-dependent biosynthesis of trehalose and sucrose, and both disaccharides turn over faster than diagnostic lipids, suggesting that these compounds serve as biomarkers for active AOM. Accordingly, disaccharides mediate a relationship that may sustain microbial food webs and influence carbon cycling in methane-rich marine sediments.

title: A framework-driven pathway to dehydration embrittlement in gypsum fault gouge
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mineral dehydration can alter the mechanics and hydraulics of fault zones and affects even plate boundaries, yet direct observations of how mineral replacement reorganises the architecture of a shearing fault gouge remain limited. Here, we combine a direct shear experiment with time-resolved synchrotron-based microtomography (4DSμCT) and digital volume correlation (DVC) to track shear deformation during the transformation of gypsum to its hemihydrate. The dehydration reaction progressively reorganises the load-bearing grain framework during shear, producing a transition from distributed granular deformation of gypsum gouge to localised brittle faulting of hemihydrate. By direct correlation between evolving microstructures and macroscopic mechanical and hydraulic behaviour, our results show that dehydration can induce a rheological transition, driving strengthening, embrittlement, and shear localisation even under drained conditions. Framework reorganisation therefore provides a direct pathway by which dehydration reactions may promote instability in fault gouges, complementing models that attribute dehydration embrittlement primarily to transient pore-pressure increases.

title: Orbital spectroscopy links dust source composition to atmospheric acidity and nitrate
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mineral dust affects atmospheric chemistry, air quality, and climate, yet its impacts remain uncertain because its mineral composition is poorly constrained. Here we combine NASA EMIT orbital imaging spectroscopy with a satellite-constrained global chemistry model to quantify how source-resolved calcite variability alters aerosol chemistry and optical properties. EMIT-derived calcite improves agreement with airborne observations and reveals contrasts in dust alkalinity. Compared with globally averaged calcite, source-resolved calcite shifts regional annual mean aerosol pH by -0.6 to +0.5 units, with local changes exceeding 1 pH unit across substantial areas of the most affected dust-influenced regions, reaching -4 to +3 units in limited areas. These acidity changes reorganize secondary inorganic aerosol formation, nitrate partitioning, and extreme nitrate events, particularly where dust interacts with anthropogenic pollution. In contrast, calcite-driven secondary-aerosol radiative effects are small relative to those caused by spatial variations in iron-oxide absorption. These results show that calcite variability strongly modulates heterogeneous chemistry, whereas iron oxides dominate radiative impacts.

title: Linking human sources to antibiotic resistance genes in global surface waters
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global public health threat driven by antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Yet global human ARG generation, environmental discharges and surface-water abundances remain poorly characterized, and their linkages remain unclear, particularly at gene-specific absolute abundances, given differences in antibiotic and pathogen associations among ARGs. Here, we compiled 464 absolute abundance measurement data of five key ARGs (qnrS, ermB, tetA, tetM, and sul1) and intI1 in wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influent covering 30 countries, and combined these data with machine learning, a WWTP removal framework and a spatially explicit dilution model to estimate these metrics. Per capita generation was highest in Africa, whereas total generation and discharges were greatest in Asia; surface-water hotspots clustered in water-scarce regions, highlighting hydrological constraints alongside discharge intensity. Raising WWTP coverage in below-average countries to the global mean and high-income standards could increase global removal from 12–29% to 53–60% and 72–76%, respectively.
