These findings quantitatively link human ARG sources to surface-water abundances, providing a foundation for surveillance and intervention to curb ARG dissemination.

title: Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Whether the recent poleward migration of tropical cyclones (TCs) reflects anthropogenic warming or natural variability remains unresolved. Here, we use paleoclimate evidence to reconstruct TC migration across the western North Pacific (WNP) and North Atlantic (NA) during the natural-forcing-dominated Medieval Warm Period (MWP, ~1000–1300 CE). We integrate a paleo-TC record from the WNP generated in this study with existing records to produce a basin-scale reconstruction of TC migration across the two major TC basins. We show that TC migration during the MWP was strongly basin dependent, with a poleward shift in the WNP but an equatorward shift in the NA, driven by differences in sea surface temperature forcing between the two basins. This contrasting behavior indicates that internal variability can drive opposing migration responses across basins under quasi‑equilibrium conditions. In contrast, recent decades show a synchronous poleward shift in both basins. We suggest that the modern basin-wide coherence reflects increasingly dominant anthropogenic forcing that overwhelms natural, regionally specific feedbacks. Our results provide a new benchmark for attributing observed TC migration and constraining future projections of TC risk.

title: Amphiphilic Interface‐Mediated Dual‐Domain Architecture Enhances Phosphatase‐Like Activity for Plastic Additives Assay
abstract: ABSTRACT Plastics are ubiquitous, and their performance depends on phosphate ester additives used as plasticizers and flame retardants. Leaching of these additives causes environmental persistence and biotoxicity, demanding efficient detection. To overcome the polarity mismatch in detecting plastic additives, we developed amphiphilic F127‐modified Pt with Pt‐OH sites (Pt‐OH/F) for colorimetric detection of mixed plastic additives. Pt‐OH/F outperforms alkaline phosphatase and works directly in water, with catalytic efficiency 2–6 orders of magnitude higher than reported nanozymes. The integration of F127 with Pt‐OH sites creates a functionally distinct dual‐domain architecture composed of an amphiphilic enrichment domain and a catalytic domain, thereby overcoming the polarity restriction of natural phosphatases. Within this architecture, the spatial separation of adsorption sites from catalytic sites prevents competitive occupancy and enhances catalytic activity. Finally, the developed nanozymes can achieve simultaneous qualitative and quantitative detection of leached plastic additives in real samples, showing the potential for on‐site analysis of plastic waste.

title: Safranine T‐Derived Activable Photosensitizer to Synergistically Regulate the RSS/ROS Dynamic Equilibrium for Boosted Photosensitization
abstract: ABSTRACT Photodynamic therapy (PDT) eliminates lesions like tumors via reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐mediated oxidative damage. However, tumors overexpress reactive sulfur species (RSS) that scavenge cytotoxic ROS, endowing cancer cells with strong antioxidant resistance and weakening PDT efficacy. We fabricated a biosafe, readily available activatable photosensitizer ST‐DNBS based on safranine T (ST). ST‐DNBS selectively consumes RSS overexpressed in tumors and recovers photochemically active ST to produce massive ROS. For example, 6 µM ST‑DNBS depletes substantial glutathione (GSH), leading to a marked reduction in the characteristic absorbance of TNB 2− (5‐thio‐2‐nitrobenzoate dianion) at 412 nm in the DTNB (Ellman's reagent) assay relative to the control; ROS produced after 24 s of irradiation causes a 6.2‐fold decrease in the UV absorbance of 1,3‐diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF). Tumor‐activatable ST‐DNBS depletes intracellular RSS to collapse tumor antioxidant systems, blocking ROS clearance and boosting intracellular ROS buildup. This RSS/ROS redox balance remodeling greatly enhances photodynamic activity, achieving a 90% tumor inhibition rate. Our RSS‐scavenging, tumor‐activated photosensitizer offers a practical strategy to overcome tumor antioxidant barriers and improve PDT antitumor performance.

title: Bidirectional Sulfur Redox Regulation Enabling Ultra‐Stable High‐Sulfur‐Loading All‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐sulfur batteries are promising for high‐energy storage but are limited by sluggish sulfur redox and poor cycling stability. Herein, we design a new amorphous‐crystalline Li 6.05 P 0.95 Nb 0.05 S 5 Cl 0.8 I 0.2 electrolyte that reconstructs interfacial Li + transport and enables bidirectional regulation of sulfur redox. The amorphous structure improves solid‐solid contact and creates additional continuous Li + pathways around sulfur, while the crystal framework maintains fast Li + ion‐conducting channels. During the discharge, we further uncover an Nb reduction mechanism in which Nb 4+ is reduced to Nb 3+ , generating Li‐rich sites that promote Li 2 S nucleation and sulfur reduction. During the charge, I − is oxidized to I 2 , which acts as the redox mediator for Li 2 S oxidation, while I 3 − formation helps stabilize unconsumed I 2 . This bidirectional regulation enables 84.2% sulfur utilization at a high sulfur loading of 6 mg cm − 2 and retains 736 mAh g − 1 with 93.1% capacity retention after 1500 cycles at 0.5 C. These findings provide a mechanistic strategy for high‐sulfur‐loading all‐solid‐state Li‐S batteries.

title: A genome-wide imaging screen reveals epigenetic and mechanistic partitioning of lamina-associated chromatin
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The nuclear periphery is a near-universal site of heterochromatin organization, where lamina-associated domains (LADs) play a crucial role in transcriptional repression and genome stability. Yet the molecular mechanisms that tether LADs in human cells have remained elusive. Here, we overcome this barrier by performing the first genome-wide, imaging-based siRNA screen of LAD positioning, identifying more than 100 genes required for perinuclear localization. We isolate a striking enrichment of RNA-binding proteins, with hnRNPK emerging as a factor required for the positioning of nearly two-thirds of LADs in the human genome. Its loss drives large-scale LAD detachment from the nuclear periphery without altering heterochromatin states or lamina components, but induces transcriptional dysregulation within these domains. Strikingly, hnRNPK-sensitive LADs are uniquely enriched for H3K27me3, distinguishing them from H3K9me3-enriched insensitive LADs. Together, these findings demonstrate that LADs comprise epigenetically distinct subclasses governed by distinct regulatory pathways and establish a framework for systematically mapping genetic control of nuclear architecture.

title: PCET beyond p K a : Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxidative multisite proton‐coupled electron transfer (MS‐PCET) reactions have emerged as a promising tool for the activation of strong O─H bonds in (cyclo)alkanols. However, these methods often require the use of e‐rich arene‐containing derivatives ( para ‐methoxyphenyl (PMP), etc.) — a factor that greatly restricts their broader applicability. In this study, we report the successful implementation of targeted modulation of the base partner in photocatalytic cascade reactions of cyclic alcohols, unlocking previously rather inaccessible, nonactivated substrates. This approach successfully bypasses the prevalent limitations of ring‐opening transformations of cycloalkanols by disaggregation of the bulk alcohol and strategic base selection. As a result, we here demonstrate an operationally simple and widely applicable protocol for the redox‐neutral transformations of cycloalkanols into terminally C(sp 3 )‐C(sp 3 )‐coupled, functionalized open‐chain products. NMR‐based mechanistic studies, comprising in‐depth H‐bond analysis as well as DOSY and ROESY experiments, have elucidated the previously unrecognized crucial role of substrate disaggregation in this multisite PCET, along with (pyridine) base effects surpassing typical p K a ‐related and/or steric effects. Ultimately, our insights, for the first time, reveal the critical importance of the aggregation state and the design of productive alcohol‐base pre‐organization beyond p K a and enabled us to successfully pioneer remote alkylative Giese‐type C─C‐bond formations of previously challenging alkyl‐substituted cycloalkanols.

title: A protein repeat interruption rule governs Nebulin stability and explains in-frame NEB mutations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nemaline myopathy is a rare congenital muscle disease associated with thin filament disruption that is currently without treatment. Biallelic mutations in Nebulin are the most common cause of nemaline myopathy. Nebulin encodes a giant protein with a primary function of establishing thin filament length. Nebulin protein has a large central region composed of a series of thin filament binding super repeats. Many Nebulin mutations are small in-frame deletions within individual super repeats. Why these deletions cause disease remains unclear. To study this, we generated a series of zebrafish lines, including ones carrying in-frame partial super repeat deletions and ones harboring complete/intact super repeat deletions. Partial super repeat deletions destabilize and reduce Nebulin protein, resulting in severe phenotypes and early death. Conversely, complete super repeat deletions preserve Nebulin stability and expression, and induce no overt phenotypes. Our work provides mechanistic insights and informs future therapeutic approaches for Nebulin-related Nemaline myopathy.

title: ER-associated biogenesis of PINK1 preprotein for neuronal mitophagy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Given the large size of neurons, local maintenance of mitochondria is crucial to counteract insults to this organelle in axons and dendrites. The Parkinson-related mitochondrial kinase PINK1 plays a central role in mitochondrial quality control, which in neurons requires the transport of Pink1 mRNA by mitochondrial hitch-hiking. However, how and where PINK1 is locally translated and processed has remained unclear. Using live-cell imaging, we trace local PINK1 translation sites and preprotein dynamics, revealing a concerted interplay between mitochondria and the ER, with endolysosomes frequently localized adjacent to the site of translation. Upon metabolically regulated untethering from mitochondria, Pink1 mRNA relocates to ribosomes in proximity to the ER and endolysosomes for translation of the PINK1 preprotein. The ER chaperone DNAJB6 shields the PINK1 preprotein in transit to mitochondria, following the post-translational ER-SURF pathway. Consequently, loss of DNAJB6 leads to persistent ER/endolysosome-associated PINK1 precursor stores and failure of mitophagy upon mitochondrial damage. Our findings reveal that neuronal PINK1 protein translation switches between mitochondrially anchored co-translational and ER-associated post-translational import states, with functional implications for mitochondrial quality control.

title: Tracking local chemomechanics in graphite–silicon composite electrodes
abstract: Operando 4D imaging reveals how local ionic pathways govern activity in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
abstract: Particle-resolved 4D nano-tomography identifies fast ionic transport pathways as key regulators of electrochemical activity and reversibility in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

title: Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
abstract: A bilayer meta-atom structure engineers the antireflective capabilities of the metasurface, without affecting its full 0–2π transmission phase coverage.

title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
abstract: Mixed-matrix membranes promise to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, yet poor compatibility between the two limits their performance. New research shows that tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings, producing improved membranes for carbon capture.

title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
abstract:
Abstract
                  Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. This enables a system-wide comparison of environmental impacts and resource requirements of global final energy provision from 2020 to 2100. We find that deep decarbonization delivers substantial cobenefits for human health and ecosystem quality, but does not systematically reduce pressures on land, water or mineral resource extraction. For metals central to electrification, climate change mitigation ambition primarily reshapes the timing of extraction rather than cumulative volumes. Pathways achieving similar climate targets can impose markedly different environmental and resource pressures, shaping the feasibility and desirability of alternative transitions.

title: Rethinking Creep in Solid-State Batteries: From a Chemo-mechanical Liability to a Design Parameter
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Creep is an inherent time-dependent mechanical response in alkali-metal-based solid-state batteries (SSBs) subjected to sustained stack pressure. Although creep can significantly influence battery performance, its role has often been interpreted narrowly as either a beneficial mechanism for maintaining interfacial contact or a detrimental contributor to cell degradation. In this perspective, we establish a unified conceptual framework by linking sustained loading in the classical definition of creep to stack pressure in SSBs, thereby explaining why creep is intrinsic to their operation. We further argue that creep should be regarded as a chemo-mechanical phenomenon with inherently dual roles, whose competing effects govern the dynamic evolution of electrode–electrolyte interfaces during electrochemical cycling. Finally, we discuss how timescale-based design principles and time-resolved in situ and operando characterization can deepen understanding and guide the rational optimization of creep under practical battery operating conditions, thereby informing the design of durable next-generation alkali-metal SSBs.

title: Mitigating the Optical-Electrical Trade-Off in Sb2S3 Solar Cells with a Buried Li-Modified ZnO Interlayer
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thinning CdS electron-selective layers reduces parasitic blue-light absorption in Sb2S3 solar cells but can compromise charge collection and absorber growth. Here, we address this optical-electrical trade-off through crystal-structure-guided buried interface engineering. Exploiting the shared wurtzite structure of ZnO and CdS, we introduce a ZnO interlayer to regulate CdS formation. Reducing CdS thickness from 70 to 30 nm enhances Sb2S3 absorptance at 400–500 nm but decreases internal quantum efficiency (IQE) and increases nonradiative voltage loss, offsetting the optical gain. Undoped sol-gel ZnO improves CdS uniformity and partially restores the cathode contact response without improving long-range structural order. Li modification produces a more ordered ZnO/CdS stack, lowers the ZnO work function, and improves Sb2S3 texture and morphology. Consequently, IQE reaches 94%, with a champion power conversion efficiency of 8.10%. These findings establish a crystallography-guided strategy for integrating optical, electrical, and structural optimization.

title: O6-type layered oxides for sustainable high-energy battery cathodes
abstract: Cobalt-free cathodes are vital for green energy but suffer from structural instability. Here the authors report a unique O6-type framework that stabilizes oxygen redox for exceptional cycling durability.

title: Plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots for crop disease management
abstract: Plant fungal pathogens in crops can lead to substantial economic losses and pose a severe threat to food security. To tackle wheat Fusarium head blight, a devastating disease infecting wheat crops, an effective antifungal strategy using plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots has been developed.

title: Concurrent atmospheric phenomena amplify precipitation extremes under anthropogenic climate change
abstract: Extreme precipitation events are increasing in many regions. Here the authors discuss how the increasing concurrence of atmospheric phenomena could contribute to these trends under anthropogenic warming.

title: Climate and glacier geometry dominate global glacier–lake interactions
abstract: The contribution of glacial lakes to glacier mass loss is unclear. This work maps global glacial lakes in 2000 and 2020 to quantify changes in number, volume and area, showing that they explain 11 ± 7% of lake-terminating glacier loss, with climate forcing and glacier geometry the dominant factors.

title: Engineering Synthetic Molecular Operations Controlled by DNA‐Binding Proteins Through Templated Proximity
abstract: ABSTRACT We describe a DNA‐based molecular framework that enables DNA‐binding proteins (DBPs) to perform diverse synthetic operations beyond their natural functions. We introduce templated proximity as a mechanism through which DBP–DNA recognition events are converted into programmable DNA strand displacement reactions. In this architecture, protein binding templates the spatial colocalization of split DNA components, generating functional nucleic acid outputs that can be propagated into downstream processes. Using representative DBPs, including EGR1, YY1, and p53, we couple protein recognition to DNA strand displacement, activation of a fluorogenic RNA aptamer, regulation of CRISPR–Cas12a and Cas13 activity, and DBP‐triggered activation of hierarchical CRISPR cascades. These results establish templated proximity as a general transduction principle for integrating DNA‐binding proteins into modular nucleic acid reaction networks and demonstrate that DBPs can function as programmable interfaces connecting natural biomolecular recognition with engineered DNA‐based information processing, enabling modular communication layers with tailored synthetic functionality.

title: Short‐Range Molecular Ordering Enables Efficient and Stable Recombination Junction in Monolithic Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have made remarkable progress in recent years and are highly promising for next‐generation photovoltaics. The recombination junction (RJ) linking the top and bottom subcells is an essential component that governs both device efficiency and operational stability. However, depositing a uniform RJ on the complex CIGS substrate while simultaneously achieving charge transport and operational robustness remains a formidable challenge. Here, we construct a short‐range ordered (SRO) hole‐selective architecture for the RJ by exploiting π–π interactions between a self‐assembled molecule (SAM) and a polymeric SAM (PCCP). The SRO architecture shortens the intermolecular π–π stacking distance to accelerate carrier transport, while the surrounding amorphous regions effectively interrupt ion migration pathways. Furthermore, this strategy enables conformal coverage over the complex CIGS topography, improves interfacial robustness, and enhances structural resilience in service. Consequently, monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells employing the SRO‐RJ achieve a maximum power conversion efficiency of 29.60% (certified 28.94%, 0.2036 cm 2 ) and retain 98% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking. Our findings establish short‐range molecular ordering as an effective strategy for engineering efficient and durable recombination junctions in monolithic tandem photovoltaics.

title: Rare‐Earth‐Modulated Fe–Tb Dual‐Metal Single‐Atom Site Catalyst Enables Enhanced Activity and Durability for Acidic Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT The critical dependence on Pt in proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a bottleneck for commercialization. Single‐atom‐site catalysts, such as Fe‐NC, show comparable activity for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in PEMFCs, yet their inferior stability constrains practical applications. In this work, we introduced the rare‐earth element Tb as a single‐atom site into the Fe‐NC system and constructed a dual‐metal single‐atom site catalyst (denoted as FeTb‐NC). Theoretical calculations and experiments suggest that Tb centers, with strong oxophilicity and unique electronic structure, synergistically regulate *OH binding on adjacent FeN 4 sites, thereby lowering the energy barrier for *OH desorption. This elevates the activity of Fe centers and, more importantly, significantly lowers *OH coverage on FeN 4 , mitigating its detrimental effects. The optimized FeTb‐NC catalyst displays improved performance: The half‐wave potential is as high as 0.89 V (vs. RHE), retaining 88% of its initial current density after 100 h at 0.8 V. The PEMFC assembled with FeTb‐NC as the cathode catalyst exhibits competitive performance and durability; the peak power density reaches 1.10 W cm −2 under H 2 /O 2 conditions, and the device maintains 80% current‐density retention after 100 h under H 2 /air conditions. This work offers new insights into performance optimization of Fe–NC‐based materials and supports development of Pt‐free PEMFCs.

title: Molecular Regulation of Excited‐State Dynamics Enables Photochemically Stable Organic Semiconductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Photochemical degradation fundamentally limits the operational stability of organic photovoltaics (OPVs), yet the molecular processes linking excited‐state dynamics to irreversible chemical reactions remain poorly understood. Here, we show that excited‐state vibrational processes represent a previously underexplored molecular degree of freedom governing photochemical stability and can be regulated to suppress degradation. By incorporating melatonin into the donor layer of an OPV device, excited‐state molecular motions are effectively modulated, reducing vibrationally induced structural fluctuations, suppressing radical generation, and mitigating subsequent photochemical degradation under prolonged illumination. Comprehensive characterization reveals that molecular regulation modifies excited‐state relaxation pathways, thereby decreasing the probability of irreversible chemical transformations while preserving efficient charge generation and transport. As a result, D18/L8‐BO based binary device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 21.10% (certified as 20.6%), together with a more than threefold enhancement in T 80 lifetime under continuous illumination. The effectiveness of this strategy is further validated across multiple systems, demonstrating its general applicability. These findings establish a molecular connection between excited‐state vibrational dynamics and photochemical degradation, and identify regulation of excited‐state molecular motions as an effective strategy for simultaneously achieving high efficiency and long‐term stability in OPV devices.

title: Unraveling Synergistic Substrate–H 2 Activation and Tunable Counteranion Effects in Ru‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of 2‐Substituted Quinolines: An Integrated Kinetic and DFT Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Although the asymmetric hydrogenation of N ‐heteroarenes has achieved remarkable synthetic advances, the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood. Herein, we combine kinetic and DFT studies to reveal a novel synergistic substrate–H 2 activation mode in the Ru‐catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of quinolines. Both the quinoline substrate and the in situ generated dihydroquinoline intermediate act as sequential proton acceptors, causing a dynamic shift in the rate‐determining step between the first and second H 2 heterolytic cleavage events. This conclusion is strongly supported by Hammett analysis ( ρ = −1.19) and saturation kinetics. Notably, we identify a pronounced and tunable counteranion effect that plays two non‐spectator roles: (i) facilitating active‐site formation via anion dissociation, and (ii) stabilizing the charge‐separated H 2 ‐cleavage transition state through electronic effects, affording up to a 13‐fold rate enhancement. DFT calculations confirm that substrate‐assisted H 2 activation and anion‐assisted direct proton transfer are energetically favorable. This synergistic, anion‐regulated mechanism has also been validated in indole hydrogenation, and offers an improved understanding of the outer‐sphere catalytic hydrogenation manifold that diverges from the traditional concerted H − /H + transfer pathway. This work thus provides a unified theoretical framework for the asymmetric hydrogenation of diverse N ‐heteroarene substrates.

title: Intravenous phage therapy for difficult-to-treat infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis of individual patient data
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Intravenous phage therapy enables systemic bacteriophage delivery in difficult-to-treat infections, but raises distinct pharmacokinetic, immunological and safety considerations, while evidence remains fragmented. Here in this systematic review we analysed 60 studies from nine high-income countries, predominantly case reports, case series and uncontrolled trials reporting intravenous phage therapy with or without local administration and mostly alongside antibiotics. We extracted and synthesised individual patient data both descriptively and through a meta-analysis using mixed-effects models, which estimated probabilities of reporting clinical improvement and microbiological eradication of 65.8% (n = 122) and 55.3% (n = 106), respectively, while the probability of reporting adverse reactions was 9.2% (n = 168), with reactions predominantly mild and self-limited. In exploratory analyses, combined intravenous and local administration was associated with more frequent reporting of clinical improvement than intravenous administration alone, raising questions regarding potential limitations of the intravenous route. However, the uncontrolled and heterogeneous nature of current evidence warrants cautious interpretation and underscores the need for rigorous research.

title: var2csa transcription implicates variant surface antigen switching in cerebral malaria pathogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Previous PCR-based gene expression studies linked severe malaria, including cerebral malaria (CM), to Plasmodium falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein-1 (PfEMP1) variants that bind endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR). Using RNA sequencing and de novo transcriptome assembly in a matched CM case-control study of Malian children, we quantify var gene transcripts encoding PfEMP1s in 13 matched pairs of CM cases and uncomplicated malaria controls and in 25 CM cases and 55 uncomplicated malaria controls. Contrary to earlier findings, PfEMP1s that bind EPCR alone are not associated with CM. Transcription of conserved gene var2csa is implicated in var gene switching in vitro. Here, its transcription is significantly associated with CM across study sites, suggesting that switching may contribute to CM pathogenesis. Importantly, this association is observed at the transcript level, but potentially not translation. We use a protein microarray to show a lack of antibody responses to the VAR2CSA antigen in cerebral malaria, supporting an association between CM and var2csa transcription rather than antigenic presence. CM is also associated with distinct var transcriptional profiles and dual ICAM-1/EPCR-binding PfEMP1 variants. These findings underscore the complexity of PfEMP1-mediated pathogenesis and highlight the need for deeper investigation of transcriptional and regulatory mechanisms underlying severe malaria.

title: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Muscle mass is central to physical function and metabolic health, but can decrease with disease, aging and weight loss interventions. As weight loss interventions become more widely used, agents that preserve or increase muscle mass are needed. To identify such therapeutic opportunities, we perform genome-wide association meta-analyses of arm, leg, trunk and total lean mass measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, a widely used method to estimate muscle mass. We identify 63 loci, including a rare missense variant in MSTN (p.Ile225Thr, rs143242500), which has the largest effect on leg lean mass (β = 0.28 SD [95% CI: 0.19, 0.37], P = 1.9 × 10-9). MSTN encodes myostatin, a negative regulator of skeletal muscle mass and a therapeutic target for muscle wasting disorders. Here, we identify a genome-wide significant association at MSTN in humans and characterize its functional consequences, providing genetic evidence that may inform the long-term systemic effects of myostatin inhibition.

title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

title: Local niche-derived immunosuppressive CXCR2+ cells impair antiviral immunity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Symptom severity after viral infection varies among individuals, yet its mechanism remains poorly understood. We categorize mice into recovering and non-recovering groups based on body weight after infection with the same titer of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). We reveal that in the olfactory bulb (OB) where VSV initially expands, non-recovering mice exhibit an anti-inflammatory environment, suggesting its detrimental effect. Importantly, CXCR2+ cells resembling immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are more abundant in the OB of non-recovering mice than in that of recovering mice after VSV infection. Depleting CXCR2+ MDSC-like cells from the brain increases inflammatory responses and the animal’s survival after infection. Furthermore, site-specific labeling indicates that a significant fraction of these cells in the OB originate from the skull-bone marrow (skull-BM) as well as circulation. This study reveals the lethal effects of CXCR2+ MDSC-like cells on local immune responses to viral infection, highlighting their therapeutic potential for antiviral defense.

title: Cholesterol dysregulation contributes to hematopoietic failure in parn-mutant zebrafish with implications for dyskeratosis congenita
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Germline mutations in PARN cause dyskeratosis congenita (DC), an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome characterized by multilineage cytopenia and progression to myeloid disease. The mechanisms underlying this malignant transformation have not been fully elucidated. Here we show, using a loss-of-function CRISPR-Cas9 zebrafish parn mutant, hematopoietic stem and progenitor (HSPC) expansion and reduced mature hematopoietic cells across various lineages. Cholesterol biosynthesis was transcriptionally activated; a finding recapitulated in patient-derived iPSCs with PARN mutations. Inhibiting cholesterol biosynthesis rescued HSPC expansion and anemia in parn mutants. Concurrent myeloid differentiation therapy or Wnt inhibition reduced HSPCs to varying degrees. We further demonstrate a role for activated Erk signaling in impairing erythrocyte differentiation and show robust rescue with trametinib treatment. Overall, our findings uncover unrecognized roles for Parn in regulating cholesterol metabolism and Erk signaling and provide preclinical evidence for targeting these pathways to restore hematopoiesis in DC.

title: Prodrug-Based Self-Assembly Enables Dual-Triggered Release of Triazole Fungicide with Improved Environmental Safety
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive prodrug-based controlled-release systems enable precise spatiotemporal regulation of the site-specific activation and release of active ingredients, thereby enhancing overall efficacy while minimizing off-target effects in pesticide application. In this study, cyproconazole (CPZ) was covalently conjugated with cinnamic acid (CAA) via a hydrolyzable ester bond to yield a prodrug (CCP), which spontaneously self-assembled into uniform nanoparticles (CCP NPs) without the addition of any auxiliary adjuvants. Benefiting from its small hydrodynamic diameter (277 nm), narrow size distribution (PDI = 0.139), and high surface charge (–33.2 mV), the resulting CCP NPs exhibited significantly improved foliar retention and spreading capacity on plant leaf surfaces. Compared with commercial CPZ suspension concentrate (CPZ SC), CCP NPs reduced soil leaching by 71.81% and 57.48% in yellowish-brown soil from Beijing and red soil from Yunnan Province, respectively. Furthermore, CCP NPs displayed pH- and esterase-dual-triggered release behavior and provided long-term antifungal activity against plant pathogens with a control efficacy of 74.86%, outperforming CPZ SC (50.36%) after 14 days of foliar application. Comprehensive biosafety evaluations revealed that CCP NPs had no adverse effects on plant growth and exhibited approximately 5-fold lower acute toxicity to earthworms. Overall, this CAA-based prodrug nano assembly provides an effective strategy that simultaneously enhances efficacy and curbs environmental mobility, thereby supporting the development of sustainable crop protection products.

title: Ligand‐Engineered Metal‐Organic‐Covalent‐Organic Frameworks Enable Red‐Light‐Driven H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Tunable Biomass Upgrading
abstract: ABSTRACT Harvesting low‐energy photons, particularly in the deep‐red and near‐infrared regions, for artificial photosynthesis remains a significant challenge due to the inherent difficulty in driving multi‐electron redox processes with limited photon energy. Herein, we reported a tunable ligand engineering strategy to construct a series of isostructural metal‐organic‐covalent‐organic frameworks (MOCOFs), namely MOCOF‐phen x ( x = 0, 1, 2 and 3). By gradient increasing the number of phenanthroline ligands around the Ru(II) center, we precisely modulated the electronic structures and excited‐state properties of the resulting MOCOFs. Remarkably, the ligand‐engineered MOCOFs showed excellent red‐light‐driven H 2 O 2 generation coupled with switchable biomass upgrading, in which the reaction selectivity of furfuryl alcohol oxidation was profoundly governed. MOCOF‐phen 0 preferentially affords 6‐hydroxy‐2H‐pyran‐3(6H)‐one (PN) with 91.4% selectivity, whereas MOCOF‐phen 3 steers the reaction towards 5‐hydroxy‐2,5‐dihydrofuran‐2‐one (FN). This work establishes a molecular‐level design blueprint for low‐energy‐light‐driven photocatalysis, demonstrating ligand engineering in crystalline framework materials for optimizing activity and selectivity towards sustainable photosynthesis.

title: Catalytic Aziridination With Simple Acyl Azides via Validated Copper‐Acyl Nitrenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Terminal copper‐nitrenes are widely proposed as reactive intermediates in catalytic N‐group transfer, but well‐defined copper‐acyl nitrenes remain largely unexplored. We show that simple aryl acyl azides serve as effective precursors to terminal copper‐acyl nitrenes that catalytically convert styrene into N‐acyl aziridines in yields of up to 76%. Ten copper‐acyl nitrenes were generated, detected, and characterized by spectroscopic, kinetic, and computational methods. The active species exhibits a singlet ground state, as supported by Evans NMR and EPR spectroscopy, and multireference calculations. Mechanistic studies reveal predominantly polar nitrene transfer together with a spin‐crossover event leading to a persistent radical intermediate. The use of readily available acyl azides broadens the scope of copper‐catalyzed aziridination beyond nitrene precursors bearing strongly electron‐withdrawing substituents and identifies copper‐acyl nitrenes as competent and mechanistically distinct nitrene‐transfer agents.

title: Core-edge integration of negative triangularity plasmas in TCV
abstract: This study demonstrates the core-edge integration of negative triangularity (NT) plasmas with reactor-relevant operation on TCV. Neutral beam injection (NBI)-heated scenarios are developed, achieving stationary, high-performance plasmas, with up to 1.7 and above 1, at a relatively high density (Greenwald fraction of approximately 0.4). Featuring a hybrid shape that combines a negative upper-triangularity and a positive lower-triangularity, the NT L-mode achieves central ion and electron temperatures that are higher than those of its positive triangularity counterpart. Before any extrinsic impurity seeding, the divertor is already cold. This is evidenced by the retreat of the C III front from the outer target, which corresponds to a low outer-target electron temperature ( ), as well as by a significant fraction of radiated power, partly attributable to the high operational density. With divertor seeding, an X-point Radiator is formed, further cooling the divertor, with only a slight reduction in plasma performance.

title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
abstract: ABSTRACT The construction of α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters—a structural motif of high value in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules—remains a formidable synthetic challenge due to inherent steric and stereoelectronic constraints. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry, enabling the direct and highly enantioselective α‐alkylation of bench‐stable fluorinated acetic esters with both silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This approach integrates anodic single‐electron oxidation with asymmetric Lewis base catalysis, converting in situ‐generated disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates into configurationally well‐defined, chiral ITU‐bound α‐carbonyl tertiary radical intermediates. Subsequent stereocontrolled radical cross‐coupling with SOMOphilic partners furnishes a broad range of esters bearing α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This work not only fills a significant gap in the single‐electron chemistry of disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates but also provides a versatile platform for the rapid assembly of optically active α‐fluorinated quaternary carbonyl compounds, with significant potential in drug discovery and complex molecule synthesis.

title: Terminal Engineering Drives Compact π–π Stacking to Suppress Electron–Phonon Coupling in Narrow‐Bandgap Electron Acceptors
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors are attractive for short‐wavelength infrared (SWIR) photodetection, yet their extended spectral response is accompanied by strong electron–phonon coupling and substantial nonradiative energy losses. Herein, we reveal that intermolecular π–π stacking provides an effective molecular handle for regulating electron–phonon coupling in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors. A series of ultranarrow‐bandgap acceptors with systematically varied terminal groups are developed, enabling progressive shortening of the π–π stacking distance from 3.74 to 3.53 Å. The resulting compact intermolecular packing strengthens intermolecular interactions and suppresses electron–phonon coupling, thereby reducing vibrational relaxation, prolonging exciton lifetimes, and mitigating nonradiative energy losses. Consequently, the BIP‐M8‐based organic photodetector delivers a responsivity of 0.29 A W −1 and a specific detectivity of 1.84 × 10 12 Jones at 1180 nm, with a detectivity exceeding 10 11 Jones over 400–1300 nm. These results establish intermolecular π–π stacking as a molecular design parameter for controlling vibronic interactions and mitigating nonradiative energy losses in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors, offering a general strategy for high‐performance SWIR optoelectronics.

title: Correction to “Microenvironment Engineering as a Design Principle for Suppressing Catalyst Metal Loss”
Tailored Mn Doping Enables Substantially Boosted Fluorescence Emission in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectric Scintillator
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic‐inorganic ferroelectric materials, due to their advantages such as spontaneous polarization, controllable electric domains and multi‐physical field coupling effects, are widely applied in fields including sensors, actuators and optoelectronics. However, there are few successful cases that combine ferroelectricity with dopant‐induced efficient luminescence effects in ferroelectric materials. Herein, through delicate Mn 2+ ion doping, we have successfully designed a multifunctional luminescent ferroelectric material, (GABA) 2 CdCl 4 :4%Mn 2+ (GABA = γ‐aminobutyric acid) which retains its excellent ferroelectric properties with a spontaneous polarization of 4.0 µC cm −2 . Meanwhile, its photoluminescence intensity can be systematically modulated by varying the Mn 2+ doping concentration, demonstrating excellent controllability and functional versatility. Notably, Mn 2+ doping induces a distinct bulk orange‐red luminescence at 610 nm, dramatically boosting the quantum yield from 0.11% to 67%. Leveraging such superior bulk luminescence, (GABA) 2 CdCl 4 :4%Mn 2+ delivers a high light yield of 52 170 photons MeV −1 and a low detection limit of 62.3 nGy s −1 , along with good environmental and radiation stability, marking the first Mn 2+ ‐doped organic‐inorganic hybrid perovskite ferroelectric x‐ray scintillator.

title: Rational Design of a Chiral Hybrid Ge(II) Halide With Giant Chiroptical Activity for Circularly Polarized Light Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral hybrid metal halides integrate semiconducting optoelectronic functionality with intrinsic chirality, offering new opportunities in the field of next‐generation chiral photonics and spintronics. However, the incorporation of chiral organic ligands alone is often insufficient to induce pronounced chiral structural distortions, thereby limiting the resulting chiroptical activity. Herein, we demonstrate for the first time that the stereochemically active 4s 2 lone‐pair of Ge 2+ can serve as an internal structural amplifier of chirality. We rationally designed and synthesized a pair of enantiomeric chiral hybrid Ge(II) halides, denoted as ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 (MBA is methylbenzylammonium). Specifically, the strong lone‐pair expression in ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 drives significant chirality‐favorable distortions, manifested by a large asymmetric bond angle variance and projected deflection angle of the chiral [−Ge−I−] ∞ chains. This enhanced structural chirality increases the circular dichroism (CD) anisotropy factor ( g CD ) of ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 to 2.66 times that of the Pb(II) homologs. Benefiting from the superior chiroptical activity, ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 further exhibits second‐harmonic generation (SHG)‐CD anisotropy factor ( g SHG‐CD ) values of −1.17/1.09, while the corresponding devices achieve photocurrent anisotropy factors ( g Iph ) of −0.403/0.391. Finally, we demonstrated a proof‐of‐concept circularly polarized light‐encrypted optical communication system. Our work provides a new insight into the rational design of high‐performance chiral functional materials.

title: Data-driven distributionally robust planning of coastal distribution networks and PV-storage-EV stations for low-carbon energy transition
abstract: Coastal distribution networks (DNs) are becoming key infrastructure for the low-carbon energy transition as electric vehicle (EV) charging, photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage, and marine renewable procurement are increasingly coupled at the planning stage. Existing planning models, however, usually treat network expansion, PV-storage-EV station (PSES) deployment, low-carbon operation, and coastal asset degradation separately. This paper proposes a data-driven distributionally robust planning framework for coastal DNs and PSESs. The framework jointly optimizes radial network topology and PSES siting while incorporating salt-spray degradation costs, carbon-emission-flow (CEF)-based nodal carbon accounting, and tidal-generation-driven procurement costs. To represent heterogeneous uncertainty, the model combines continuous box uncertainty for load and PV availability with probability ambiguity over EV-charging scenarios generated from historical charging profiles. The resulting two-stage distributionally robust optimization problem is reformulated through exact relaxation of ESS mode binaries and KKT-based decomposition, and is solved by an inexact column-and-constraint generation (i-C&CG) algorithm. Case studies on a realistic 47-node coastal feeder show that salt-spray exposure can alter the selected topology and PSES siting, while the proposed planning scheme improves voltage quality, reduces annualized total cost, and reveals the cost--carbon trade-off of tidal procurement. The tailored i-C&CG algorithm obtains the same optimal design as conventional C&CG with about an order-of-magnitude reduction in solution time.

title: Autonomous Scanning Electrochemical Cell Microscopy Enables Rapid Exploration of Large Compositionally Complex Material Spaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Alloying is a central strategy in electrocatalysis, enabling fine‐tuning of the electronic structure. In particular, compositionally complex solid solutions (CCSSs), often called high‐entropy alloys, are of high interest. However, the “combinatorial explosion” in the number of possible compositions poses a critical bottleneck for the discovery of CCSS electrocatalysts. We present an autonomous scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) system for ultrahigh‐throughput and large‐scale CCSS activity screening. The platform rapidly establishes composition–activity relationships across multiple thin‐film CCSS materials libraries via active learning and automated library exchange. Embedding analytical expressions of voltammetry in the algorithm enables the learning of whole voltammograms rather than a single selected metric. As a demonstration, we investigated hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activities of Au–Ir–Rh, where Ir and Rh exhibit strong metal‐hydrogen binding and Au exhibits weak binding as derived from the HER volcano plot. The activity trend was accurately predicted after measuring only 15% of all 966 measurement areas. Au 30 Ir 20 Rh 50 and Au 10 Ir 35 Rh 55 exhibit the highest activities with standard rate constants of ∼0.012 cm s −1 , demonstrating positive synergistic contributions from elemental mixing. The proposed platform is broadly applicable to a wide range of electrocatalytic reactions, providing a general pathway for accelerating CCSS electrocatalyst discovery.

title: Selective Oxidation of Toluene to Benzaldehyde Driven by Electroreduction of Oxygen to Hydrogen Peroxide Coupled With In Situ Electro‐Fenton Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective toluene oxidation is a pivotal reaction in the fine chemical industry. While electrooxidation at high anodic potentials shows promise, the low efficiency of the generation of reactive oxygen species limits the product yield. Herein, we describe a cathodic strategy for selective oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde via coupling the electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen reduction with an in situ electro‐Fenton reaction (eH 2 O 2 ‐EF). Among the different metal–nitrogen–carbon single‐atom catalysts (M‐NC SAC, M = Fe, Co, and Ni), Co‐NC SAC stands out as the best catalyst, featuring a benzaldehyde selectivity of 90.63% and a yield of 21.9 mmol h −1 at −0.3 V versus RHE with stable operation over 23 cycles. In situ spectroscopy and radical scavenging and quantification experiments indicate that the eH 2 O 2 ‐EF proceeds via toluene adsorption, ·OH‐mediated oxidation, and desorption of products, where the ·OH generation and intermediate adsorption/desorption jointly determine the benzaldehyde yield. Theoretical analysis indicates that the Co‐NC SAC thermodynamically facilitates H 2 O 2 generation, accompanied by moderate benzaldehyde adsorption and an uphill further‐oxidation step, leading to selective benzaldehyde production. This work establishes a novel cathodic paradigm for the selective oxidation of inert aromatic ‐H bonds under mild conditions.

title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Templated Spatial Confinement of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as efficient hole‐contacting layers for p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and weak bonding with the substrate result in heterogeneous buried interfaces. Herein, a covalent organic framework (COF)‐templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy is developed by employing a newly designed phosphonate–carbazole‐based COF, namely COF‐TPACz , to regulate the buried interface. The nanoscale island‐like COF domains could restrict the penetration of aggregated SAM molecules and allow well‐distributed ones to anchor on exposed substrates. Meanwhile, hydrogen‐bonding and π–π interactions between COF‐TPACz and SAM favor a more uniform molecular arrangement on the COF domains. These adjustments synergistically suppress molecular aggregation and improve surface coverage, yielding a denser and more homogeneous SAM interface. Furthermore, the improved interface optimizes upper perovskite crystallization, promotes compact and vertically extended grains, and strengthens buried interfacial contact, thereby suppressing nonradiative recombination and facilitating charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the CTSC‐based PSCs achieve a peak efficiency of 27.03%, together with enhanced long‐term stability. We believe these findings provide a conceptual advance for realizing homogeneous SAM via spatial confinement and a viable route toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Stabilizing High‐Voltage Oxygen Holes via π‐Bonding Mediated Frontier‐Orbital Character Inversion in Intermediate‐Regime Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen redox chemistry offers a promising route to higher energy densities in layered oxide cathodes. However, it is commonly plagued by unstable O─O dimerization that leads to voltage hysteresis and capacity loss. While oxygen hole can mitigate these degradation pathways, its lower operating voltage results in reduced energy density. Herein, high‐voltage oxygen‐hole states are stabilized in Li 2 RuO 3 through precisely tailoring the Ru─O π‐bonding interaction. The successful modulation arises from a dynamic evolution of the electronic structure during delithiation, the so‐called frontier‐orbital character inversion, which has been experimentally validated through combined analysis of the elemental contributions to states near the Fermi level. Oxygen oxidation subsequently involves an O 2p‐dominated antibonding state, avoiding the pronounced bond destabilization associated with electron removal from bonding orbitals. Such behavior is attributed to the unique position of ruthenates within the intermediate regime between Mott–Hubbard and charge‐transfer insulators. And this specific electronic state positioning facilitates a dynamic transition toward a stable negative charge‐transfer regime. This boundary‐crossing effect is especially pronounced in high‐valent systems owing to intense covalency modulations upon oxidation. These insights establish a clear electronic‐structure‐based design principle, highlighting the importance of orbital engineering in boundary‐regime systems to achieve stable and high‐voltage anionic redox.

title: Coupled Self‐Alkalization and Chelation Chemistry Enables Highly Reversible Zn Anodes and Rechargeable Alkaline Zn–I 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical development of alkaline rechargeable zinc‐based batteries (ARZBs) is fundamentally limited by the intrinsic trade‐off among redox potential, high Zn 2+ concentration, and Zn anode stability. Herein, we report a synergistic “self‐alkalization + chelation chemistry” electrolyte using ethylenediamine (EN) as a multifunctional co‐solvent. Acting simultaneously as an organic base and a Zn 2+ chelating ligand, EN enables in situ OH − generation while forming soluble five‐membered Zn chelates, thereby reconstructing Zn dissolution chemistry in alkaline media. The resulting electrolyte achieves a Zn 2+ concentration of 1 M at pH 12.45, transforming Zn transport from diffusion‐limited to migration‐assisted behavior. Meanwhile, preferential adsorption and in situ decomposition of EN generate an organic–inorganic hybrid interphase that effectively suppresses corrosion and parasitic reactions. As a result, Zn||Zn coin cells exhibit stable Zn plating/stripping for 380 h. Furthermore, EN stabilizes reactive I + intermediates through coordination chemistry, enabling rechargeable alkaline Zn||I 2 batteries with a high energy density of 812.9 Wh kg −1 . More importantly, the exceptionally high Zn 2+ flux and interfacial reversibility enable the first demonstration of anode‐free alkaline Zn||I 2 batteries, which operate stably for 860 cycles. This work establishes a general electrolyte engineering strategy for decoupling the long‐standing electrolyte trilemma in ARZBs and advancing high‐energy aqueous batteries.

title: Encapsulating Metal–Organic Cluster in Metal–Organic Framework Film for Tandem Amplifying Third‐Order Nonlinear Optics
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and metal–organic clusters (MOCs) are promising platforms for third‐order nonlinear optics (NLO) because their inorganic–organic components enable designable structures and tunable photo/electronic properties. However, integrating MOFs and MOCs for tandem third‐order NLO remains unexplored. Here, we combine MOF and MOC for third‐order NLO by encapsulating MOC in a porous MOF film. A [001]‐oriented conductive MOF Ni‐HHTP film (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) is prepared by liquid‐phase heating drop‐coating and shows excellent electro‐regulated third‐order NLO. Furthermore, iron‐based MOC (FeOC) is encapsulated into the ordered nanochannels of Ni‐HHTP film (Ni‐HHTP@FeOC) using an immersion strategy. The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient ( β ) increasing from 4.9 × 10 −6 to 9.7 × 10 −6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10 −6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

title: Surfactant‐Induced Morphology Reconstruction for High‐Performance Near‐Infrared Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐performance near‐infrared (NIR) perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) require the simultaneous suppression of nonradiative recombination and efficient photon extraction, in which additive often play a vital role. However, molecular design rules that connect additive structure with both crystallization control and optical morphology remain poorly defined. Here, we employ a series of hydroxyl‐functional quaternary ammonium surfactants—TMPAC, HDPAC, and DDPAC—with different alkyl‐chain lengths while retaining a common polar headgroup. This molecular design reveals how hydrophobic‐tail length regulates precursor organization and governs the balance among emissive quality, optical outcoupling, and charge transport. Increasing the alkyl‐chain length alters the phase‐conversion kinetics, suppresses lateral grain coalescence, and promotes anisotropic out‐of‐plane growth, thereby producing corrugated FAPbI 3 films. The intermediate‐chain HDPAC provides sufficient interfacial organization to improve radiative efficiency and photon extraction while maintaining favorable charge‐transport balance. HDPAC‐based devices achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 27.0%, exhibit markedly suppressed efficiency roll‐off, and deliver a maximum radiance exceeding 513 W sr − 1 m − 2 . These results establish hydrophobic‐tail length as an effective molecule‐level modulator for coupling interfacial crystallization control with photon management in perovskite emitters.

title: One‐Step Conversion of Thermoplastic Elastomers into Ionic Ordered Mesoporous Polymers via Interface‐Directed Chain Scission: A Plastic Upcycling Strategy for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT As a cornerstone of the circular materials economy, chemical recycling typically breaks commodity plastics down into small molecular building blocks. While this strategy is reasonable for most plastics, styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) can be a notable exception. These materials can intrinsically self‐assemble into ordered nanostructures, yet most upcycling methods discard this morphological asset, leaving TPEs a compelling but underexploited feedstock for high‐value applications. Here, we report a one‐step approach that upcycles TPEs into ionic ordered mesoporous polymers (OMPs) in their solid state, through interface‐directed chain scission. Adding a small amount of radical initiator (dicumyl peroxide) during the sulfonation of polystyrene‐ block ‐poly(ethylene‐ran‐butylene)‐ block ‐polystyrene (SEBS) leverages a diffusion‐controlled reaction front to selectively cleave the minority polystyrene domains, while crosslinking and sulfonating the majority phase. This one‐step process at 145°C installs ionic character and establishing uniform mesoporosity without the high‐temperature calcination (typically > 350°C) that conventionally erodes functional groups. Furthermore, the resulting OMPs act as high‐performance sorbents for atmospheric water harvesting, demonstrating rapid kinetics, solar‐driven regeneration, and excellent cycling stability, while a simple lithium chloride (LiCl) encapsulation step enhances their water uptake capacity to 2.46 g/g.

title: Photoinduced Homolytic Carbon–Palladium Bond Cleavage of Zwitterionic π ‐Allylpalladium Species and Annulation with 1,3‐Dienes and 1,3‐Enynes
abstract: ABSTRACT The zwitterionic π ‐allylpalladium species are versatile intermediates in modern annulation chemistry, yet their assembling partners have been largely limited to electrophilic reagents or dipolarophiles. Herein, we report a previously inaccessible (4 + 2) annulation reaction of common π ‐allylpalladium(II) dipoles with electron‐neutral 1,3‐dienes and 1‐aryl‐substituted 1,3‐enynes via a distinct cooperative photo‐induced pathway. Mechanistic studies indicate that the process proceeds through visible light‐promoted homolytic cleavage of the allylic C–Pd bond to generate Pd(I) and allylic radicals, which undergo addition to polyunsaturated systems. Subsequent Pd(I)–radical recombination and intramolecular allylic substitution furnish a broad array of multifunctional oxa‐ and aza‐heterocycles, as well as carbocyclic frameworks, in moderate to good yields. In addition, their assemblies with electron‐poor dienes are also applicable, whereas the regioselectivity is distinct from that observed in traditional dipole‐based annulations. Furthermore, the asymmetric version is successful by employing chiral bisphosphine ligands, with fair to good enantioselectivity achieved.

title: Selective Reductive Amination of Long‐Chain Diols to Primary Diamines Over Nitrogen‐Modulated Ru 0 /Ru δ+ Dual Sites
abstract: ABSTRACT Linear primary diamines (DAs) are essential monomers for nylon and polyamide. Sustainable production of DAs from bio‐diols via reductive amination (RA) requires to achieve the tandem diols dehydrogenation (rate‐determining), aldimine condensation and imine hydrogenation, which remains challenging due to low efficiency, poor selectivity, and rapid catalyst deactivation under ammonia‐rich conditions. In this study, we report an efficient and durable catalytic system for the RA of linear primary bio‐diols to DAs by constructing a Ru n ‐N x ‐C catalyst with N‐modulated Ru 0 /Ru δ+ dual sites. In the RA of 1,9‐nonanediol, a high yield of 1,9‐nonanediamine up to 98.5% is achieved under mild conditions (170°C, 0.3 MPa H 2 , 0.7 MPa NH 3 ) for at least 10 cycles. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ru δ+ and Ru 0 sites cooperatively drive diol dehydrogenation through O─H and Cα─H bond activation, respectively, while their synergistic interplay further promotes the subsequent RA toward DAs formation. DFT and AIMD simulations reveal that N‐modulated Ru δ+ sites exhibit weaker NH 3 adsorption than pristine Ru δ+ surfaces, thereby mitigating the excessive deposition of imine‐derived intermediates and improving catalytic stability. Ru n ‐N x ‐C was further evaluated for the conversion of selected biomass‐ and polyester‐derived substrates into value‐added DAs.

title: The person behind the scientist
abstract: Matteo Seita and Mengying Liu discuss their reflections as organizers of The Past Metallurgists Society lecture series, where scientists meet to share stories of distinguished metallurgists from the past.

title: Bifunctional Pt/CeO2 Nanozyme-Mediated Metabolic Regulation Promotes NAD+ Regeneration and ROS Clearance to Ameliorate Age-Related Osteoporosis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Age-related osteoporosis is characterized by progressive loss of bone mass and deterioration of trabecular microarchitecture, driven by chronic inflammation, redox imbalance, mitochondrial dysfunction, and osteoblast senescence that uncouples bone formation from resorption. During aging, declining nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) availability further exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and stress responses, suggesting that restoring NAD+ redox homeostasis could be a viable therapeutic strategy. Here, we reported a bifunctional nanozyme-mediated metabolic regulation strategy to promote NAD+ regeneration and scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) for the treatment of age-related osteoporosis. The bifunctional nanozyme (Pt/CeO2) was constructed by in situ growth of platinum nanoparticles on cerium oxide nanorods and was designed for ROS scavenging and NAD+ regeneration via NADH (reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) oxidation. In senescent osteoblasts, Pt/CeO2 reduced ROS, restored mitochondrial integrity, and alleviated senescence, thereby promoting osteogenic differentiation. In vivo results confirmed that systemic administration of Pt/CeO2 preserved trabecular architecture and increased bone mineral density in naturally aged mice. These findings demonstrated that coupling ROS scavenging with the restoration of NAD+ redox homeostasis via Pt/CeO2 nanozyme provided a promising therapeutic strategy to counteract osteoblast senescence and slow the progression of age-related osteoporosis.

title: Boron Nitride-Enhanced Thermally Conductive, Color-Developer-Free Thermochromic Polyurethane Composite Phase Change Material
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional thermochromic phase-change materials (TC-PCMs) face several limitations, including the use of potentially toxic color developers, low heat storage/release efficiency, and the compositional complexity of conventional color-developing systems. In this study, we synthesized a negative photochromic spiropyran (SPOH) that undergoes heat-driven ring-opening isomerization, thereby enabling a direct color change. SPOH was employed as the thermochromic unit, lauric acid (LA) as the phase-change energy storage component, and amino-functionalized boron nitride (BN-NH2) as a thermally conductive filler. Through the reaction of polyethylene glycol (PEG2K) with hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) and its trimer (THDI), a cross-linked polyurethane network (TC-CPCMs) was constructed to encapsulate SPOH, LA, and BN-NH2. The TC-CPCMs exhibited high thermal energy storage performance, with an enthalpy efficiency (φ) of 82.1%. The introduction of BN-NH2 increased the thermal conductivity to 0.9196 W/(m·K), representing a 252% enhancement compared with that of BN-free TC-CPCMs, while maintaining stable and reversible thermochromic properties, thereby enabling the functional integration of thermal energy storage and temperature indication. In applications involving wastewater waste heat recovery and the thermal management of electronic devices, TC-CPCMs demonstrated significant performance improvements while enabling visual monitoring of the energy storage process through color changes.

title: Laser Fabrication of Vibrating Microcavities on Silicon: Formation Dynamics and Frequency Tunability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Laser processing of silicon has long since become a standard method for wafer dicing, surface texturing, recrystallization after ion implantation, as well as surface amorphization, to name a few examples. Here, we introduce a different concept: the fabrication of vibrating microcavities in a commercial platform, Si wafers covered by a thick SiO2 layer, acting as a membrane. We demonstrate that by exposing our material system to single ultrashort laser pulses above the evaporation threshold of Si, a controlled delamination of the cover layer without fracture can be achieved, leading to the formation of a microcavity accompanied by a surface bulging up to 1.5 μm. The formation dynamics of the microcavities have been investigated by time-resolved optical probe techniques. Ultrafast pump–probe microscopy resolves the initial stages of substrate melting and the onset of layer expansion followed by relaxation. Real-time reflectivity measurements with nanosecond resolution resolve the long-lived, highly complex oscillation process of the membrane, extending over tens of μs. The formed cavities can be re-excited at low fluence without damage or degradation, featuring vibrations at single frequencies with high Q factors. The frequencies can be tuned continuously from 8 MHz up to 19 MHz by adjusting the fabrication fluence. A simple classical model is found to well describe the behavior of the membranes. Our results pave the way for applications in micro- and nano-optics and acoustics, in great part due to the commercial availability of the Si–SiO2 platform and the simplicity of the fabrication method. An extension to the field of microelectromechanical system (MEMS) of this technology is proposed.

title: A fully electromagnetic hybrid PIC-fluid model for predictive fusion neutron yield in dense plasma focus
abstract: A fully electromagnetic hybrid ion-PIC/electron-fluid framework is developed for the implosion-to-pinch phase of dense plasma focus (DPF) discharges. Ions are advanced kinetically, electrons form a charge-neutralizing fluid under the quasi-neutral approximation, and the full Maxwell equations are solved in both plasma and vacuum. The generalized Ohm law includes resistive, electron pressure-gradient, and Hall terms. Applied to a non-hollow 180 kA geometry initialized from a pre-ionized end-of-rundown state, the framework reproduces the axial rundown, radial compression, and pinch stages. The sheath front trajectory agrees with fully kinetic benchmarks within 10%, and a pinch-radius comparison captures the radial collapse. A beam-target neutron diagnostic applied to the simulated ion distribution gives a yield of , at the same scale as the fully kinetic reference. The ion spectrum develops a non-Maxwellian suprathermal tail to about 0.25 MeV. The yield remains sensitive to the electron-temperature closure and anode geometry. The framework captures relevant macroscopic observables and ion-kinetic diagnostics at a computational cost roughly – times lower than comparable fully kinetic electromagnetic PIC simulations.

title: Black Titanium‐Oxo Cluster as a Dual‐Mode Catalyst for Regioselective Protein Editing
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically precise titanium‐oxo clusters are discrete molecular analogues of TiO 2 and structural building blocks of many metal–organic frameworks. Combining features of homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, they provide a versatile platform for catalyst design. However, due to limited stability in aqueous media, they remain largely unexplored in biologically relevant catalysis. Here, we report a structurally engineered hexanuclear titanium‐oxo cluster (tBu‐Ti 6 ) with promising photophysical properties, including a very low optical gap of 1.56 eV. Using β‐lactoglobulin as a model protein, we demonstrate that tBu‐Ti 6 is an effective heterogeneous catalyst in aqueous solution, promoting both hydrolytic and photooxidative protein cleavage via two distinct pathways: Lewis acid‐mediated hydrolysis and reactive oxygen species‐driven photocatalysis. Nano‐scale liquid chromatography‐tandem mass spectrometry (nLC‐MS/MS) reveals preferential cleavage near negatively charged regions of the protein, indicating electrostatic substrate recognition. Under 370 nm irradiation, tBu‐Ti 6 induces oxidation of tyrosine, tryptophan, and methionine residues in the intact β‐lactoglobulin, underscoring its potential as a photocatalyst for selective protein modifications. During reactions in aqueous solutions, the cluster remains structurally intact, shows no decomposition or dissolution, and is reusable without loss of activity. Together, these results establish TOCs as versatile molecular catalysts for controlled protein modifications and underscore their potential in bioinspired catalysis.

title: Damping and accumulation characteristics of flow driven by fishbone instability
abstract: The persistence of fishbone-driven flows across successive bursts is critical to their potential role in regulating turbulence and improving core confinement, yet the damping characteristics of such flows have not been experimentally characterized. Here we report the first direct measurement of the damping rate of fishbone-driven flows using Doppler reflectometry on the EAST tokamak. The experimentally obtained damping rate exceeds prior theoretical predictions, and this discrepancy can be reconciled by incorporating the effective charge number into the calculation of the damping rate. Furthermore, we observe that flow accumulation occurs when the time interval between successive fishbone bursts is sufficiently short, and we estimate the critical inter-burst interval threshold for accumulation to be approximately 1 ms under the present discharge conditions. These results establish an essential experimental foundation for understanding the temporal persistence of fishbone-driven flows and their implications for transport barrier dynamics.

title: Adaptive Active Site Programming via Electrolyte Engineering Toward Enhanced Catalytic Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over active site coordination is essential for advancing electrocatalysis, yet remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of how operating environments, particularly electrolyte anions, reshape local structure, and coordination. Here, we combine grand canonical ensemble calculations with experimental validations to investigate five representative anions (F − , Cl − , Br − , NO 3 − , and H 2 PO 4 − ) across a range of pH and potential conditions. Using Fe─N─C single‐atom catalysts and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) as a prototypical system, we reveal the adaptive evolution of active site coordination: Anions act as axial ligands that modulate the electronic structure of active sites and enable pH‐dependent regulation of catalytic activity. Specifically, NO 3 − serves as the most effective axial ligand for enhancing catalytic activity across the entire pH range. Electrochemical measurements show enhanced ORR activity, and spectroscopic characterizations directly reveal axial NO 3 coordination upon introducing NO 3 − , supporting the theoretical predictions. Based on these insights, we propose an adaptive framework for electrolyte‐guided active site programming, which enables the selection of proper anion ligand with optimal catalytic activity under specific working conditions. This work bridges mechanistic modeling and experimental design, precisely constructing the active center for enhanced electrocatalytic activity.

title: Steering C–C Coupling via Amorphous Nd 2 O 3 Pinning for Efficient CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐catalyzed electrochemical CO 2 reduction provides a sustainable route for carbon fixation. However, the undercoordinated Cu active sites that facilitate C–C coupling readily undergo rapid, detrimental structural reconstruction under negative potentials. To tackle this challenge, we introduce amorphous Nd 2 O 3 nanostructures pinned at the Cu 2 O interface to stabilize the undercoordinated Cu sites. Electron microscopy and spectroscopy reveal that this pinning interface not only refines the Cu 2 O grains by approximately half but also stabilizes the high density of defect sites generated during reconstruction. Density functional theory further unveils that the interface thermodynamically redirects the coupling pathway from the energy‐demanding CO–CO dimerization towards the more favorable CO–CHO asymmetric coupling (*CO + *CHO → *COCHO). The desired catalyst achieves a peak C 2 H 4 Faradaic efficiency of 59.5% at 1.1 A cm −2 and a record partial current density of 762.5 mA cm −2 at 1.5 A cm −2 in a flow cell, with stable operation over 30 hours. We showcase a facile yet effective material design strategy that breaks the selectivity‐stability trade‐off of Cu catalysts, paving the way for industrially viable CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 electrolysis.

title: Programmable Amino Migration−Enabled Diversification of Allylamines
abstract: ABSTRACT Migration−enabled alkene functionalization offers an attractive strategy for accessing molecular architectures beyond the reach of conventional alkene transformations. Yet existing approaches typically channel translocated radical intermediates into a single reaction manifold, limiting the broader potential of migration chemistry for divergent synthesis. Here, we establish a programmable migration−enabled synthesis platform that redirects allylamines from passive alkene substrates into versatile synthons for divergent molecular construction. Through the integration of radical functionalization with amino migration, this strategy generates a migratory radical intermediate that undergoes selective diversification via complementary radical−trapping, atom−transfer radical addition (ATRA), and radical−polar crossover (RPC) pathways under mild photocatalytic conditions, enabling divergent 1,2,3−trifunctionalization of allylamines. Broad compatibility with radical precursors, bifunctional reagents, nucleophiles, and diverse allylamine scaffolds provides access to more than 70 densely functionalized, C(sp 3 )−rich amino architectures, including molecules bearing quaternary carbon centers. More broadly, this work establishes radical migration as a programmable design principle for molecular diversification and expands the synthetic utility of allylamines as modular synthons for the systematic exploration of structure−function relationships.

title: Gold‐Catalyzed “Anti‐Baldwin” Cyclization of Unactivated Alkenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Owing to the unfavorable orbital alignments and geometric constraints, 5‐ endo‐trig cyclizations are kinetically disfavored as stated by Sir Jack Baldwin. Consequently, reports of such cyclization are scarce and primarily rely on the use of activated alkenes. Herein, we report a rare example of “anti‐Baldwin” cyclization of unactivated alkenes. The key to the success of this transformation is that the kinetically favored 4‐ exo ‐ trig cyclization is reversible, thereby enabling equilibration to the thermodynamically favored 5‐ endo‐trig cyclization intermediate, which then undergoes reductive elimination to form the product.

title: Expert operating skills learning-based intelligent shared control method for a CT-guided percutaneous biopsy robot
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accurate and minimally invasive percutaneous biopsy is critical for early lung cancer diagnosis, yet conventional manual procedures suffer from repeated radiation exposure, high reliance on doctor expertise, and risk of tissue injury. This study presents a 5 degree-of-freedom robotic system combined with an intelligent shared control framework guided by expert skills learning. Expert skills were modeled using a variational autoencoder–hidden Markov model to segment latent procedural phases, and dynamic motion primitives reconstructed representative expert trajectories.
