source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo
abstract: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

title: Harness design matters for AI capabilities in mathematics
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: To assess the ability of current AI systems to correctly solve research-level mathematics problems, we tested four AI systems on a set of ten problems in a broad range of mathematical fields; these problems arose naturally in the research process of the contributors. This document includes our methodology, and the results of our testing, including the assessment of human reviewers and a report of costs. We provide links to supplementary documents including the human solutions, the AI-generated solutions, and the referee reports and logs for the AI-generated solutions.

title: Windblown dunes are born in sand at the brink of transport
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Windblown dunes are found everywhere in the Solar System where a supply of loose sediment is mobilized by gas flows, from the sluggish winds of Venus to speed-of-sound sublimation flows on comets. Their abundance is nontrivial because dunes only form where grains hop ballistically (“saltate”). This implies that winds across the Solar System reach “goldilocks” speeds that are just right to initiate and maintain saltation of whatever sediment is available despite vast variations in material and fluid properties, and gravity. Based on select observations, it was proposed that dune fields may be characterized by a near-threshold transport state where dune-forming winds minimally exceed the saltation threshold on Earth. Here, we demonstrate that this is indeed the case globally. Next, we show that, unlike riverbeds—which evolve to a similar state through adjustments of channel geometry—dune fields are born in it due to the rapid decrease in wind frequency with increasing wind speed. These results imply that grain sizes in windblown dunes provide a robust record of formative winds, such that corresponding wind speeds can be estimated from aeolian sandstones and dune deposits across planets. The near-threshold state of windblown dunes thus opens a promising line of investigation for paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate reconstructions on Earth and beyond.

title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
abstract:
Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY
                    p
                    HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY
                    p
                    HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a
                    trans
                    -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY
                    p
                    HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

title: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Multi-principal element alloys are promising structural materials for nuclear, aerospace, and fusion applications, yet their accelerated discovery is limited by the prohibitive cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing behavior across vast compositional spaces. Here, we establish local lattice distortion (LLD), an intrinsic feature of chemically complex alloys, as a predictive and universal descriptor for vacancy–interstitial diffusivity convergence. We develop and validate a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential based on the moment tensor potential formalism for body-centered-cubic Zr–Ti–Nb alloys, enabling accurate large-scale simulations of defect energetics and migration. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a robust inverse correlation between LLD and the activation energy disparity between vacancies and interstitials. This relationship is further validated in face-centered-cubic V–Co–Ni and Ni–Pd systems, demonstrating transferability across distinct chemistries and crystal structures. LLD-induced narrowing of vacancy–interstitial mobility differences promotes Frenkel pair recombination and defect self-healing. Mechanistically, vacancy diffusion is governed by the energy barrier associated with bond-length compression at the saddle state, together with statistical sampling of low-barrier jumps mediated by oversized atoms. These findings establish lattice distortion as a powerful, physically grounded design lever that links nanoscale disorder to point-defect self-healing, offering a practical pathway for the accelerated discovery of next-generation structural materials for extreme environments.

title: Structure and dynamics of the cellular belt driving bacterial gliding motility
abstract:
Various bacteria move on solid surfaces through a process known as gliding motility. Gliding bacteria of the phylum
                    Bacteroidota
                    are major ecological players in a wide variety of niches, as commensals or as pathogens. They use the type IX secretion system (T9SS) to transport adhesins to the cell surface, which then travel in a helical pattern to propel the cell. Here, we purified the filament that drives adhesin helical movement and uncovered its structure by cryo–electron microscopy. Live imaging showed that this outer membrane–associated periplasmic belt, built from T9SS core components, is powered by T9SS molecular motors. This structure functions as a moving walkway that conveys outer membrane β barrel protein–adhesin complexes, therefore coupling motor activity to directional surface translation. This study reveals a unique machinery coupling protein secretion with rapid directed movement of membrane-embedded protein complexes.

title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
abstract:
To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in
                    Drosophila
                    to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

title: A floss-based platform for native gingival crevicular fluid analysis enables noninvasive systemic and oral health monitoring
abstract:
Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) is a serum-derived biofluid in the gingival sulcus, offering access to systemic metabolic signals and localized oral inflammation. However, its diagnostic utility remains underutilized because native submicroliter volumes cannot be analyzed without specimen pooling and reagent-mediated dilution. We overcome this barrier using a floss-based platform that enables on-demand GCF analysis during routine flossing. The device integrates a dual-fiber system exploiting shear-dependent property for efficient mobilization, liquid-bridge retention, a pyramidal microfluidic sensor stack, and real-time electrofluidic volume correction. This architecture supports multiplexed electrochemical quantification of glucose, uric acid (UA), pH, and H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    from native GCF within minutes. In human studies, GCF glucose and UA correlated with capillary blood (glucose:
                    r
                     = 0.89, UA:
                    r
                     = 0.78). Site-specific pH and H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    levels differentiated inflamed from healthy periodontal sites, correlating with probing pocket depth. By converting a daily hygiene practice into a dual tool for systemic and oral health monitoring, this platform advances comorbidity management for chronic disease populations.

title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
abstract:
Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr
                    2+
                    –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

title: Seasonal effects of simulated marine heatwaves on temperature-dependent growth performance
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly longer and more frequent globally, but the cumulative impacts of multiple events on organism performance remain poorly understood. Using thermal performance models, we simulate the effects of simple seasonal MHW scenarios on the predicted growth of 36 mariculture species across the western Pacific Ocean. Simulations suggested that winter MHWs could generally benefit growth, while summer MHWs produced generally negative impacts, especially at higher latitudes where species experience summer growth periods. When combined, winter and summer MHW scenarios indicated a cumulative negative effect for most species. Vulnerability was highest at the warm- and cold-range edges of species’ distributions. These simulations suggest that temperature-dependent growth may be closely linked to the seasonal timing and frequency of extreme events, with multi-season MHWs posing potential challenges for mariculture species in the future. Our simulations highlight the importance of considering multi-season impacts in climate adaptation strategies.

title: Somatostatin 6, a master maternal mRNA driving early development
abstract:
Vertebrate genomes contain six somatostatin (SST) gene family members, of which only SST1 and cortistatin (CORT or SST2) are present in mammalian genomes. These genes encode peptides that predominantly exert inhibitory effects on growth, metabolism, reproduction, and the immune system. However, their roles in nonmammalian vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we examined zebrafish
                    sst6
                    (
                    sst6.2
                    ) loss of function and discovered that maternally inherited
                    sst6
                    mRNA is vital for embryonic cleavage and gastrulation. Its absence impaired calcium release from stores, calcium wave propagation, F-actin assembly, furrow ingression, and overall embryonic development. Moreover, maternal
                    sst6
                    mRNA is crucial for degrading maternal mRNAs, for calcium-dependent phosphorylation of Stat3 and Smad1/5, and for activating zygotic gene transcription, including
                    pou5f1
                    ,
                    nanog
                    , and
                    sox2
                    , as well as downstream pluripotency factors. This suggests that maternal
                    sst6
                    mRNA acts as a master regulator of early development, a function likely conserved in other vertebrates.

title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

title: NET‐Inhibiting Bio‐Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence
abstract: ABSTRACT Maladaptive trained immunity (MTI) establishes pathogenic innate immune memory that amplifies the immune response to recurrent chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, but erasing this memory remains challenging. In this study, we identified neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) as key mediators of periodontitis‐induced MTI that reprogrammed bone marrow epigenetics and transcriptomics to amplify inflammation upon secondary challenge. Thus, we designed a NET‐inhibiting bioengineered platform (tPA@AGNs‐DNase I) to erase MTI and prevent recurrent inflammation. This platform was constructed by encapsulating tPA within activated gelated neutrophils (AGNs) and conjugating DNase I onto the surface by glycoengineering and click chemistry. Leveraging the inflammation‐homing property of AGNs, the platform enabled co‐delivery of two enzymes: DNase I degraded the DNA scaffold of NETs, while tPA disrupted fibrin‒neutrophil engagement to block NETosis, thereby achieving synergistic NET clearance. Local periodontal administration of tPA@AGNs‐DNase I not only resolved primary inflammation but also reversed established MTI by restoring aberrant bone marrow epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming, thereby markedly attenuating recurrent hyperinflammation and alveolar bone loss in a religature‐induced periodontitis model. Collectively, this work provides a bioengineered platform that erases central MTI via in situ NET clearance, offering a paradigm‐shifting strategy to control chronic inflammatory disease recurrence.

title: Unblockable communication with gravity
abstract: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism. However, electromagnetic signals are readily susceptible to screening and blocking, so their availability cannot be guaranteed in adverse environments. This raises a fundamental question: Can information be transmitted through an unblockable channel? Here, we show that gravity, under physically realistic conditions, offers such a path. We propose and implement a wireless communication protocol in which a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, while a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with a gravimeter. We validate this scheme experimentally, successfully transmitting a gravitational message a distance of ≈0.7 meters through a brick wall at a rate of 1 bit per minute. These results establish gravity as a viable platform for practically unblockable communication.

title: An Inflammation‐Responsive and Biodegradable Microneedle Patch for Periodontal Soft and Hard Tissue Regeneration via Temporally Coordinated Sustained Release of Hydrogen and Calcium Ions
abstract: ABSTRACT Periodontitis progression is driven by a self‐perpetuating pathological microenvironment that couples inflammation, oxidative stress, osteoimmune disruption, and impaired regeneration, leading to alveolar bone resorption and periodontal tissue destruction. To address this challenge, we developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive microneedle system (CaSi 2 @PLGA MNs). By integrating CaSi 2 @PLGA microspheres, formed by encapsulating calcium silicide (CaSi 2 ) in poly(lactic‐ co ‐glycolic acid) (PLGA), into a ROS‐responsive microneedle matrix, we established a temporally coordinated therapeutic strategy featuring hierarchical release that couples two sequential processes: rapid microsphere release triggered by the inflammatory microenvironment, followed by gradual microsphere hydrolysis to enable sustained H 2 and Ca 2+ delivery over several days. This staged delivery enables an orderly transition from early periodontal inflammation to longer‐term tissue regeneration and repair. In vitro, the microspheres alleviated macrophage oxidative stress, promoted macrophage polarization toward a repair‐associated phenotype, and further supported osteogenic differentiation, cell migration, and angiogenesis. In vivo, CaSi 2 @PLGA MNs improved the periodontal inflammatory status, reduced alveolar bone resorption, promoted collagen remodeling and regeneration‐related marker expression, thereby demonstrating periodontal tissue repair potential. Overall, this study establishes a temporally coordinated local‐delivery platform that integrates inflammation control with regenerative support, providing a promising adjunctive strategy for periodontitis and demonstrating potential for extension to other inflammation‐associated osteolytic diseases.

title: A Route to High‐Temperature Creep Resistant Ultra‐High Molecular Weight Polyethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐performance lightweight polymers for load‐bearing applications at elevated temperatures demand strong creep resistance to ensure long‐term dimensional and mechanical stability. Conventional uniaxial drawn polyethylene tapes and fibers suffer from poor creep resistance owing to intrinsically weak van der Waals intermolecular forces, especially above their α ‐relaxation temperature (∼90°C) as chain mobility is enhanced. Here we demonstrate that introducing as little as 0.2 mol% 1‐decene branches into low‐entangled ultra‐high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) profoundly suppresses high‐temperature creep. Solvent‐free solid‐state processing at a draw ratio of 250 yields branched and linear UHMWPE tapes with a specific tensile strength of 4.5 N/tex and a specific modulus of ∼200 N/tex. For the constant load of 250 MPa (∼2500 kg/cm 2 ), the linear UHMWPE tape at 110°C accumulates a creep strain of 15%, whereas the branched UHMWPE tapes maintain a negligible creep strain even at 150°C. This exceptional creep resistance is attributed to the ability of the branches to suppress the entropy‐driven relaxation of the oriented chains under constraints. This work resolves the long‐standing high‐temperature creep bottleneck of high‐performance PE, enabling high‐value, sustainable applications in automotive, energy distribution/storage, and advanced structural applications.

title: Three‐Dimensional In Situ Tunable Mechanical Metamaterials
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical metamaterials with in situ, smooth, and broad‐range tunability of stiffness are highly anticipated in engineering, but existing designs are limited to unidirectional or bidirectional control. As the stiffness lacks the multi‐directional coupling effect for shape morphing, creating three‐dimensional (3D) metamaterials with triaxial tunability remains challenging in configuration design, fabrication, and actuation. Here we create two types of gear‐based 3D mechanical metamaterials that achieve in situ, wide‐range, continuous, reversible tunability of 3D stiffness. The first uses spherical gears containing ellipsoidal cavities as the variable‐stiffness components, while the second conceives planetary‐like 3D gear assemblies as the metacell. They feature orthotropic stiffness in three axes—all can be tuned in situ by about 30 times via synchronous rotation. Moreover, the nonlinear buckling properties are also tunable in 3D space. The integrated actuation methods are conceived to achieve robust and smooth control. We clarify the principles and demonstrate the properties of 3D in situ tunability by analytical, numerical, and experimental methods. Therefore, this work systematically proves the possibility of programmable metamaterials with in situ 3D tunability, offering feasible ways for conceiving advanced structures with actively controllable 3D static and dynamic properties.

title: Phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization enables record NIR-II-to-visible-light photon upconversion
abstract:
Near-infrared-to-visible triplet−triplet annihilation photon upconversion (TTA-UC) enables harvesting low-energy photons; however, extending nanocrystal-sensitized TTA-UC into the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) remains challenging because triplet sensitization is thermodynamically disfavored under sub-triplet excitation. Here, we demonstrate that lead-free AgBiS
                    2
                    nanocrystals facilitate phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization, enabling efficient NIR-II-to-visible upconversion. Under the sub-bandgap single-photon excitation, AgBiS
                    2
                    nanocrystals exhibit anti-Stokes photoluminescence, suggesting strong exciton−phonon coupling mediated by surface states. When coupled with 5-tetracene carboxylic acid transmitters and rubrene annihilators, AgBiS
                    2
                    achieves 980 nm-to-visible upconversion with a record quantum yield of 6.22% (normalized to 100%) and an anti-Stokes shift of 0.95 eV. Time-resolved photoluminescence and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy support a surface-state-mediated uphill energy-transfer pathway coupled to low-frequency vibrational modes. Our work establishes phonon-assisted triplet sensitization as a strategy to overcome the NIR-II red wall for lead-free photon upconversion.

title: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens ’ dispersal
abstract:
To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of
                    Homo sapiens
                    , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and
                    H. sapiens
                    lived in Europe. These spatially explicit estimates were incorporated into an agent-based model simulating human demographic dynamics under various scenarios. Results indicate that carrying capacity changes cannot explain Neanderthal extinction at a continental scale, though they are essential to understanding spatiotemporal distribution patterns of both human species. Conversely, the arrival of
                    H. sapiens
                    remarkably increased Neanderthal extinction likelihood. Because of the successive demographic expansions and contractions, group connectivity emerges as the key factor shaping population stability in both species. These findings support that Neanderthal disappearance and
                    H. sapiens
                    dispersals were interconnected demographic processes.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
abstract:
Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl
                    −
                    induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

abstract: Emergency electricity planning for urban shelters requires comparing heterogeneous supply resources under uncertain, time-varying demand. This study assesses eight specified emergency electricity-supply configurations, including two Vehicle-to-Shelter (V2S) arrangements, for a 1000-person shelter during a 72-h grid outage. A common framework combines paired Monte Carlo simulation, hourly supply–demand matching, continuous resource-state evolution, and access-conditioned variance decomposition, while retaining configuration-specific constraints on power, usable energy, infrastructure continuity, resource access, and deployment timing. Across nine demand and disaster-severity scenarios, adequacy declined as shelter services expanded and cold-season demand increased, while access-dependent resources were additionally constrained by infrastructure continuity, allocation, and arrival. High coverage of the specified diesel-generator configuration depended strongly on its usable energy in the most demanding scenario, where a 20% stock reduction lowered mean energy coverage ratio (ECR) from 0.819 to 0.659. Similar aggregate coverage also concealed different temporal risks. Under hot conditions with moderate disaster severity, a mobile power-supply truck and a local-plus-external V2S arrangement had nearly identical mean ECRs (0.368 and 0.367) under baseline access assumptions but different temporal shortfall patterns. The truck provided no support before allocation and arrival, whereas locally parked EVs supplied limited early power. Access-state differences accounted for most observed ECR variance for the access-dependent configurations in the two examined scenarios, distinguishing conditional resource capability from unconditional shelter adequacy. These findings support mechanism-based screening by power, endurance, immediate availability, and credible access arrangements, while suggesting a potential role for V2S as a conditional supplement rather than a universal substitute for dedicated backup supply.

abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

This reversible, optically readable rigidification offers a design principle for responsive porous materials.

title: Discerning between Excimer and Singlet Fission Sites Using Modulated Magnetic Field Photoluminescence
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Magnetic field effects play a key role in the characterization of organic electronic materials. In particular, the microscopic processes underlying singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation have been clarified in recent years through the observation and subsequent theoretical explanation of magnetic field effects in these processes. Here, we study magnetic field effects on the luminescence of 5,12-bis((triisopropylsilyl)ethynyl)tetracene, a well-studied material in which both singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation occur. By performing highly sensitive modulated-field magneto-photoluminescence experiments we observe magnetic field effect lineshapes with rich detail, allowing a precise characterization of triplet exciton dynamics. By additionally filtering these magnetic field effects by luminescence wavelength, we can identify the excimer state by its unique magnetic field signature. Finally, we show that a theoretical explanation of these field effects requires a model that explicitly accounts for quantum coherences, which highlights the importance of detailed spin dynamics modeling in understanding magnetic field effects, even at room temperature.

title: Cathode Surface Reconfiguration via Solvent Chemistry for Durable All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrode surfaces and interfaces critically dominate the performance of all-solid-state lithium batteries. However, established additive-oriented strategies physically isolate the cathode from the electrolyte without improving the restricted Li+ transport pathways of the cathode surface. Here, we propose a solvation-mediated chemical etching mechanism governing cathode surface reconfiguration, driven by competition between solvent coordination and lattice stabilization. The solvent coordination, coupled with electron and proton transfer, weakens transition-metal–oxygen covalency and destabilizes lattice-bound surface species, shifting the interfacial energy landscape toward solvation-favored states. This triggers selective transition-metal dissolution and oxygen modulation, ultimately reorganizing confined surface regions into continuous Li+ transport networks. Using micron-sized single-crystalline Li- and Mn-rich cathodes as a model, we demonstrate the formation of a Mn- and O-deficient interfacial layer equipped with a three-dimensional Li+ diffusion network. This functional layer accelerates Li+ diffusion and anionic redox kinetics while suppressing transition metal migration and oxygen release. Consequently, charge-transfer resistance drops drastically (from 585 to 67 Ω) and Li+ diffusion increases 90-fold at 4.8 V, enabling 80.3% capacity retention after 2800 cycles at 2C. This solvent-driven reconfiguration provides a scalable framework for stabilizing diverse cathodes in next-generation advanced batteries.

title: Supramolecular Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the design, preparation, and study of a supramolecular pseudopeptidic cage that selectively binds twin phosphotyrosine (pTyr–pTyr) peptides and modulates their enzymatic dephosphorylation in water. The receptor combines an expanded aromatic cavity specifically designed to encapsulate a twin Tyr-Tyr motif with peripheral Lys-derived ammonium groups that engage phosphate residues through electrostatic interactions. In addition to studying the cage’s binding properties through different experimental and computational techniques, we investigated the ability of the receptor to modulate the kinetics of the irreversible phosphate hydrolysis catalyzed by alkaline phosphatase (ALP). When different substrates are connected through irreversible catalytic reactions, forming a nascent network, the presence of a supramolecular protecting host, able to selectively bind these substrates, modifies the system outcome in a way that cannot be predicted from the mere comparison of individual binding constants. This leads to unexpected, emerging behaviors, altering the relative intermediate concentrations through time and therefore regulating the network response. We demonstrate the biochemical potential of this cage by protecting the twin pTyr–pTyr motif within the activation loop of JAK2 kinase from dephosphorylation by λ-protein phosphatase. Altogether, our results establish supramolecular substrate protection as an effective strategy to regulate multistep enzymatic reaction networks.

title: Extraframework Cations Promoted Ultratrace Acetylene Capture by Coordinatively Unsaturated Nickel Sites in FAU Zeolites
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Removal of ultratrace alkynes to produce polymer- and electronic-grade olefins is an important but extremely challenging task. Here, we report a dual-cation strategy in FAU-type zeolites that enables the unprecedented capture of acetylene at concentrations of parts per million (ppm). The optimized Ni–Ba–Y adsorbent delivers high dynamic uptakes of 0.37–0.82 mmol·g–1 at acetylene concentrations of 500–10,000 ppm, with acetylene/ethylene selectivity exceeding 100 under industrial relevant conditions. Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) and theoretical calculations reveal that Ba2+ at Site I modulate the coordinatively unsaturated Ni2+ centers at Site II, enhancing π-back-donation to adsorbed acetylene. Process simulations demonstrate that adsorptive separation using Ni–Ba–Y achieves over 200-fold higher space-time productivity (STP) of ethylene and reduces energy consumption by over 44% compared with conventional catalytic hydrogenation processes. This dual-cation strategy will promote the design of zeolite adsorbents for challenging industrial separations.

title: In Situ STEM Imaging of Colloidal Crystals Based on Programmable Atom Equivalents
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract It is challenging to image the assembly of colloidal crystals composed of programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) using electron microscopy (EM). PAEs typically consist of nanoparticle cores densely functionalized with radially oriented DNA shells, which assemble in the liquid phase via DNA bonds. EM requires high-vacuum conditions, and electron beams can damage soft materials like nucleic acids. Here, we present a liquid-phase scanning transmission electron microscopy (LPSTEM) method for imaging PAEs composed of ∼5 nm gold nanoparticle cores in solution, enabling the direct investigation of their DNA-directed assembly processes. This system is particularly well-suited for in situ studies of soft-matter dynamics because the gold nanoparticle cores provide strong electron contrast. Using a nanofluidic liquid cell, the nucleation and growth of PAE assemblies, governed via the principles of colloidal crystal engineering with DNA, were directly observed. Imaging conditions were established to resolve colloidal assemblies in liquid while also characterizing electron-beam-induced damage under both conventional STEM and STEM-in-SEM conditions. Quantitative image analysis reveals changes in local coordination during crystal growth and subsequent beam-induced dissociation. Complementary ex situ simulations corroborate that radiolytic species generated in the buffer are major contributors to beam-induced damage. Together, these results establish a versatile and accessible platform for probing the in situ dynamics of PAE assembly in liquids, with broad applicability to the study of other soft nanomaterials and composites relevant to sensing, actuation, energy storage, catalysis, and medicine.

title: Radical Molecular-Junction Covalent Organic Framework for Asymmetric Iodide Conversion: 100,000 Cycles in Zn-Iodine Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous Zinc–iodine batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their eco-friendliness and safety. However, conventional two-electron cathode hosts suffer from poor cycling life due to polyiodide shuttling and sluggish one-step I–/I2 redox kinetics, which limits their practical usage. Herein, we designed a molecular-junction covalent organic framework (COF) denoted as TNCOF, integrating the tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) donor and the naphthalene diimide (NDI) acceptor. Typically, TTF forms a robust radical-cationic TTF•+ structure by anchoring to iodine electrostatically. TTF•+ and electron-withdrawing NDI within the T•+NCOF molecular junction provide a driving force through an intense local electrostatic potential for the asymmetric iodine conversion (AIC) pathway (I–/I3–/I2 vs. I2/I–), markedly boosting reaction kinetics and suppressing polyiodide shuttling. The optimized T•+NCOF cathode delivers a specific capacity of 228.7 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 and achieves an ultralong cycling stability exceeding 100,000 cycles, which is one of the highest records in this field. In situ measurements, Peak Force Tunneling atomic force microscopy (AFM) results, and calculations confirm the robust adsorption capability of T•+NCOF and demonstrate the accelerated I3– conversion kinetics. This work establishes that a radical-cationic molecular-junction COF enables robust I3– anchoring and a unique AIC pathway, offering a novel strategy to overcome inherent stability challenges in Zinc-halogen batteries.

title: Transition-Metal-Mediated Discharge Intermediates Set Anionic-Redox Potentials and Voltage Hysteresis in Li-Rich Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Voltage hysteresis arising from anionic redox reactions remains a central bottleneck for lithium-rich cathodes. While ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has been invoked to describe the charging pathway, its proposed reverse counterpart, metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT), remains experimentally unresolved during discharge. Here, using cation-disordered rock-salt Li2Ni0.33Ta0.66O3 (LNTO) as a model system, we combine electrochemical relaxation analysis with synchrotron-based spectroscopy to identify, for the first time, a metastable reduction intermediate characterized by Ni(2-δ)+/(O–O)n− during discharge, thereby providing direct experimental validation for the MLCT framework. The discovery of this metastable intermediate demonstrates that discharge proceeds through a two-step electrochemical–chemical pathway, wherein the spontaneous relaxation evolution of the metastable intermediate drives free-energy dissipation and voltage hysteresis. Guided by this picture, Ru substitution was introduced to modulate the cation–anion electronic structure, enabling Ru 4d–O 2p hybridization to generate persistent low-energy hole states that lower the energy of the metastable discharge intermediate and shift O–O dimer reduction to higher potentials. We further show that the discharge intermediate serves as the energetic link through which transition-metal electronic structure governs the effective anionic-redox potential. This work provides a discharge-side thermodynamic framework for understanding and mitigating voltage hysteresis in Li-rich anionic-redox cathodes.

title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
abstract:
RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived
                    SPOP
                    mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Conjugated molecular belts attract increasing attention because of the unusual electronic and magnetic behaviour arising from their radially oriented
                    p
                    orbitals. A π-conjugated molecular belt is expected to behave like a quantum ring, showing global aromatic or antiaromatic ring currents, but in most hydrocarbon benzenoid belts, localized Clar sextets preclude the emergence of global ring currents. Here we report the synthesis of anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts that sustain global antiaromatic ring currents in the neutral state. Macrocyclization was achieved by nickel(0)-mediated Yamamoto coupling. Scholl oxidation with DDQ/TfOH, promoted by electron-donating methoxy substituents, yielded the strained triple-stranded nanobelts. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons, as revealed by
                    1
                    H NMR spectroscopy and corroborated by computational analysis. This work establishes a platform for synthesizing other heterocyclic nanobelts, in cases where the corresponding hydrocarbon nanobelt is not yet synthetically accessible.

title: Symmetry-Breaking Charge Localization Controls Radiationless Decay in a Multibranched Charge-Transfer State
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Symmetry breaking in multibranched charge-transfer (CT) excited states is generally viewed as a mechanism for excited-state localization, yet how such localization controls the subsequent fate of the excitation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that environmental stabilization of a symmetry-broken CT state can fundamentally reshape radiationless decay in a bent donor–acceptor–donor chromophore. Increasing solvent stabilization drives rapid reorganization toward a lower-energy CT configuration, collapsing the singlet lifetime from 1.98 ns in toluene to 9.2 ps in acetonitrile while increasing the effective nonradiative rate (knr) from 2.14 × 108 to >1.11 × 1011 s–1. Femtosecond transient absorption establishes that formation of the stabilized CT configuration precedes terminal population loss, while triplet accumulation observed in nonpolar media disappears as singlet depletion becomes ultrafast. Controlled toluene–acetonitrile mixtures further reveal that the nonradiative rate does not obey a single invariant energy-gap dependence: distinct energy-gap-law regimes emerge as the CT state is progressively stabilized, followed by a strongly reorganized regime in which knr continues to accelerate despite little additional change in the energy gap. Independently, the changing relationship between emission spectral variance and Stokes shift shows that the nuclear reorganization of the relaxed CT ensemble also changes with stabilization. Together, these results support a solvent-dependent symmetry-breaking landscape in which progressive charge localization reshapes both the excited-state energy and the nuclear coordinates governing access to the ground state. Symmetry breaking therefore acts not simply as an electronic localization process, but as an environmental kinetic switch, converting a long-lived, emissive and triplet-forming CT state into a rapidly quenched excited state.

title: Accessing Alkyl Linkers for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rise of macrocyclic peptides as a therapeutic modality has exposed gaps in the synthetic chemistry toolbox available for drug discovery teams to rapidly explore diverse linkers for structural optimization. In contrast to the thioether linkers common in peptide leads identified from mRNA display, all-carbon linkers are desirable for imparting solubility and stability, but existing approaches suffer from limited amino acid diversity, incompatibility with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), stereochemical loss, multistep requirements, or restricted linker placement. We report a Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization (D2AM) to install alkyl linkers via C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. This method uses pyridinium monomers derived from commercial amino acids that are stable to SPPS for the seamless synthesis of complex macrocyclic and polycyclic peptides with conservation of stereochemistry. This deaminative method is anticipated to accelerate optimization of peptide macrocycle structure in drug discovery.

title: Concerted Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer Absorption and Localized Photoluminescence in an Fe(III) Photosensitizer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract There is tremendous interest in the electronic structure of [FeIII(phtmeimb)2]+, the first iron complex to show room temperature photoluminescence (PL) with an excited-state lifetime sufficient for dynamic quenching in fluid solution. Two types of excited states are generated by light absorption, termed the Franck–Condon (FC) state and the thermally equilibrated excited state (THEXI) that is photoluminescent. Herein we report solvatochromic and electroabsorption studies to probe the electronic structure of these two states. The doublet ligand-to-metal-charge-transfer absorption was found to be mostly solvent independent while a notable solvatochromism in the PL spectra indicated the presence of an excited-state dipole in polar solvents (μ⃗ = 16 ± 10 D), best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb•+)(phtmeimb)]+*. However, standard and higher-order electroabsorption spectra revealed concerted and equal charge transfer from the two tridentate ligands to the metal, giving rise to a significant polarizability change (Δα) without the generation of a dipole moment (Δμ⃗ = 0) best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb+1/2)2]+*. The strong interligand coupling necessary for such concerted charge transfer is proposed to be mediated by a t2g orbital of the Fe(III) center. Taken together, these findings provide new insights into this famed photoluminescent open-shell iron complex relevant to the design of improved iron photosensitizers.

title: Electrothermal Mapping: A Methodology for Decoupling Redox, Protonation, and Denaturation Dynamics of Cytochrome c
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Differential scanning calorimetry, fluorometry, circular dichroism, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry are routinely used to study thermal and chemical denaturation of proteins. However, these powerful methods monitor protein unfolding in bulk aqueous solutions but overlook interfacial environments, such as lipid membranes and confined crevices, where electrostatic and hydrophobic forces reshape protein conformational landscapes and dictate their function. Herein, we introduce an electrothermal methodology that uniquely probes protein conformational changes in a potential-modulated biomimetic environment. Electrochemistry at the Interface between Two Immiscible Electrolyte Solutions (ITIES) captures nonredox fingerprints of cytochrome c under heat stress, offering a unique perspective on protein behavior without relying on electron transfer reactions and revealing interfacial activity not evident in bulk solutions by conventional methods. Electrothermal mapping presents the protein thermal stability as a current–potential–temperature landscape, enabling direct comparison of the protein’s native and non-native conformational states driven by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Ultimately, our work establishes a new paradigm for predicting protein behavior under heat stress at membrane-like interfaces, with far-reaching implications for biotechnology and medicine, including drug development, enzyme engineering, and protein expression, where protein stability and crevice accessibility are critical.

title: Author Correction: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines sensitize tumours to immune checkpoint blockade
Spatiotemporally Decoupled Cascade Photocatalysis on Dual S-Scheme Heterostructure with Interfacial Polarization Fields and Proton Shuttle Channels
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transient surface reaction dynamics govern artificial-photosynthesis-enabled multistep tandem biomass oxidation but are hindered by spatially intermingled reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and temporally entangled elementary-step sequences. A spatial-engineering strategy for fabricating ZnS/Sv-chalcogenide/MoSe2 (Sv = sulfur vacancies, chalcogenide = ZnIn2S4, Zn0.5Cd0.5S, CdIn2S4) dual S-scheme heterostructure, with chalcogenide as the shared mediator between the ZnS/chalcogenide and chalcogenide/MoSe2 S-junctions, is developed by anchoring MoSe2 nanoparticles onto chalcogenide nanosheets epitaxially grown from ZnS hollow dodecahedral cages. These ternary-component nanoreactors integrate dual interfacial features, the interfacial localized polarization field and the interfacial proton shuttle channel, to orchestrate dynamic intelligent catalysis. Specifically, the interfacial localized polarization field drives spatially decoupled ROS generation (•OH, •O2–, •OOH) via the asymmetric charge distributions, enabling zone-specific ROS to undertake differentiated oxidation tasks. Interfacial proton shuttle channel drives temporally decoupled elementary-step sequences via the interfacial dynamic hydrogen-bonding networks, thereby liberating pH-dependent proton transfer through directed radical protonation (•O2– → •OOH). This synergy provides a proof of concept for neutral 5-hydroxymethylfurfural-to-2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (HMF-to-FDCA) conversion and demonstrates a fundamental research-to-practical-application capability. This work proposes a generalizable catalyst design paradigm integrating interfacial localized polarization fields and interfacial proton shuttle channels, offering innovative insights for guiding spatiotemporally decoupled multistep cascade catalysis.

title: Taming Metal–Electrolyte Interface via Two-Dimensional Organic Metal Chalcogenide Colloids for Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anode-free metal batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technologies, yet their application is severely limited by dendrite growth and rapid capacity decay induced by an unstable metal–electrolyte interface. Herein, we propose a “colloid electrolyte” strategy employing coordination polymer nanosheets as electrolyte additives for constructing anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs). Unlike conventional molecular additives or inert particle suspensions, these colloidal nanosheets provide spatially organized and continuously available interfacial reaction domains, thereby spatially regulating electrolyte component distribution and interfacial reactions. These nanosheets, composed of AgS layers uniformly decorated with fluorinated groups, undergo in situ decomposition at the metal–electrolyte interface. This process generates gradient distributions of Ag nanoparticles and NaF/Na2S species, which guide the spontaneous formation of a functionally graded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This hierarchical SEI enables dendrite-free Na deposition and imparts sustained interfacial protection during cycling. Consequently, high-cathode-loading AFSMBs achieve an ultralong lifespan (>1600 cycles), representing a 10-fold improvement over counterpart cells without the colloidal additive. Notably, 0.5-Ah-level anode-free pouch cells exhibit stable cycling for 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes coordination polymer colloids as a new class of electrolyte additives for advanced alkali metal batteries.
